They answered, "They were men just like you — every one of them looked like the son of a king." ¹⁹ Gideon replied, "Those were my brothers, my own mother's sons. As surely as the LORD lives, if you had spared their lives, I would not kill you." ²⁰ Then he said to his firstborn son Jether, "Draw your sword and kill them." But the boy did not draw his sword, because he was still young and afraid.

²¹ Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Come, kill us yourself. 'As the man is, so is his strength.'" So Gideon stepped forward and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescent ornaments from their camels' necks. ²² The Israelites said to Gideon, "Rule over us — you, your son, and your grandson — because you have saved us from the hand of Midian." ²³ But Gideon told them, "I will not rule over you, nor will my son rule over you. The LORD will rule over you." ²⁴ And he said, "I do have one request: each of you give me an earring from your share of the plunder." (It was the custom of the Ishmaelites to wear gold earrings.) ²⁵ "We'll be glad to give them," they answered. So they spread out a garment, and each man threw in an earring from his plunder.

²⁶ The weight of the golden earrings he had requested came to seventeen hundred shekels of gold, not counting the ornaments, pendants, and purple robes worn by the kings of Midian, or the chains around their camels' necks. ²⁷ Gideon made an ephod from this gold and set it up in his city of Ophrah. All Israel prostituted themselves by worshiping it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his family. ²⁸ So Midian was subdued before the Israelites and no longer raised its head. The land had peace for forty years during Gideon's lifetime. ²⁹ Jerubbaal (Gideon) the son of Joash went back to live in his own house. ³⁰ He had seventy sons of his own, for he had many wives.

³¹ His concubine who lived in Shechem also bore him a son, whom he named Abimelech. ³² Gideon the son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash at Ophrah of the Abiezrites. ³³ As soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned back to prostituting themselves with the Baals. They made Baal-Berith their god. ³⁴ The Israelites did not remember the LORD their God, who had rescued them from all their enemies on every side. ³⁵ Nor did they show loyalty to the house of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, in return for all the good he had done for Israel.

chapters.title: Judges 9
paragraphs: ¹ Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem, to his mother's brothers, and spoke with them and with all his mother's family, saying, ² "Ask all the citizens of Shechem: which is better for you — that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or that one man rule over you? Remember that I am your own flesh and blood." ³ His mother's brothers repeated all these words to the citizens of Shechem, and their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother." ⁴ They gave him seventy pieces of silver from the temple of Baal-Berith, and with this money Abimelech hired worthless and reckless men, who followed him. ⁵ He went to his father's house at Ophrah and killed his brothers, the seventy sons of Jerubbaal, on a single stone. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, escaped by hiding.

⁶ Then all the citizens of Shechem and all Beth-millo gathered together and made Abimelech king, by the oak of the pillar at Shechem. ⁷ When Jotham heard this, he went and stood on top of Mount Gerizim and called out loudly: "Listen to me, citizens of Shechem, so that God may listen to you. ⁸ Once the trees went out to anoint a king over themselves. They said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.' ⁹ But the olive tree answered, 'Should I give up my rich oil, by which both gods and humans are honored, and go to hold sway over the trees?' ¹⁰ Next the trees said to the fig tree, 'Come and reign over us.'

¹¹ But the fig tree answered, 'Should I give up my sweetness and my good fruit, and go to hold sway over the trees?' ¹² Then the trees said to the vine, 'Come and reign over us.' ¹³ But the vine answered, 'Should I give up my wine, which cheers both gods and humans, and go to hold sway over the trees?' ¹⁴ Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, 'Come and reign over us.' ¹⁵ The thornbush said to the trees, 'If you really want to anoint me king over you, come and take shelter in my shade. But if not, let fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.'

¹⁶ Now then, if you have acted honorably and in good faith when you made Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his family and treated him as he deserved — ¹⁷ for my father fought for you and risked his life to rescue you from the hand of Midian, ¹⁸ but today you have risen against my father's house and killed his seventy sons on a single stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his slave girl, king over the citizens of Shechem, just because he is your relative — ¹⁹ if you have acted honorably and in good faith toward Jerubbaal and his family today, then may you be glad about Abimelech and may he be glad about you. ²⁰ But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and consume the citizens of Shechem and Beth-millo; and let fire come out from the citizens of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech."

²¹ Then Jotham fled, escaping to Beer, and lived there because he was afraid of his brother Abimelech. ²² After Abimelech had ruled over Israel for three years, ²³ God stirred up ill will between Abimelech and the citizens of Shechem, and the citizens of Shechem acted treacherously against Abimelech. ²⁴ This was so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might be avenged, and their blood might be charged against their brother Abimelech, who killed them, and against the citizens of Shechem, who gave him the strength to kill his brothers. ²⁵ In their hostility the citizens of Shechem set ambushers against him in the hills, and they robbed everyone who passed by. Abimelech was told about this.

²⁶ Now Gaal the son of Ebed came with his relatives and moved to Shechem, and the citizens of Shechem put their confidence in him. ²⁷ They went out into the fields, harvested their vineyards, trod the grapes, and held a festival. They went into the temple of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech. ²⁸ Gaal the son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who are we of Shechem, that we should serve him? Isn't he the son of Jerubbaal? And isn't Zebul his deputy? Serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem — why should we serve Abimelech? ²⁹ If only this people were under my command, then I would get rid of Abimelech." He said to Abimelech, "Muster your army and come out!" ³⁰ When Zebul the governor of the city heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger burned.

³¹ He sent messengers secretly to Abimelech, saying, "Gaal the son of Ebed and his relatives have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you. ³² So tonight you and your men should get up and lie in wait in the fields. ³³ In the morning at sunrise, advance against the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, do whatever you can to them." ³⁴ So Abimelech and all his men got up at night and positioned themselves in four groups near Shechem. ³⁵ Gaal the son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate. Abimelech and his troops rose from their hiding places.

³⁶ When Gaal saw the troops, he said to Zebul, "Look, there are people coming down from the mountaintops!" But Zebul replied, "You're seeing the shadows of the mountains — they look like people." ³⁷ Gaal spoke again: "Look, there are people coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming from the direction of the oak of Meonenim." ³⁸ Zebul said to him, "Where's all your boasting now — when you said, 'Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?' Aren't these the troops you despised? Go out now and fight them!" ³⁹ So Gaal led the citizens of Shechem out and fought against Abimelech. ⁴⁰ Abimelech chased him, and Gaal fled. Many fell wounded all the way to the entrance of the gate.

⁴¹ Abimelech returned to Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaal and his relatives so they could no longer live in Shechem. ⁴² The next day the people of Shechem went out into the fields, and Abimelech was told about it. ⁴³ He took his men, divided them into three companies, and set an ambush in the fields. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose and attacked them. ⁴⁴ Abimelech and his company rushed forward and took up a position at the entrance of the city gate, while the other two companies charged all the people who were in the fields and struck them down. ⁴⁵ Abimelech fought against the city all that day. He captured it, killed its people, demolished the city, and sowed it with salt.

⁴⁶ When all the people of the Tower of Shechem heard this, they went into the stronghold of the temple of El-Berith. ⁴⁷ Abimelech was told that all the people of the Tower of Shechem had gathered there. ⁴⁸ He and all his troops went up to Mount Zalmon. Abimelech took an ax in his hand, cut off a bundle of branches, lifted it onto his shoulder, and said to his men, "Hurry — do what you see me doing!" ⁴⁹ So each of his men also cut a bundle and followed Abimelech. They piled the branches against the stronghold and set it on fire over those inside. All the people of the Tower of Shechem also died — about a thousand men and women. ⁵⁰ Then Abimelech went to Thebez and besieged it and captured it.

⁵¹ But inside the city was a strong tower, and all the men and women — everyone in the city — fled into it. They locked themselves in and climbed up to the roof. ⁵² Abimelech came up to the tower door to set it on fire. ⁵³ But a woman dropped an upper millstone on his head and cracked his skull. ⁵⁴ He quickly called to his armor-bearer and said, "Draw your sword and run me through, so no one can say a woman killed me." His young man ran him through, and he died. ⁵⁵ When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went back to their homes.

⁵⁶ In this way God repaid the wickedness that Abimelech had done to his father by killing his seventy brothers. ⁵⁷ And God also repaid the men of Shechem for all their wickedness. The curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal came true against them.

chapters.title: Judges 10
paragraphs: ¹ After Abimelech, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, rose up to save Israel. He lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim. ² He judged Israel for twenty-three years, then died and was buried in Shamir. ³ After him came Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel for twenty-two years. ⁴ He had thirty sons who rode thirty donkeys, and they controlled thirty towns in Gilead, which are called Havvoth-jair to this day. ⁵ Jair died and was buried in Kamon.

⁶ The Israelites again did what was evil in the sight of the LORD. They served the Baals and the Ashtoreths, and the gods of Aram, of Sidon, of Moab, of the Ammonites, and of the Philistines. They abandoned the LORD and stopped serving him. ⁷ The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hands of the Philistines and the Ammonites. ⁸ From that year on, for eighteen years, they shattered and oppressed all the Israelites on the east side of the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, in Gilead. ⁹ The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim, so that Israel was in great distress. ¹⁰ The Israelites cried out to the LORD, "We have sinned against you by forsaking our God and serving the Baals."

¹¹ The LORD replied to the Israelites, "Did I not rescue you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines? ¹² When the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites oppressed you and you cried out to me, did I not save you from their hands? ¹³ Yet you have abandoned me and served other gods, so I will not rescue you anymore. ¹⁴ Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen — let them save you when you're in trouble!" ¹⁵ But the Israelites said to the LORD, "We have sinned. Do to us whatever you think best, but please rescue us today."

¹⁶ And they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD, and he could no longer bear to see Israel suffer. ¹⁷ The Ammonites mustered for war and camped in Gilead, and the Israelites assembled and camped at Mizpah. ¹⁸ The leaders of Gilead said to one another, "Whoever will lead the attack against the Ammonites will become head over all who live in Gilead."

chapters.title: Judges 11
paragraphs: ¹ Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty warrior, but he was the son of a prostitute. His father was Gilead. ² Gilead's wife also bore him sons, and when those sons grew up they drove Jephthah away. "You will get no inheritance in our father's house," they told him, "because you are the son of another woman." ³ So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob, where a band of worthless men gathered around him and went out with him. ⁴ Some time later, when the Ammonites made war on Israel, ⁵ the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob.

⁶ "Come," they said, "be our commander, so we can fight the Ammonites." ⁷ Jephthah replied to the elders of Gilead, "Didn't you hate me and drive me from my father's house? Why are you coming to me now when you're in trouble?" ⁸ The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "That's exactly why we're turning to you now — come with us to fight the Ammonites, and you will be head over all of us who live in Gilead." ⁹ Jephthah answered them, "If you take me back to fight the Ammonites and the LORD gives them over to me, will I really be your head?" ¹⁰ The elders of Gilead replied, "The LORD is our witness — we will do as you say."

¹¹ So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and commander over them. And Jephthah stated all his terms before the LORD at Mizpah. ¹² Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, saying, "What do you have against me that you have come to fight against my land?" ¹³ The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah's messengers, "Because Israel seized my land when they came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and all the way to the Jordan. Now give it back peaceably." ¹⁴ Jephthah sent messengers back to the king of the Ammonites ¹⁵ with this reply: "This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.

¹⁶ When Israel came up from Egypt, they traveled through the wilderness to the Red Sea and then came to Kadesh. ¹⁷ Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Let us pass through your land,' but the king of Edom would not listen. They sent the same request to the king of Moab, who also refused. So Israel stayed at Kadesh. ¹⁸ Then they traveled through the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and Moab. They approached from the east and camped on the other side of the Arnon. They did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was Moab's border. ¹⁹ Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, 'Let us pass through your land to our own place.' ²⁰ But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. He assembled all his troops and camped at Jahaz and fought Israel.

²¹ The LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and his whole army into Israel's hand. Israel defeated them and took possession of all the land of the Amorites who lived in that country. ²² They took over all the Amorite territory from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan. ²³ Since the LORD, the God of Israel, drove out the Amorites before his people Israel, what right do you have to take it over? ²⁴ Take whatever your god Chemosh gives you, and we will take whatever the LORD our God gives us! ²⁵ Are you any better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel or go to war against them?

²⁶ Israel has been living in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the towns along the Arnon for three hundred years. Why haven't you reclaimed them during all that time? ²⁷ I have not wronged you, but you are doing wrong by making war against me. Let the LORD, the Judge, decide the dispute this day between the Israelites and the Ammonites." But the king of the Ammonites ignored Jephthah's message. ²⁹ Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah. He passed through Gilead and Manasseh, through Mizpah in Gilead, and from there crossed over to the Ammonites. ³⁰ And Jephthah made a vow to the LORD: "If you give the Ammonites into my hands,

³¹ then whatever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I return triumphant from the Ammonites will be the LORD's, and I will sacrifice it as a burnt offering." ³² So Jephthah crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into his hands. ³³ He devastated twenty towns from Aroer to the vicinity of Minnith and all the way to Abel-keramim. Thus Israel subdued Ammon. ³⁴ When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, his daughter came out to meet him, dancing to the sound of tambourines! She was his only child — he had no son or daughter besides her. ³⁵ When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried, "Oh no, my daughter! You have brought me to my knees! You are one of those who trouble me — for I have given my word to the LORD and I cannot take it back."

³⁶ She replied, "My father, you have given your word to the LORD. Do to me as you promised, now that the LORD has vindicated you against your enemies, the Ammonites." ³⁷ She added, "Grant me this one request. Give me two months to roam the hills and weep with my friends, because I will never marry." ³⁸ "Go," he said. And he let her go for two months. She and her companions went into the hills and wept for her lost future. ³⁹ At the end of two months she returned to her father, and he kept the vow he had made. She had never been with a man. This gave rise to a custom in Israel: ⁴⁰ each year the young women of Israel would go out for four days to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.

chapters.title: Judges 12
paragraphs: ¹ The men of Ephraim mustered their forces and crossed north to Zaphon. They said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We're going to burn your house down over you!" ² Jephthah answered them, "I and my people were in a great struggle with the Ammonites, and when I called you, you didn't save me from their hands. ³ When I saw that you weren't going to help, I took my life in my hands and crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them to me. Why are you coming to fight me today?" ⁴ Then Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim. The Gileadites struck Ephraim down — for the Ephraimites had said, "You Gileadites are renegades from Ephraim and Manasseh!" ⁵ The Gileadites captured the fords of the Jordan before Ephraim could get there. Whenever a survivor of Ephraim said, "Let me cross," the men of Gilead would ask, "Are you an Ephraimite?" If he said no,

⁶ they would say, "Then say 'Shibboleth.'" If he said "Sibboleth," because he could not pronounce the word correctly, they would seize him and kill him at the ford of the Jordan. Forty-two thousand Ephraimites were killed at that time. ⁷ Jephthah led Israel for six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in one of the towns of Gilead. ⁸ After him, Ibzan of Bethlehem became judge over Israel. ⁹ He had thirty sons and thirty daughters. He arranged marriages for all his daughters outside his clan and brought in thirty young women from outside his clan for his sons. He led Israel for seven years. ¹⁰ Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.

¹¹ After him, Elon the Zebulunite became judge over Israel and led it for ten years. ¹² Then Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun. ¹³ After him, Abdon the son of Hillel, from Pirathon, became judge over Israel. ¹⁴ He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He led Israel for eight years. ¹⁵ Then Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

chapters.title: Judges 13
paragraphs: ¹ Again the Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD handed them over to the Philistines for forty years. ² A certain man of Zorah, from the tribe of Dan, whose name was Manoah, had a wife who was barren and had borne no children. ³ The angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, "You are barren and childless, but you are going to become pregnant and give birth to a son. ⁴ Now then, be careful not to drink wine or other fermented drink and not to eat anything unclean. ⁵ You will become pregnant and have a son whose head is never to be touched by a razor, because the boy will be dedicated to God as a Nazirite from the womb. He will begin the deliverance of Israel from the Philistines."

⁶ Then the woman went and told her husband: "A man of God came to me. He looked like an angel of God — very awe-inspiring. I didn't ask him where he came from, and he didn't tell me his name. ⁷ But he said to me, 'You are going to become pregnant and give birth to a son. Don't drink wine or other fermented drink and don't eat anything unclean, because the boy will be dedicated to God as a Nazirite from birth until the day of his death.'" ⁸ Then Manoah prayed to the LORD: "Please, Lord, let the man of God you sent come to us again to teach us how to raise the boy who is to be born." ⁹ God heard Manoah's prayer, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field. But her husband Manoah was not with her. ¹⁰ The woman hurried to tell her husband, "The man who appeared to me the other day is here!"

¹¹ Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he came to the man, he asked, "Are you the man who spoke to my wife?" "I am," he said. ¹² Manoah asked, "When your word comes true, what will be the rules for the boy's life and work?" ¹³ The angel of the LORD replied, "Let the woman pay attention to everything I told her. ¹⁴ She must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, nor drink wine or other fermented drink, nor eat anything unclean. She must do everything I commanded her." ¹⁵ Then Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "Please stay and let us prepare a young goat for you."

¹⁶ The angel of the LORD replied, "Even if you keep me here, I will not eat your food. But if you want to prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD." For Manoah did not yet realize that it was the angel of the LORD. ¹⁷ Then Manoah asked the angel of the LORD, "What is your name, so that we may honor you when your word comes true?" ¹⁸ The angel of the LORD replied, "Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding." ¹⁹ Then Manoah took a young goat and a grain offering and sacrificed them on a rock to the LORD. And the LORD did something remarkable while Manoah and his wife watched. ²⁰ As the flame blazed up from the altar toward heaven, the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame. Seeing this, Manoah and his wife fell face down on the ground.

²¹ The angel of the LORD did not appear again to Manoah and his wife. Then Manoah realized it was the angel of the LORD. ²² "We are going to die!" he said to his wife. "We have seen God!" ²³ But his wife replied, "If the LORD had meant to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and grain offering from our hands, nor shown us all these things, nor told us this at this time." ²⁴ The woman gave birth to a boy and named him Samson. The child grew and the LORD blessed him. ²⁵ The Spirit of the LORD began to stir him while he was in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

chapters.title: Judges 14
paragraphs: ¹ Samson went down to Timnah and saw a young Philistine woman there. ² When he returned home, he told his father and mother, "I've seen a Philistine woman in Timnah. Get her for me as my wife." ³ His father and mother replied, "Isn't there an acceptable woman among the women of your relatives or among all our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?" But Samson said to his father, "Get her for me. She's the right one for me." ⁴ His parents did not know that this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion to confront the Philistines. At that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel. ⁵ Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother. As they approached the vineyards of Timnah, suddenly a young lion came roaring toward him.

⁶ The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon Samson, and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as he might have torn a young goat — yet he told neither his father nor his mother what he had done. ⁷ Then he went down and talked with the woman, and he liked her. ⁸ Some time later, when he went back to marry her, he turned aside to look at the lion's carcass, and he saw a swarm of bees and some honey there. ⁹ He scooped it out with his hands and ate it as he walked along. He gave some to his parents, and they also ate it. But he didn't tell them he had taken the honey from the lion's carcass. ¹⁰ Then his father went down to see the woman. Samson held a feast there, as was the custom for young men.

¹¹ When the Philistines saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him. ¹² Samson said to them, "Let me tell you a riddle. If you can give me the answer within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes. ¹³ But if you can't tell me the answer, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes." "Tell us your riddle," they said. "Let's hear it." ¹⁴ He said to them, "Out of the eater, something to eat; out of the strong, something sweet." For three days they could not solve the riddle. ¹⁵ On the seventh day they said to Samson's wife, "Coax your husband into explaining the riddle for us, or we will burn you and your father's household. Did you invite us here to rob us?"

¹⁶ Samson's wife threw herself on him, sobbing, "You hate me! You don't really love me. You've given my people a riddle but you haven't told me the answer." "Look," he said, "I haven't even told my father or mother. Why would I tell you?" ¹⁷ She wept throughout the rest of the feast. On the seventh day he finally told her, because she had pressed him so hard. She then told the riddle's answer to her people. ¹⁸ Before sunset on the seventh day, the men of the town said to Samson, "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" Samson answered, "If you hadn't plowed with my heifer, you wouldn't have solved my riddle!" ¹⁹ Then the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him. He went down to Ashkelon, struck down thirty of their men, stripped them of their belongings, and gave their clothes to those who had answered the riddle. Burning with anger, he went up to his father's house. ²⁰ And Samson's wife was given to the companion who had attended him at the feast.

chapters.title: Judges 15
paragraphs: ¹ Later on, during the wheat harvest, Samson went to visit his wife, bringing a young goat as a gift. He said, "I want to go to my wife in her room." But her father would not let him in. ² Her father said, "I was so sure you hated her that I gave her to your companion. Isn't her younger sister more attractive? Take her instead." ³ Samson said to them, "This time I have a right to get even with the Philistines — I will really harm them." ⁴ So Samson went and caught three hundred foxes and tied them tail to tail in pairs. He then fastened a torch to every pair of tails, ⁵ lit the torches, and let the foxes loose in the standing grain of the Philistines. He burned up the shocks and standing grain, together with the vineyards and olive groves.

⁶ The Philistines asked, "Who did this?" They were told, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because the Timnite took his wife and gave her to his companion." So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death. ⁷ Samson said to them, "Since you've done this, I won't stop until I get my revenge on you." ⁸ He attacked them viciously and slaughtered many of them. Then he went down and stayed in a cave in the rock of Etam. ⁹ The Philistines went up and camped in Judah, spreading out near Lehi. ¹⁰ The people of Judah asked, "Why have you come to fight us?" They answered, "We've come to take Samson prisoner and do to him what he did to us."

¹¹ Three thousand men from Judah went down to the cave in the rock of Etam and said to Samson, "Don't you realize that the Philistines are rulers over us? What have you done to us?" He answered, "I only did to them what they did to me." ¹² They told him, "We've come to tie you up and hand you over to the Philistines." Samson said, "Swear to me that you won't kill me yourselves." ¹³ They replied, "Agreed. We'll only tie you up and hand you over to them. We certainly won't kill you." So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock. ¹⁴ As he approached Lehi, the Philistines came shouting to meet him. The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him, and the ropes on his arms became like charred flax, and the bindings dropped from his hands. ¹⁵ Finding a fresh jawbone of a donkey, he grabbed it and struck down a thousand men.

¹⁶ Then Samson said, "With a donkey's jawbone I have made donkeys of them! With a donkey's jawbone I have killed a thousand men!" ¹⁷ When he finished speaking, he threw away the jawbone and called that place Ramath-lehi. ¹⁸ Desperately thirsty, he cried out to the LORD, "You have given your servant this great victory. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?" ¹⁹ God split open the hollow place at Lehi, and water gushed out. When Samson drank, his strength returned and he revived. So the place was called En-hakkore, and it is still there at Lehi to this day. ²⁰ Samson led Israel for twenty years during the time of the Philistines.

chapters.title: Judges 16
paragraphs: ¹ Samson went to Gaza, where he saw a prostitute and slept with her. ² The people of Gaza were told, "Samson is here!" So they surrounded the place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They made no move during the night, saying, "When morning comes, we'll kill him." ³ But Samson lay there only until the middle of the night. Then he got up, grabbed the doors of the city gate along with the two posts, tore them loose, bar and all, hoisted them on his shoulders, and carried them to the top of the hill overlooking Hebron. ⁴ Later he fell in love with a woman in the valley of Sorek whose name was Delilah. ⁵ The Philistine rulers went to her and said, "Seduce him and find out what makes his strength so great, and how we can overpower and tie him up and subdue him. Each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver."

⁶ So Delilah said to Samson, "Tell me the secret of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued." ⁷ Samson answered her, "If someone ties me with seven fresh bowstrings that haven't been dried, I'll become as weak as any other man." ⁸ Then the Philistine rulers brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him with them. ⁹ While men were hidden in the room, she called out to him, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" But he snapped the bowstrings as easily as a piece of string snaps when it catches fire. So the secret of his strength was not discovered. ¹⁰ Then Delilah said to Samson, "You have made a fool of me and lied to me. Tell me how you can really be tied."

¹¹ He said, "If someone ties me securely with new ropes that have never been used, I'll become as weak as any other man." ¹² So Delilah took new ropes and tied him with them. Then she called out, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" And the men lying in wait were in the room. But he snapped the ropes off his arms like thread. ¹³ Delilah then said to Samson, "All this time you've been making a fool of me and lying to me. Tell me how you can really be tied." He replied, "If you weave the seven braids of my hair into the fabric on the loom and tighten it with the pin, I'll be as weak as any other man." ¹⁴ So while he slept, she wove his hair into the fabric and tightened it with the pin. Then she called, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" He awoke from his sleep and pulled out the loom pin, taking the loom and the fabric with him. ¹⁵ She said to him, "How can you say you love me when you won't confide in me? This is the third time you've made a fool of me and haven't told me the secret of your great strength."

¹⁶ With such nagging she prodded him day after day until he was sick to death of it. ¹⁷ So he told her everything. "No razor has ever been used on my head," he said, "because I have been dedicated to God as a Nazirite since birth. If my head were shaved, my strength would leave me, and I would become as weak as any other man." ¹⁸ When Delilah saw that he had told her everything, she sent word to the Philistine rulers: "Come back once more; he has told me everything." So the rulers came with the silver in their hands. ¹⁹ After putting him to sleep on her lap, she called for someone to shave off the seven braids of his hair. She began to subdue him, and his strength left him. ²⁰ Then she called, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" He awoke from his sleep and thought, "I'll go out as before and shake myself free." But he did not know that the LORD had left him.

²¹ The Philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes, and took him down to Gaza. They bound him with bronze shackles and set him to work grinding grain in the prison. ²² But his hair began to grow again after it had been shaved. ²³ Then the Philistine rulers gathered to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon and to celebrate, saying, "Our god has delivered Samson, our enemy, into our hands." ²⁴ When the people saw him, they praised their god and chanted, "Our god has delivered into our hands our enemy, the one who laid waste our land and multiplied our slain." ²⁵ While they were in high spirits, they shouted, "Bring out Samson to entertain us!" So they called Samson out of the prison, and he performed for them. They made him stand between the pillars.

²⁶ Samson said to the servant who held his hand, "Put me where I can feel the pillars that support the temple, so that I may lean against them." ²⁷ The temple was crowded with men and women; all the Philistine rulers were there, and on the roof were about three thousand men and women watching Samson perform. ²⁸ Then Samson prayed to the LORD, "Sovereign LORD, remember me. Please, God, strengthen me just once more, and let me with one blow get revenge on the Philistines for my two eyes." ²⁹ Then Samson reached toward the two central pillars on which the temple stood. Bracing himself against them — his right hand on one and his left on the other — ³⁰ he said, "Let me die with the Philistines!" Then he pushed with all his might, and down came the temple on the rulers and all the people in it. He killed many more when he died than while he lived.

³¹ Then his brothers and his father's whole family went down to get him. They brought him back and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. He had led Israel for twenty years.

chapters.title: Judges 17
paragraphs: ¹ There was a man named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim. ² He said to his mother, "The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you — I heard you utter a curse about it. Look, I have the silver. I took it." His mother replied, "The LORD bless you, my son!" ³ When he returned the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother, she said, "I solemnly dedicate this silver to the LORD for my son, to make an idol overlaid with silver. So now I will give it back to you." ⁴ He returned the money to his mother, and she took two hundred pieces of silver and gave them to a silversmith, who made them into an idol. It was placed in Micah's house. ⁵ Now this man Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and some household idols and consecrated one of his sons to be his priest.

⁶ In those days there was no king in Israel, and everyone did whatever seemed right to them. ⁷ There was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, from the tribe of Judah, who was a Levite living there. ⁸ He left Bethlehem to find a place to settle and came to the hill country of Ephraim, stopping at the house of Micah along the way. ⁹ Micah asked him, "Where are you from?" He answered, "I'm a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I'm looking for a place to live." ¹⁰ Micah said to him, "Stay with me and be my priest and spiritual father — I'll pay you ten pieces of silver a year, provide your clothing, and give you your meals." The Levite agreed to stay.

¹¹ The Levite was happy to live with the man, and Micah treated the young man like one of his own sons. ¹² Micah installed the Levite as his priest, and the young man lived in Micah's house. ¹³ Micah said, "Now I know the LORD will be good to me, because I have a Levite as my priest."

chapters.title: Judges 18
paragraphs: ¹ In those days there was no king in Israel. The tribe of Dan was still looking for a territory of their own to settle, because they had not yet received their full share among the tribes of Israel. ² The Danites sent five warriors from their clans, from Zorah and Eshtaol, to scout the land and explore it. They were told, "Go and explore." When they reached the hill country of Ephraim, they came to Micah's house and spent the night there. ³ While staying at Micah's house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite. They went in and asked him, "How did you end up here? What are you doing in this place? What's your work here?" ⁴ He told them what Micah had arranged with him — that he had hired him to be his priest. ⁵ They asked him, "Please inquire of God for us, so we can know whether our mission will succeed."

⁶ The priest said to them, "Go in peace. Your journey has the LORD's blessing." ⁷ The five men set out and arrived at Laish. They saw that the people there lived in safety, like the Sidonians — peaceful and secure. No one in the region had the authority to oppress them in any way. They were far from Sidon and had no ties to anyone else. ⁸ The scouts returned to their kinsmen at Zorah and Eshtaol, who asked, "What's your report?" ⁹ They said, "Get moving — let's attack them! We've seen the land, and it's excellent. Are you just going to sit here? Don't hesitate — go and take possession of it. ¹⁰ When you arrive, you'll find an unsuspecting people in a spacious land. God has given it into your hands — a place that lacks nothing the earth has to offer."

¹¹ Six hundred Danite warriors, armed for battle, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol. ¹² They camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah — that place is still called Mahaneh-dan to this day; it lies west of Kiriath-jearim. ¹³ From there they moved on through the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah's house. ¹⁴ The five men who had spied out the region around Laish spoke up to their kinsmen: "Do you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household idols, a carved image, and a cast idol? Think about what you want to do." ¹⁵ They turned toward the house and went to the home of the young Levite — Micah's house — and greeted him.

¹⁶ The six hundred armed Danite warriors stood guard at the entrance of the gate, ¹⁷ while the five scouts went in and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the cast idol. The priest stood at the gate with the six hundred armed men. ¹⁸ When the scouts went into Micah's house and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the cast idol, the priest said, "What are you doing?" ¹⁹ They told him, "Be quiet. Keep your mouth shut and come with us. Be our father and priest — is it better to be priest for one man's house, or priest for a whole tribe and clan in Israel?" ²⁰ The priest was glad. He took the ephod, the household idols, and the carved image and went along with the people.

²¹ They set out with the children, the livestock, and the valuables leading the way. ²² When they had gone some distance from Micah's house, his neighbors came together and caught up with the Danites. ²³ They called out to them, and the Danites turned and said to Micah, "What's the matter with you that you've come after us with this mob?" ²⁴ He said, "You took my gods that I made, and the priest — you've gone off with everything. What do I have left? How can you say 'What's the matter with you?'" ²⁵ The Danites replied, "Don't raise your voice against us, or some hot-tempered men will come at you and cost you your life and the lives of your household."

²⁶ So the Danites went on their way. Micah, seeing that they were too strong for him, turned around and went home. ²⁷ They took what Micah had made, along with his priest, and attacked Laish — a peaceful, unsuspecting people. They killed them with the sword and burned down the city. ²⁸ There was no one to rescue them, for Laish was far from Sidon and had no alliance with anyone. It lay in the valley near Beth-rehob. They rebuilt the city and settled there. ²⁹ They named it Dan after their ancestor Dan, a son of Israel — though the city had originally been called Laish. ³⁰ The Danites set up the carved image, and Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses, along with his sons, served as priests to the tribe of Dan until the time of the exile.
³¹ They kept Micah's carved image in place throughout the entire time the house of God was at Shiloh.

chapters.title: Judges 19
paragraphs: ¹ In those days, when there was no king in Israel, a Levite living in a remote part of the hill country of Ephraim took a woman from Bethlehem in Judah as his concubine. ² But she was unfaithful to him and left, returning to her father's house in Bethlehem, where she stayed for four months. ³ Her husband set out after her to speak tenderly to her and bring her back. He had his servant and a pair of donkeys with him. She brought him into her father's house, and when her father saw him, he was glad to meet him. ⁴ His father-in-law, the young woman's father, urged him to stay; so he remained there three days, and they ate and drank and spent the nights together. ⁵ On the fourth day they rose early to leave, but the young woman's father said to his son-in-law, "Have something to eat first, then you can be on your way."

⁶ So the two of them sat down and ate and drank together. Then the young woman's father said, "Please stay tonight and enjoy yourself." ⁷ When the man got up to leave, his father-in-law pressed him, so he spent another night there. ⁸ On the fifth day he rose early to go, but the young woman's father said, "Please refresh yourself first." They lingered until afternoon, and the two of them ate together. ⁹ When the man finally got up to leave with his concubine and servant, his father-in-law said, "Look, it's nearly evening — the day is almost gone. Stay the night. It'll be good for you, and tomorrow you can get an early start and head home." ¹⁰ But this time the man would not stay. He set out and traveled as far as Jebus — that is, Jerusalem — with his two saddled donkeys and his concubine.

¹¹ When they were near Jebus, the day was almost gone, and the servant said to his master, "Let's stop at this Jebusite city and spend the night here." ¹² His master replied, "We won't turn in to a foreign city where the people are not Israelites. We'll go on to Gibeah." ¹³ He told his servant, "Come, let's try to reach Gibeah or Ramah and spend the night in one of those places." ¹⁴ They pressed on, and the sun went down just as they were approaching Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin. ¹⁵ They turned off there to spend the night in Gibeah. The man went in and sat down in the town square, but no one took them in for the night.

¹⁶ That evening an old man came in from his work in the fields. He was from the hill country of Ephraim and was living in Gibeah, though the townspeople were Benjamites. ¹⁷ He looked up and saw the traveler in the town square and asked, "Where are you going? Where did you come from?" ¹⁸ The man answered, "We're traveling from Bethlehem in Judah to a place in the hill country of Ephraim — that's where I'm from. I went to Bethlehem, and now I'm heading back home. But no one here has taken us in. ¹⁹ We have straw and fodder for our donkeys, and there is bread and wine for me and the woman and our young servant. We don't need anything." ²⁰ "You are welcome," the old man said. "Let me provide everything you need. Just don't spend the night in the square."

²¹ He brought them into his house and fed the donkeys. They washed their feet and ate and drank. ²² While they were enjoying themselves, a mob of troublemakers from the town surrounded the house, pounding on the door. They shouted to the old man, the owner of the house, "Bring out the man who came to your house! We want to have sex with him." ²³ The owner of the house went outside and said to them, "No, my friends, please don't do such a wicked thing. This man is a guest in my house — don't commit this outrage. ²⁴ Look, here is my virgin daughter, and the man's concubine. Let me bring them out. You can have your way with them and do to them whatever you like. But don't do this disgraceful thing to this man." ²⁵ The men wouldn't listen. So the man took his concubine and pushed her outside to them. They raped her and abused her throughout the night until morning. When dawn broke, they let her go.

²⁶ At daybreak the woman came and collapsed at the doorway of the house where her master was staying and lay there until it grew light. ²⁷ When her master got up in the morning and opened the door to continue his journey, he found his concubine lying at the entrance with her hands on the threshold. ²⁸ "Get up," he said. "Let's go." But there was no answer. He lifted her onto the donkey and set out for home. ²⁹ When he reached his house, he took a knife and cut his concubine limb from limb into twelve pieces, then sent them throughout all the territories of Israel. ³⁰ Everyone who saw it declared, "Nothing like this has ever happened or been seen since the day the Israelites came up from Egypt. Think about it! What are we going to do? Let's hear what you have to say."

chapters.title: Judges 20
paragraphs: ¹ All the Israelites came out as one, from Dan to Beersheba and throughout the land of Gilead, and assembled before the LORD at Mizpah. ² The leaders of all the people and all the tribes of Israel took their places in the assembly of God's people — four hundred thousand soldiers armed with swords. ³ (The Benjamites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah.) Then the Israelites said, "Tell us — how did this terrible thing happen?" ⁴ The Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered: "I and my concubine came to Gibeah in Benjamin territory to spend the night. ⁵ During the night the men of Gibeah came after me and surrounded the house. They intended to kill me. They raped my concubine, and she died.

⁶ "I took my concubine's body, cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the territory of Israel, because they committed this vile and outrageous act in Israel. ⁷ You are all Israelites — speak up and decide what should be done." ⁸ All the people rose as one and declared, "None of us will go home. Not a single one of us will return to his house. ⁹ This is what we'll do to Gibeah: we'll go up against it by lot, ¹⁰ taking ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel — a hundred from a thousand, a thousand from ten thousand — to gather provisions for the army. When the force arrives at Gibeah in Benjamin, they will repay them for all the outrage they have committed in Israel."

¹¹ So all the Israelites came together united against the city. ¹² The tribes of Israel sent messengers throughout the tribe of Benjamin, saying, "What is this terrible thing that has happened among you? ¹³ Hand over those scoundrels in Gibeah so we can put them to death and purge this evil from Israel." But the Benjamites refused to listen to their fellow Israelites. ¹⁴ Instead, they gathered from their towns at Gibeah to fight the Israelites. ¹⁵ At that time the Benjamites mustered from their towns twenty-six thousand swordsmen, plus seven hundred elite fighters from Gibeah itself.

¹⁶ Among all these warriors were seven hundred specially chosen left-handed men, every one of whom could sling a stone and hit a target within a hair's width without missing. ¹⁷ The Israelites, not counting Benjamin, mustered four hundred thousand swordsmen, all experienced soldiers. ¹⁸ The Israelites went up to Bethel and consulted God. They asked, "Which tribe should attack Benjamin first?" The LORD answered, "Judah shall go first." ¹⁹ The Israelites rose the next morning and took up positions against Gibeah. ²⁰ The Israelite army marched out to fight Benjamin and drew up their battle lines at Gibeah.

²¹ The Benjamites came out of Gibeah and struck down twenty-two thousand Israelites in the field that day. ²² But the Israelite soldiers rallied and took up their positions again in the same place as the first day. ²³ (They had gone up and wept before the LORD until evening, and had asked, "Should we go and fight our brother Benjamin again?" The LORD said, "Go up against him.") ²⁴ The Israelites advanced against the Benjamites the second day. ²⁵ Again Benjamin came out from Gibeah to meet them and cut down another eighteen thousand Israelites — all of them armed soldiers.

²⁶ Then all the Israelites, the whole army, went up to Bethel and sat weeping before the LORD. They fasted that day until evening and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings to the LORD. ²⁷ The Israelites inquired of the LORD — for the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days, ²⁸ and Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, was serving before it — asking, "Should we go out once more to fight our brother Benjamin, or should we stop?" The LORD answered, "Go, for tomorrow I will give them into your hands." ²⁹ Israel set an ambush around Gibeah. ³⁰ The Israelites went up against the Benjamites on the third day and took their positions against Gibeah as before.

³¹ The Benjamites came out against the army and were drawn away from the city. They began inflicting casualties as before, killing about thirty Israelites in the open fields — along the roads leading to Bethel and Gibeah. ³² The Benjamites thought, "We're defeating them as before." But the Israelites had said, "Let's retreat and draw them away from the city toward the roads." ³³ All the Israelites moved from their positions and formed up at Baal-tamar, while those in the ambush burst out from their positions west of Gibeah. ³⁴ Ten thousand elite Israelite fighters launched a direct assault on Gibeah. The fighting was fierce, and the Benjamites did not realize that disaster was closing in on them. ³⁵ The LORD struck down Benjamin before Israel, and the Israelites killed twenty-five thousand one hundred Benjamite swordsmen that day.

³⁶ The Benjamites saw that they were beaten — the Israelites had given ground only because they trusted the men in the ambush they had set near Gibeah. ³⁷ Those in ambush made a sudden dash into Gibeah and swept through the city, killing everyone with the sword. ³⁸ The prearranged signal between the main Israelite force and those in ambush was a great cloud of smoke rising from the city. ³⁹ When the Israelites turned back in the fighting, the Benjamites had already killed about thirty of them, thinking, "We're winning — just like the first battle!" ⁴⁰ But then the signal column of smoke began rising from the city. The Benjamites looked back, and the whole city was going up in flames.

⁴¹ When the Israelites turned back to attack, the Benjamites panicked, for they could see that disaster had overtaken them. ⁴² They retreated before the Israelites toward the desert road, but they could not escape the battle. The Israelites who came out of the towns cut them down right there. ⁴³ They had the Benjamites surrounded; they chased them down and easily trampled them in the area east of Gibeah. ⁴⁴ Eighteen thousand Benjamites fell — all of them fighting men. ⁴⁵ The rest turned and fled toward the desert to the rock of Rimmon. The Israelites cut down five thousand more along the roads, then pursued them as far as Gidom and killed another two thousand.

⁴⁶ In all, twenty-five thousand Benjamite swordsmen fell that day — all of them warriors. ⁴⁷ But six hundred men escaped to the desert and took refuge at the rock of Rimmon, where they stayed for four months. ⁴⁸ Then the Israelite army turned back against the remaining Benjamites and put to the sword every person in the towns, including the animals and everything else they found. They also set fire to every town they came to.

chapters.title: Judges 21
paragraphs: ¹ Now the men of Israel had taken an oath at Mizpah: "None of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjamite." ² The people came to Bethel and sat before God until evening, wailing loudly. ³ "LORD, God of Israel," they cried, "why has this happened in Israel — that today one tribe is missing from Israel?" ⁴ The next morning the people rose early, built an altar there, and presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. ⁵ Then the Israelites asked, "Which of the tribes of Israel did not come up with the assembly to the LORD?" They had bound themselves with a solemn oath that anyone who did not come up to Mizpah before the LORD would be put to death.

⁶ The Israelites grieved for their brother Benjamin. "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel," they said. ⁷ "How can we provide wives for those who are left, since we've sworn by the LORD not to give them our daughters?" ⁸ They asked, "Which of the Israelite tribes did not come to Mizpah before the LORD?" They found that no one from Jabesh-gilead had come to the assembly camp. ⁹ When the people were counted, not a single person from Jabesh-gilead was there. ¹⁰ So the assembly sent twelve thousand warriors with orders: "Go and put the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead to the sword, including the women and children."

¹¹ "This is what you must do," they were told. "Kill every man and every woman who has slept with a man." ¹² They found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young women who had never slept with a man, and brought them to the camp at Shiloh in Canaan. ¹³ The whole assembly sent a message to the Benjamites at the rock of Rimmon, offering them peace. ¹⁴ Benjamin returned at that time, and the Israelites gave them the women from Jabesh-gilead who had been spared — but there were not enough to go around. ¹⁵ The people felt sorry for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a gap in the tribes of Israel.

¹⁶ The elders of the assembly asked, "How can we find wives for those who are left, since the women of Benjamin have been destroyed? ¹⁷ There must be survivors for Benjamin's descendants so that a tribe of Israel is not wiped out. ¹⁸ But we cannot give them our own daughters as wives, because the Israelites swore an oath: 'Cursed be anyone who gives a wife to a Benjamite.'" ¹⁹ Then they thought of something. "Look," they said, "there is an annual festival of the LORD at Shiloh — north of Bethel, east of the main road that runs from Bethel up to Shechem, and south of Lebonah." ²⁰ So they told the Benjamites, "Go and hide in the vineyards,

²¹ and watch. When the young women of Shiloh come out to join in the dancing, rush out from the vineyards and each of you seize a wife from among them and go to the land of Benjamin. ²² If their fathers or brothers come to us with a complaint, we'll tell them, 'Do us this favor, for we couldn't get wives for all of them in the war. You aren't guilty of breaking your oath, since you didn't give your daughters to them — they took them.'" ²³ The Benjamites did as they were told. Each man caught a wife from among the dancers. They went back to their own land, rebuilt the towns, and settled in them. ²⁴ The Israelites also left at that time, each returning to his own tribe and clan, and they all went back to their own lands. ²⁵ In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in their own eyes.

chapters.title: Ruth 1
paragraphs: ¹ In the days when the judges ruled Israel, a famine struck the land. A man from Bethlehem in Judah left to live as a foreigner in the country of Moab, taking his wife and two sons with him. ² The man's name was Elimelech, his wife's name was Naomi, and his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion — Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They arrived in Moab and settled there. ³ Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons. ⁴ The sons married Moabite women — one named Orpah, the other Ruth — and they lived there for about ten years. ⁵ Then Mahlon and Chilion also died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and her husband.

⁶ Then Naomi prepared to return from Moab with her daughters-in-law, because she had heard that the LORD had come to the aid of his people by providing food for them. ⁷ She set out from the place where she had been living, and her two daughters-in-law went with her along the road back to Judah. ⁸ Naomi said to them, "Go back, each of you, to your mother's home. May the LORD show you the same kindness you have shown to the dead and to me. ⁹ May the LORD grant that each of you will find rest in the home of a new husband." Then she kissed them, and they all wept aloud. ¹⁰ They said to her, "We will go back with you to your people."

¹¹ But Naomi said, "Go back, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Do I still have sons in my womb who could become your husbands? ¹² Go back, my daughters — I am too old to marry again. Even if I thought there was still hope, even if I married tonight and bore sons, ¹³ would you wait for them to grow up? Would you go without husbands all that time? No, my daughters. This is far more bitter for me than for you, because the LORD's hand has turned against me." ¹⁴ They wept aloud again. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her. ¹⁵ Naomi said, "Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods. Go back with her."

¹⁶ But Ruth said, "Don't urge me to leave you or to turn back from you. Where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay. Your people will be my people and your God my God. ¹⁷ Where you die I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD deal with me, ever so severely, if anything but death separates us." ¹⁸ When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her. ¹⁹ So the two women traveled on until they came to Bethlehem. When they arrived, the whole town was stirred because of them, and the women asked, "Can this be Naomi?" ²⁰ She said to them, "Don't call me Naomi — call me Mara, because the Almighty has made my life very bitter.

²¹ I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi? The LORD has afflicted me; the Almighty has brought misfortune upon me." ²² So Naomi returned from Moab, accompanied by her daughter-in-law Ruth the Moabite. They arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

chapters.title: Ruth 2
paragraphs: ¹ Now Naomi had a relative on her husband's side, a prominent and wealthy man from Elimelech's family, whose name was Boaz. ² Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go to the fields and pick up the leftover grain behind anyone who will allow me to do so." Naomi said to her, "Go ahead, my daughter." ³ So she went out, and began gleaning in the fields behind the harvesters. As it turned out, she found herself working in the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the family of Elimelech. ⁴ Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and greeted the harvesters, "The LORD be with you!" They answered, "The LORD bless you!" ⁵ Boaz asked the overseer of his harvesters, "Who does that young woman belong to?"

⁶ The overseer replied, "She is the Moabite woman who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab. ⁷ She asked, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' She came in the morning and has been working steadily, except for a short rest in the shelter." ⁸ So Boaz said to Ruth, "My daughter, listen to me. Don't go to glean in another field, and don't leave this one. Stay here close to my women workers. ⁹ Watch which fields they are harvesting and follow along after them. I have told the men not to lay a hand on you. And whenever you are thirsty, go drink from the water jars the men have filled." ¹⁰ At this, she bowed down with her face to the ground and asked him, "Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you notice me — a foreigner?"

¹¹ Boaz replied, "I have heard the full story of everything you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband's death — how you left your father and mother and your homeland and came to live with a people you did not know before. ¹² May the LORD repay you for what you have done. May you be richly rewarded by the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge." ¹³ She said, "May I continue to find favor in your eyes, my lord. You have put me at ease and spoken kindly to your servant, even though I am not one of your own servants." ¹⁴ At mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come over here and have some bread. Dip it in the vinegar." She sat down beside the harvesters, and he offered her some roasted grain. She ate until she was satisfied and had some left over. ¹⁵ As she got up to glean, Boaz instructed his men, "Let her glean even among the sheaves and do not rebuke her.

¹⁶ Also pull out some stalks from the bundles and leave them for her to pick up — and don't reprimand her." ¹⁷ So Ruth gleaned in the field until evening. When she threshed what she had gathered, it amounted to about an ephah of barley. ¹⁸ She carried it back to town, and her mother-in-law saw how much she had gathered. Ruth also brought out and gave her what she had saved from her meal. ¹⁹ Her mother-in-law asked her, "Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who took notice of you!" Then Ruth told her mother-in-law about the man she had worked with. "The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz," she said. ²⁰ Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "May the LORD bless him! He has not stopped showing his kindness to the living and to the dead." Then Naomi added, "That man is a close relative of ours — one of our guardian-redeemers."

²¹ Ruth the Moabite said, "He also told me, 'Stay close to my workers until they have finished harvesting all my grain.'" ²² Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It will be good for you, my daughter, to go with his women workers, so that you will not be harmed in another field." ²³ So Ruth stayed close to the women workers of Boaz and gleaned until the end of the barley and wheat harvests. And she lived with her mother-in-law.

chapters.title: Ruth 3
paragraphs: ¹ One day Naomi, Ruth's mother-in-law, said to her, "My daughter, I need to find a home for you where you will be well provided for. ² Now, Boaz, whose women workers you have been with, is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be winnowing barley on the threshing floor. ³ Wash and perfume yourself, put on your best clothes, and go down to the threshing floor. But don't let him know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking. ⁴ When he lies down, note the place where he is lying. Then go and uncover his feet and lie down. He will tell you what to do." ⁵ Ruth answered, "I will do everything you say."

⁶ So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had told her. ⁷ When Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he went to lie down at the far end of the grain pile. Ruth approached quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down. ⁸ In the middle of the night something startled the man; he turned and discovered a woman lying at his feet. ⁹ "Who are you?" he asked. "I am your servant Ruth," she said. "Spread the corner of your garment over me, since you are a guardian-redeemer of our family." ¹⁰ "The LORD bless you, my daughter," he replied. "This act of kindness is greater than the one before — you have not run after younger men, whether rich or poor."

¹¹ "And now, my daughter, don't be afraid. I will do for you all you ask. All the people of my town know that you are a woman of noble character. ¹² Although it is true that I am a guardian-redeemer, there is another who is more closely related than I. ¹³ Stay here for the night, and in the morning, if he wants to do his duty as your guardian-redeemer, good — let him do it. But if he is not willing, then as surely as the LORD lives, I will do it. Lie down until morning." ¹⁴ So she lay at his feet until morning, but she got up before anyone could be recognized. He said, "No one must know that a woman came to the threshing floor." ¹⁵ He also said, "Bring me the shawl you are wearing and hold it out." When she did so, he poured into it six measures of barley and placed it on her. Then he went back to town.

¹⁶ When Ruth came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, "How did it go, my daughter?" Then Ruth told her everything the man had done for her. ¹⁷ She added, "He gave me these six measures of barley, saying, 'Don't go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.'" ¹⁸ Then Naomi said, "Wait, my daughter, until you find out what happens. The man will not rest until the matter is settled today."

chapters.title: Ruth 4
paragraphs: ¹ Meanwhile, Boaz went up to the town gate and sat down there. When the guardian-redeemer he had mentioned came along, Boaz said, "Come over here, friend, and sit down." So he went over and sat down. ² Boaz then gathered ten of the town elders and said, "Sit here." And they did so. ³ Then he said to the guardian-redeemer, "Naomi, who has come back from Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our relative Elimelech. ⁴ I thought I should bring it to your attention so that you may buy it in the presence of these seated here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, do so. But if you will not, tell me so I will know, because no one else has the right to redeem it except you, and I am next after you." "I will redeem it," he said. ⁵ Then Boaz said, "On the day you buy the land from Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the widow of the deceased, in order to maintain the name of the dead with his property."

⁶ At this, the guardian-redeemer said, "Then I cannot redeem it, because it might endanger my own inheritance. You redeem it yourself — I cannot do it." ⁷ (Now in earlier times in Israel, for the redemption and transfer of property to become final, one party took off his sandal and gave it to the other. This was the method of legalizing transactions in Israel.) ⁸ So the guardian-redeemer said to Boaz, "Buy it yourself." And he removed his sandal. ⁹ Then Boaz announced to the elders and all the people, "Today you are witnesses that I have bought from Naomi all the property of Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon. ¹⁰ I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon's widow, as my wife, in order to maintain the name of the dead with his property, so that his name will not disappear from among his family or from his hometown. Today you are witnesses!"

¹¹ Then the elders and all the people at the gate said, "We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman who is coming into your home like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the family of Israel. May you have standing in Ephrathah and be famous in Bethlehem. ¹² Through the offspring the LORD gives you by this young woman, may your family be like that of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah." ¹³ So Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife. When he made love to her, the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son. ¹⁴ The women said to Naomi, "Praise be to the LORD, who this day has not left you without a guardian-redeemer. May his name become famous throughout Israel! ¹⁵ He will renew your life and sustain you in your old age. For your daughter-in-law, who loves you and who is better to you than seven sons, has given him birth."

¹⁶ Then Naomi took the child in her arms and cared for him. ¹⁷ The women living there said, "Naomi has a son!" And they named him Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David. ¹⁸ This, then, is the family line of Perez: Perez was the father of Hezron, ¹⁹ Hezron the father of Ram, Ram the father of Amminadab, ²⁰ Amminadab the father of Nahshon, Nahshon the father of Salmon,
²¹ Salmon the father of Boaz, Boaz the father of Obed, ²² Obed the father of Jesse, and Jesse the father of David.

chapters.title: 1 Samuel 1
paragraphs: ¹ There was a man from Ramathaim-Zophim in the hill country of Ephraim named Elkanah son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephrathite. ² He had two wives; one was named Hannah and the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none. ³ Year after year this man would go up from his town to worship and offer sacrifices to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh, where Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, served as priests. ⁴ Whenever the day came for Elkanah to sacrifice, he would give portions of the meat to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters. ⁵ But to Hannah he gave a double portion, because he loved her—and yet the LORD had closed her womb.

⁶ Her rival Peninnah would taunt and provoke her constantly because the LORD had kept her from having children. ⁷ This happened year after year. Whenever Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, Peninnah would mock her until she wept and could not eat. ⁸ Her husband Elkanah would say to her, "Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why are you so heartbroken? Am I not better to you than ten sons?" ⁹ Once, after they had eaten and drunk at Shiloh, Hannah got up. Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the LORD's temple. ¹⁰ Deeply distressed, she prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly.

¹¹ She made a vow, saying, "LORD of Hosts, if you will look on the suffering of your servant and remember me—if you will not forget me but give me a son—then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor will ever touch his head." ¹² As she continued praying before the LORD, Eli was watching her mouth. ¹³ Hannah was praying silently; her lips were moving but her voice was inaudible, so Eli thought she was drunk. ¹⁴ He said to her, "How long are you going to be drunk? Get rid of your wine." ¹⁵ "No, my lord," Hannah replied, "I am a woman in deep anguish. I haven't been drinking wine or beer; I've been pouring out my soul to the LORD.

¹⁶ Don't take your servant for a worthless woman. I've been speaking all this time out of great anguish and grief." ¹⁷ Then Eli answered, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant what you have asked of him." ¹⁸ "May your servant find favor in your eyes," she said. Then she went her way, ate something, and her face was no longer downcast. ¹⁹ Early the next morning they rose, worshiped before the LORD, and returned home to Ramah. Elkanah made love to his wife Hannah, and the LORD remembered her. ²⁰ Before the year was out, Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, "Because I asked the LORD for him."

²¹ When Elkanah and all his household went up to offer the annual sacrifice and to fulfill his vow to the LORD, ²² Hannah did not go. She told her husband, "After the boy is weaned, I'll take him and present him before the LORD, and he will stay there permanently." ²³ Her husband Elkanah said to her, "Do what seems best to you. Stay home until you have weaned him. May the LORD bring his word to pass." So Hannah stayed and nursed her son until she weaned him. ²⁴ After she had weaned him, she took him up to Shiloh, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. The boy was still young. They brought him to the house of the LORD. ²⁵ Then they slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eli.

²⁶ She said, "Excuse me, my lord. As surely as you live, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD. ²⁷ I prayed for this child, and the LORD has given me what I asked of him. ²⁸ So now I'm giving him back to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is given to the LORD." And they worshiped the LORD there.

chapters.title: 1 Samuel 2
paragraphs: ¹ Then Hannah prayed and said: "My heart rejoices in the LORD; in the LORD my strength is lifted high. My mouth boasts over my enemies, for I delight in your deliverance. ² There is no one holy like the LORD; there is no one besides you; there is no Rock like our God. ³ Don't keep talking so proudly or let your mouth speak such arrogance, for the LORD is a God who knows, and by him deeds are weighed. ⁴ The bows of the warriors are broken, but those who stumbled are armed with strength. ⁵ Those who were well-fed hire themselves out for bread, but those who were hungry are hungry no more. The barren woman has borne seven children, but she who had many sons pines away.

⁶ The LORD brings death and gives life; he sends down to the grave and raises up. ⁷ The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he humbles and he exalts. ⁸ He lifts the poor from the dust and raises the needy from the ash heap; he seats them with princes and has them inherit a place of honor. For the foundations of the earth are the LORD's; on them he has set the world. ⁹ He guards the feet of his faithful servants, but the wicked are silenced in the darkness. It is not by strength that a person prevails; ¹⁰ those who oppose the LORD will be shattered. The Most High will thunder from heaven; the LORD will judge the ends of the earth. He will give strength to his king and exalt the power of his anointed."

¹¹ Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy ministered before the LORD under Eli the priest. ¹² Eli's sons were wicked men; they had no regard for the LORD. ¹³ Now it was the practice of the priests that whenever anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come with a three-pronged fork in his hand while the meat was still boiling. ¹⁴ He would plunge the fork into the pan, kettle, cauldron, or pot, and the priest would take whatever the fork brought up. This is how they treated all the Israelites who came to Shiloh. ¹⁵ But even before the fat was burned, the priest's servant would come and say to the person sacrificing, "Give the priest some meat to roast. He won't accept boiled meat from you—only raw."

¹⁶ If the man said, "Let the fat be burned first, and then take as much as you want," the servant would reply, "No, hand it over right now, or I'll take it by force." ¹⁷ This sin of the young men was very serious in the LORD's sight, because they were treating the LORD's offering with contempt. ¹⁸ But Samuel was ministering before the LORD—a boy wearing a linen ephod. ¹⁹ Each year his mother made him a little robe and brought it to him when she came up with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice. ²⁰ Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, "May the LORD give you children by this woman to take the place of the one she prayed for and gave to the LORD." Then they would go home.

²¹ The LORD was gracious to Hannah; she conceived and gave birth to three more sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD. ²² Now Eli was very old, and he kept hearing about everything his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they slept with the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting. ²³ He said to them, "Why do you do such things? I hear from all these people about your wicked deeds. ²⁴ No, my sons; it is not a good report that I hear spreading among the LORD's people. ²⁵ If one person sins against another, God may mediate; but if someone sins against the LORD, who will intercede for them?" His sons, however, would not listen to their father's rebuke, for it was the LORD's will to put them to death.

²⁶ And the boy Samuel continued to grow in stature and in favor with the LORD and with people. ²⁷ Now a man of God came to Eli and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Did I not clearly reveal myself to your ancestor's family when they were in Egypt under Pharaoh? ²⁸ I chose your ancestor out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, and to wear an ephod in my presence. I also gave your ancestor's family all the offerings made by fire from the Israelites. ²⁹ Why do you scorn my sacrifice and offering that I prescribed for my dwelling? Why do you honor your sons more than me by fattening yourselves on the best parts of every offering made by my people Israel?'

³¹ 'The time is coming when I will cut off your strength and the strength of your ancestral house, so that no one in your family will reach old age. ³² You will see distress in my dwelling. Although good things will happen to Israel, no one in your family line will ever reach old age. ³³ Every one of you that I do not cut off from my altar will waste away with grief; and all the rest of your descendants will die by the sword. ³⁴ And what happens to your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will be a sign to you—they will both die on the same day. ³⁵ I will raise up for myself a faithful priest who will do what is in my heart and mind. I will build for him an enduring family line, and he will minister before my anointed one always.

³⁶ Then everyone left in your family line will come and bow down before him for a piece of silver and a crust of bread, and will plead, "Please give me some priestly work so I can have food to eat."'"

chapters.title: 1 Samuel 3
paragraphs: ¹ The boy Samuel ministered before the LORD under Eli. In those days the word of the LORD was rare; visions were not common. ² One night Eli, whose eyesight had grown so weak that he could barely see, was lying down in his usual place. ³ The lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the house of the LORD, where the ark of God was. ⁴ Then the LORD called Samuel. Samuel answered, "Here I am." ⁵ He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am; you called me." But Eli said, "I didn't call you; go back to bed." So he went and lay down.

⁶ The LORD called again, "Samuel!" Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am; you called me." "I didn't call you, my son," Eli said. "Go back to bed." ⁷ Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD; the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him. ⁸ The LORD called Samuel a third time, and Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am; you called me." Then Eli realized that the LORD was calling the boy. ⁹ So Eli told Samuel, "Go and lie down. If he calls you, say, 'Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening.'" So Samuel went and lay down in his place. ¹⁰ The LORD came and stood there, calling as at the other times, "Samuel! Samuel!" Then Samuel said, "Speak, for your servant is listening."

¹¹ And the LORD said to Samuel: "See, I am about to do something in Israel that will make the ears of everyone who hears about it tingle. ¹² At that time I will carry out against Eli everything I spoke against his family—from beginning to end. ¹³ For I told him that I would judge his family forever because of the sin he knew about; his sons blasphemed God, and he failed to restrain them. ¹⁴ Therefore I swore to the house of Eli: 'The guilt of Eli's house will never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering.'"

¹⁶ Eli called Samuel and said, "Samuel, my son." Samuel answered, "Here I am." ¹⁷ "What was it he said to you?" Eli asked. "Do not hide it from me. May God deal with you severely if you hide from me anything he told you." ¹⁸ So Samuel told him everything, hiding nothing from him.
