Whenever anyone came with a complaint to bring before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out to him, “What town are you from?” He would answer, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel.” ³ Then Absalom would say, “Look, your claims are valid and proper, but there is no representative of the king to hear you.” ⁴ And Absalom would add, “If only I were appointed judge in the land! Then everyone who has a complaint or case could come to me, and I would see that he receives justice.” ⁵ Also, whenever anyone approached him to bow down before him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him and kiss him.

⁶ Absalom behaved in this way toward all the Israelites who came to the king for a decision, and so he stole the hearts of the men of Israel. ⁷ At the end of four years, Absalom said to the king, “Let me go to Hebron and fulfill a vow I made to the LORD. ⁸ While your servant was living at Geshur in Aram, I made a vow: 'If the LORD takes me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron.'” ⁹ The king said to him, “Go in peace.” So he went to Hebron. ¹⁰ Then Absalom sent secret messengers throughout the tribes of Israel to say, “As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpets, then say, 'Absalom is king in Hebron!'”

¹¹ Two hundred men from Jerusalem had accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and went quite innocently, knowing nothing about the matter. ¹² While Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he also sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his hometown of Giloh. And so the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom's following kept growing. ¹³ A messenger came and told David, “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.” ¹⁴ Then David said to all his officials who were with him in Jerusalem, “Come! We must flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. We must leave immediately, or he will move quickly to overtake us, bring ruin on us, and put the city to the sword.” ¹⁵ The king's officials answered him, “Your servants are ready to do whatever our lord the king chooses.”

¹⁶ The king set out with his entire household following him; but he left ten concubines to take care of the palace. ¹⁷ So the king set out, with all the people following him, and they halted at the edge of the city. ¹⁸ All his servants passed by him; all the Kerethites, all the Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who had accompanied him from Gath marched past the king. ¹⁹ The king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you come along with us? Go back and stay with King Absalom. You are a foreigner, an exile from your homeland. ²⁰ You came only yesterday. And today shall I make you wander about with us, when I do not know where I am going? Go back, and take your people with you. May the LORD show you kindness and faithfulness.”

²¹ But Ittai replied to the king, “As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be.” ²² David said to Ittai, “Go ahead, march on.” So Ittai the Gittite marched on with all his men and all the families that were with him. ²³ The whole countryside wept aloud as all these people passed by. The king also crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people moved on toward the wilderness. ²⁴ Zadok was there too, and all the Levites who were with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had finished leaving the city. ²⁵ Then the king said to Zadok, “Take the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the LORD's eyes, he will bring me back and let me see it and his dwelling place again.

²⁶ But if he says, 'I am not pleased with you,' then I am ready; let him do to me whatever seems good to him.” ²⁷ The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Do you understand? Go back to the city in peace, with your son Ahimaaz and Jonathan son of Abiathar. ²⁸ I will wait at the river crossings in the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.” ²⁹ So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there. ³⁰ But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went; his head was covered and he was walking barefoot. All the people with him covered their heads too and wept as they went up.

³¹ David was told that Ahithophel was among the conspirators with Absalom. He said, “LORD, turn Ahithophel's counsel into foolishness.” ³² When David arrived at the summit, where people used to worship God, Hushai the Archite was there to meet him, his robe torn and dust on his head. ³³ David said to him, “If you go with me, you will be a burden to me. ³⁴ But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'Your Majesty, I will be your servant; I was your father's servant in the past, but now I will be your servant,' then you can help me by frustrating Ahithophel's advice. ³⁵ Won't the priests Zadok and Abiathar be there with you? Tell them everything you hear in the king's palace.

³⁶ Their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with anything you hear.” ³⁷ So Hushai, David's trusted friend, went to Jerusalem, arriving just as Absalom was entering the city.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 16
paragraphs: ¹ When David had gone a short distance beyond the summit, Ziba, the steward of Mephibosheth (Jonathan's son), was waiting to meet him. He had a string of donkeys saddled and loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred cakes of raisins, a hundred cakes of figs, and a skin of wine. ² The king asked Ziba, “Why have you brought these?” Ziba answered, “The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on, the bread and fruit are for the men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.” ³ The king then asked, “Where is your master's grandson?” Ziba said to him, “He is staying in Jerusalem, because he thinks, 'Today the Israelites will restore to me my grandfather's kingdom.'” ⁴ Then the king said to Ziba, “All that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours.” “I humbly bow,” Ziba said. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king.”

⁶ He pelted David and all the king's officials with stones, though all the troops and the special guard were on David's right and left. ⁷ As he cursed, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you murderer, you scoundrel! ⁸ The LORD has repaid you for all the blood you shed in the household of Saul, in whose place you have reigned. The LORD has given the kingdom into the hands of your son Absalom. You have come to ruin because you are a murderer!” ⁹ Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head.” ¹⁰ But the king said, “What does this have to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? If he is cursing because the LORD said to him, 'Curse David,' who can ask, 'Why do you do this?'”

¹¹ David then said to Abishai and all his officials, “My own son is trying to kill me. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone; let him curse, for the LORD has told him to. ¹² Perhaps the LORD will see my distress and repay me with good for the cursing I am receiving today.” ¹³ So David and his men continued along the road while Shimei was going along the hillside opposite him, cursing as he went and throwing stones at him and showering him with dirt. ¹⁴ The king and all the people with him arrived at their destination exhausted. And there he refreshed himself. ¹⁵ Meanwhile, Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.

¹⁶ When Hushai the Archite (David's friend) came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, “Long live the king! Long live the king!” ¹⁷ Absalom said to Hushai, “So this is the love you show your friend? Why didn't you go with your friend?” ¹⁸ Hushai said to Absalom, “No, the one chosen by the LORD, by these people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and I will remain with him. ¹⁹ Furthermore, whom should I serve? Should I not serve the king's son? Just as I served your father, so I will serve you.”

²¹ Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Sleep with your father's concubines whom he left to take care of the palace. Then all Israel will hear that you have made yourself obnoxious to your father, and the hands of everyone with you will be more resolute.” ²² So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom slept with his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel. ²³ Now in those days the advice Ahithophel gave was like that of one who inquires of God. That was how both David and Absalom regarded all of Ahithophel's advice.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 17
paragraphs: ¹ Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David. ² I will attack him while he is weary and weak. I will strike him with terror, and then all the people with him will flee. I will strike down only the king ³ and bring all the people back to you. The death of the man you seek will mean the return of all; all the people will be unharmed.” ⁴ This plan seemed good to Absalom and to all the elders of Israel. ⁵ But Absalom said, “Summon Hushai the Archite also, so we can hear what he has to say.”

⁶ When Hushai came to Absalom, Absalom said, “Ahithophel has given this advice. Should we follow his advice? If not, give us your opinion.” ⁷ Hushai replied to Absalom, “The advice Ahithophel has given is not good this time. ⁸ You know your father and his men; they are fighters, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Besides, your father is an experienced soldier; he will not spend the night with the troops. ⁹ Even now, he is hidden in a cave or some other place. If he should attack your troops first, whoever hears about it will say, 'There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.' ¹⁰ Then even the bravest soldier, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will melt with fear, for all Israel knows that your father is a fighter and that those with him are brave.”

¹¹ So I advise you: Let all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba—as numerous as the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, with you yourself leading them into battle. ¹² Then we will attack him wherever he may be found, and we will fall on him as dew settles on the ground. Neither he nor any of his men will be left alive. ¹³ If he withdraws into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not so much as a pebble is left.” ¹⁴ Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had determined to frustrate the good advice of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.

¹⁵ Then Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar the priests, “Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel to do such and such, but I have advised them to do otherwise. ¹⁶ Now send a message at once and tell David, 'Do not spend the night at the river crossings in the wilderness; cross over without fail, or the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.'”

²¹ After they had gone, the two climbed out of the well and went to inform King David. They said, “Set out and cross the river at once; Ahithophel has advised such and such against you.” ²² So David and all the people with him set out and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, everyone had crossed. ²³ When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his house in order and then hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father's tomb. ²⁴ David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel. ²⁵ Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Jether, an Israelite who had married Abigail daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.

²⁶ So Israel and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead. ²⁷ When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, and Makir son of Ammiel from Lo Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim ²⁸ brought bedding, bowls, and articles of pottery. They also brought wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, ²⁹ honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from cows' milk for David and his people to eat. For they said, “The people have become hungry and tired and thirsty in the wilderness.”

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 18
paragraphs: ¹ David mustered the men who were with him and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds. ² David sent out his troops, a third under the command of Joab, a third under Joab's brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. The king told the troops, “I myself will surely march out with you.” ³ But the men said, “You must not go out; if we are forced to flee, they won't care about us. Even if half of us die, they won't care; but you are worth ten thousand of us. It would be better now for you to give us support from the city.” ⁴ The king answered, “I will do whatever seems best to you.” So the king stood beside the gate while all his men marched out in units of hundreds and of thousands. ⁵ The king commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “Be gentle with the young man Absalom for my sake.” And all the troops heard the king's command to each of the commanders about Absalom.

⁶ So the army went out into the field against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim. ⁷ There Israel’s troops were routed by David’s men, and the casualties that day were great—twenty thousand men. ⁸ The battle spread out over the whole countryside, and the forest swallowed up more men that day than the sword.

¹¹ Joab said to the man who had told him, "You saw him — why didn't you strike him down on the spot? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a belt." ¹² But the man replied, "Even if you had put a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, I would not have raised a hand against the king's son. We all heard the king order you and Abishai and Ittai, 'Protect the young man Absalom.' ¹³ If I had done it, I would have been risking my own life — nothing is hidden from the king, and you yourself would have turned against me." ¹⁴ Joab said, "I'm not going to waste time arguing with you." He took three spears in his hand and drove them into Absalom's chest while he was still alive, hanging in the oak tree. ¹⁵ Then ten of Joab's armor-bearers surrounded Absalom and finished him off.

¹⁶ Joab sounded the trumpet, and the troops stopped pursuing Israel, for Joab called them back. ¹⁷ They took Absalom, threw him into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge heap of stones over him. All Israel fled to their own homes. ¹⁸ During his lifetime, Absalom had set up a stone pillar for himself in the King's Valley, for he had said, "I have no son to carry on the memory of my name." He named the pillar after himself, and it is still called Absalom's Monument to this day. ¹⁹ Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and bring the news to the king that the LORD has vindicated him against his enemies." ²⁰ But Joab told him, "You're not the one to bring news today. You can bring news another time, but not today — the king's son is dead."

²¹ Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed to Joab and ran off. ²² But Ahimaaz son of Zadok pressed Joab again: "Whatever happens, please let me run after the Cushite." Joab said, "Why do you want to run, my son? You have no news that will bring you a reward." ²³ "No matter," he said, "let me run." So Joab said, "Run." Ahimaaz took the route through the plain and outran the Cushite. ²⁴ David was sitting between the inner and outer gates. The watchman had gone up to the roof of the gateway by the wall. He looked out and saw a man running alone. ²⁵ The watchman called down and told the king. The king said, "If he's alone, he must be bringing news." He kept coming, drawing nearer.

²⁶ The watchman saw another man running and called out to the gatekeeper, "Look — another man running alone!" The king said, "He's bringing news too." ²⁷ The watchman said, "The first man runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok." "He's a good man," said the king. "He comes with good news." ²⁸ Ahimaaz called out to the king, "All is well!" He bowed down before the king with his face to the ground and said, "Praise the LORD your God! He has delivered up the men who lifted their hands against my lord the king." ²⁹ "Is the young man Absalom safe?" the king asked. Ahimaaz answered, "I saw a great commotion just as Joab was sending the king's servant and me, your servant, but I didn't know what it was." ³⁰ The king said, "Step aside and wait here." So he stepped aside and stood there.

³¹ Then the Cushite arrived and said, "Good news, my lord the king! The LORD has vindicated you today against all who rose up against you." ³² The king asked the Cushite, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" The Cushite answered, "May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise against you to harm you end up like that young man." ³³ The king was shaken. He went up to the room over the gateway and wept. As he went, he cried out, "O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you — O Absalom, my son, my son!"

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 19
paragraphs: ¹ Joab was told that the king was weeping and mourning for Absalom. ² The victory that day was turned into grief for all the people, for they heard it said, "The king is mourning for his son." ³ The troops slipped into the city that day like men ashamed after fleeing in battle. ⁴ The king covered his face and cried loudly, "O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!" ⁵ Joab went into the palace to the king and said, "Today you have humiliated all your men — the ones who saved your life today, and the lives of your sons and daughters, and your wives and concubines.

⁶ You love those who hate you and hate those who love you. You have made it plain today that your officers and soldiers mean nothing to you — I can see that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, that would please you. ⁷ Now go out and speak encouragingly to your servants, because I swear by the LORD, if you don't go out, not one man will stay with you tonight. That would be a worse disaster for you than all the troubles that have come on you from your youth until now." ⁸ So the king got up and sat in the gateway. The word went out: "The king is sitting in the gateway." And all the people came before the king. Meanwhile, Israel had fled to their own homes. ⁹ Throughout all the tribes of Israel, the people were arguing, saying, "The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies; he delivered us from the Philistines. But now he has fled the country because of Absalom. ¹⁰ And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. So why are you saying nothing about bringing the king back?"

¹¹ King David sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests: "Say to the elders of Judah, 'Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his palace? The word of all Israel has reached the king where he is staying. ¹² You are my relatives, my own flesh and blood. Why should you be the last to bring back the king?' ¹³ And say to Amasa, 'Aren't you my own flesh and blood? May God deal with me, ever so severely, if you are not commander of my army from now on in place of Joab.'" ¹⁴ He won over the hearts of all the men of Judah as one man, so that they sent word to the king: "Come back, you and all your men." ¹⁵ Then the king returned and came as far as the Jordan. The men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and escort him across the Jordan.

¹⁶ Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David. ¹⁷ With him were a thousand men from Benjamin, and Ziba, the steward of Saul's household, along with his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed to the Jordan ahead of the king. ¹⁸ They crossed the ford to bring the king's household over and to do whatever he wished. When the king was about to cross the Jordan, Shimei son of Gera fell down before the king ¹⁹ and said, "May my lord not hold me guilty. Do not remember the wrong your servant did on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem — please put it out of your mind. ²⁰ For I your servant know that I have sinned, and here I am, the first from the whole house of Joseph to come down today to meet my lord the king."

²¹ But Abishai son of Zeruiah spoke up: "Shouldn't Shimei be put to death for this? He cursed the LORD's anointed." ²² David replied, "What does this have to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? Why should you be my adversaries today? Should anyone be put to death in Israel today? Don't I know that today I am king over Israel?" ²³ So the king said to Shimei, "You will not die." And the king gave him his oath. ²⁴ Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, also came down to meet the king. He had not taken care of his feet, trimmed his beard, or washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day he returned safely. ²⁵ When he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, the king asked him, "Why didn't you come with me, Mephibosheth?"

²⁶ He answered, "My lord the king, my servant Ziba deceived me. I said, 'I'll have my donkey saddled so I can ride along with the king' — because your servant is lame. ²⁷ He has slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of God, so do whatever seems right to you. ²⁸ All my grandfather's family deserved nothing but death from my lord the king, but you included your servant among those who eat at your own table. What further right do I have to appeal to the king?" ²⁹ The king said to him, "Why say more? I have already decided: you and Ziba will divide the land." ³⁰ Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take it all, since my lord the king has come home safely."

³¹ Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and accompanied the king to the Jordan to see him on his way. ³² Now Barzillai was eighty years old and a very wealthy man. He had supplied the king during his stay at Mahanaim. ³³ The king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me and I will provide for you in Jerusalem." ³⁴ But Barzillai answered, "How many years do I have left, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem? ³⁵ I'm already eighty years old. Can I even tell the difference between good and bad? Can I taste what I eat or drink? Can I still hear the voices of men and women singers? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?

³⁶ Your servant will cross the Jordan with the king for a short way, but why should the king reward me with such a great honor? ³⁷ Let your servant return so that I can die in my own city, near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham — let him cross over with my lord the king. Do for him whatever seems right to you." ³⁸ The king answered, "Chimham will cross over with me, and I will do for him whatever you wish. And whatever you ask of me, I will do for you." ³⁹ So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and gave him his blessing, and Barzillai returned home. ⁴⁰ The king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham came with him. All the people of Judah and half the people of Israel had escorted the king.

⁴¹ Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and said, "Why did our brothers from Judah steal the king away and bring him and his household across the Jordan, along with all his men?" ⁴² All the men of Judah replied to the men of Israel, "Because the king is our close relative. Why are you angry about it? Have we eaten anything at the king's expense? Have we taken anything for ourselves?" ⁴³ The men of Israel answered Judah: "We have ten shares in the king! We have a greater claim on David than you do. Why do you treat us with contempt? Were we not the first to speak of bringing back our king?" But the men of Judah spoke even more harshly than the men of Israel.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 20
paragraphs: ¹ Now a troublemaker happened to be there, a man named Sheba son of Bicri, a Benjaminite. He blew a trumpet and shouted, "We have no share in David, no part in Jesse's son! Every man to his tent, Israel!" ² So all the men of Israel deserted David and followed Sheba son of Bicri. But the men of Judah stayed loyal to their king, all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. ³ When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to take care of the palace and put them under guard. He provided for them but had no relations with them. They were kept in seclusion until the day they died, living as if in widowhood. ⁴ The king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah for me within three days, and be here yourself." ⁵ So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time the king had set.

⁶ David said to Abishai, "Sheba son of Bicri will do us more harm now than Absalom ever did. Take your lord's men and pursue him, or he'll find fortified cities and slip away from us." ⁷ So Joab's men, the Cherethites and Pelethites, and all the mighty warriors marched out of Jerusalem after Sheba son of Bicri. ⁸ When they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was wearing his battle dress, and he had a dagger strapped to his belt at his hip. As he stepped forward, it slipped out. ⁹ Joab said to Amasa, "How are you, my brother?" And Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him. ¹⁰ Amasa was not watching the dagger in Joab's other hand, and Joab drove it into his belly, spilling out his intestines on the ground. He did not need to stab him again, and Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai continued in pursuit of Sheba son of Bicri.

¹¹ One of Joab's men stood over Amasa and called out, "Anyone who favors Joab and is for David, follow Joab!" ¹² Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road. The man saw that everyone was stopping there, so he dragged Amasa off the road into a field and threw a garment over him, since anyone who came by stopped to look. ¹³ Once Amasa was moved from the road, all the men followed Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bicri. ¹⁴ Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel Beth Maakah, and all the Bicrites gathered together and followed him. ¹⁵ All Joab's troops came and besieged Sheba at Abel Beth Maakah. They built a siege ramp against the city, and it stood against the outer wall while all Joab's troops battered the wall to bring it down.

¹⁶ Then a wise woman called from the city, "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come here so I can speak to him." ¹⁷ When he came near, the woman asked, "Are you Joab?" "I am," he answered. "Then listen to what your servant has to say," she said. "I'm listening," he replied. ¹⁸ She continued, "Long ago people used to say, 'Get your answer at Abel,' and that settled matters. ¹⁹ I am one of the peaceable and faithful in Israel. You are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you want to swallow up the LORD's inheritance?" ²⁰ Joab replied, "Far be it from me, far be it indeed, to swallow up or destroy!

²¹ That is not my aim. There is a man named Sheba son of Bicri, from the hill country of Ephraim, who has raised his hand against King David. Hand him over alone, and I'll withdraw from the city." "His head will be thrown to you over the wall," the woman replied. ²² Then the woman went to all the people with her wise counsel, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bicri and threw it to Joab. He sounded the trumpet, and his troops withdrew from the city, each to his home. And Joab returned to the king at Jerusalem. ²³ Now Joab was in command of all Israel's army; Benaiah son of Jehoiada commanded the Cherethites and Pelethites; ²⁴ Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the historian; ²⁵ Sheva was the secretary; Zadok and Abiathar were the priests;
²⁶ And Ira the Jairite was also David's personal priest.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 21
paragraphs: ¹ During David's reign there was a famine for three consecutive years. David inquired of the LORD, and the LORD said, "It is on account of Saul and his blood-stained house; he put the Gibeonites to death." ² The king called the Gibeonites and spoke with them. (Now the Gibeonites were not Israelites but survivors of the Amorites; the Israelites had sworn an oath to spare them, but Saul in his zeal for Israel and Judah had tried to annihilate them.) ³ David asked them, "What can I do for you? How can I make atonement so that you will bless the LORD's inheritance?" ⁴ The Gibeonites said, "We want no silver or gold from Saul or his family, nor do we want anyone in Israel put to death." "What do you want then?" David asked. ⁵ They answered the king, "The man who devastated us and schemed against us so that we would be destroyed from all Israel —

⁶ hand over seven of his male descendants, and we will execute them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the LORD's chosen one." The king said, "I will hand them over." ⁷ The king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan (who was Saul's son) because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul. ⁸ But the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul, along with the five sons of Merab daughter of Saul, whom she had raised for Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite. ⁹ He handed them over to the Gibeonites, who executed them on the hill before the LORD. All seven fell together; they were put to death during the first days of harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest. ¹⁰ Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out on a rock. From the beginning of harvest until rain fell from the sky she kept the birds away from the bodies by day and the wild animals away by night.

¹¹ When David was told what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul's concubine, had done, ¹² he went and retrieved the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the people of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the public square at Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hung them on the day they struck down Saul at Gilboa. ¹³ David brought up from there the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan, and the bones of those who had been executed were gathered as well. ¹⁴ They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in the tomb of Saul's father Kish, at Zela in Benjamin, and did everything the king commanded. After that, God answered prayer on behalf of the land. ¹⁵ Once more the Philistines went to war against Israel. David went down with his men and fought the Philistines, but David grew exhausted.

¹⁶ Ishbi-Benob, one of the descendants of Rapha, whose bronze spearhead weighed three hundred shekels and who carried a new sword, said he would kill David. ¹⁷ But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to David's rescue, struck the Philistine down, and killed him. Then David's men swore to him: "Never again will you go out with us into battle, so that the lamp of Israel will not be extinguished." ¹⁸ In the course of time, there was another battle with the Philistines at Gob. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, one of the descendants of Rapha. ¹⁹ In another battle with the Philistines at Gob, Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's rod. ²⁰ In still another battle at Gath, there was a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot — twenty-four in all. He too was descended from Rapha.
²¹ When he taunted Israel, Jonathan son of Shimeah, David's brother, killed him. ²² These four were descendants of Rapha in Gath, and they all fell by the hand of David and his soldiers.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 22
paragraphs: ¹ David sang this song to the LORD on the day the LORD rescued him from the hand of all his enemies, including Saul. ² He said: "The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer; ³ my God is my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold and my refuge, my savior — you save me from violence. ⁴ I call to the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies. ⁵ When the waves of death swirled around me, the torrents of destruction overwhelmed me;

⁶ the ropes of the grave coiled around me; the snares of death confronted me. ⁷ In my distress I called to the LORD; I cried out to my God. From his temple he heard my voice; my cry reached his ears. ⁸ The earth trembled and shook; the foundations of the heavens rocked, because he was angry. ⁹ Smoke rose from his nostrils; consuming fire came from his mouth, burning coals blazed out of it. ¹⁰ He parted the heavens and came down; dark clouds were under his feet.

¹¹ He mounted the cherubim and flew; he soared on the wings of the wind. ¹² He made darkness his canopy around him — the dark rain clouds of the sky. ¹³ Out of the brightness of his presence bolts of lightning blazed forth. ¹⁴ The LORD thundered from heaven; the Most High raised his voice. ¹⁵ He shot his arrows and scattered the enemy; great bolts of lightning, and they were routed.

¹⁶ The valleys of the sea were exposed, and the foundations of the earth laid bare, at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of breath from his nostrils. ¹⁷ He reached down from on high and took hold of me; he drew me out of deep waters. ¹⁸ He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from my foes who were too strong for me. ¹⁹ They confronted me in the day of my disaster, but the LORD was my support. ²⁰ He brought me out into a spacious place; he rescued me because he delighted in me.

²¹ The LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he has repaid me. ²² For I have kept the ways of the LORD; I have not turned from my God to do evil. ²³ All his laws are before me; I have not turned away from his decrees. ²⁴ I have been blameless before him and have kept myself from sin. ²⁵ The LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in his sight.

²⁶ To the faithful you show yourself faithful; to the blameless you show yourself blameless; ²⁷ to the pure you show yourself pure, but to the devious you show yourself shrewd. ²⁸ You save the humble, but your eyes are on the proud to bring them low. ²⁹ You, LORD, are my lamp; the LORD turns my darkness into light. ³⁰ With your help I can advance against a troop; with my God I can scale a wall.

³¹ As for God, his way is perfect; the LORD's word is flawless. He shields all who take refuge in him. ³² For who is God besides the LORD? And who is the Rock except our God? ³³ It is God who arms me with strength and keeps my way secure. ³⁴ He makes my feet like the feet of a deer; he causes me to stand on the heights. ³⁵ He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.

³⁶ You have given me the shield of your salvation; your help has made me great. ³⁷ You provide a wide path for my feet so that my ankles do not give way. ³⁸ I pursued my enemies and crushed them; I did not turn back till they were destroyed. ³⁹ I crushed them completely, and they could not rise; they fell beneath my feet. ⁴⁰ You armed me with strength for battle; you humbled my adversaries before me.

⁴¹ You made my enemies turn their backs in flight, and I destroyed my foes. ⁴² They cried for help, but there was no one to save them — to the LORD, but he did not answer them. ⁴³ I beat them as fine as the dust of the earth; I pounded and trampled them like mud in the streets and spread them out. ⁴⁴ You have delivered me from the attacks of the peoples; you have preserved me as the head of nations. People I did not know now serve me. ⁴⁵ Foreigners come cringing to me; as soon as they hear of me, they obey me.

⁴⁶ They all lose heart; they come trembling from their strongholds. ⁴⁷ The LORD lives! Praise be to my Rock! Exalted be my God, the Rock, my Savior! ⁴⁸ He is the God who avenges me, who subdues nations under me, ⁴⁹ who sets me free from my enemies. You exalted me above my foes; from a violent man you rescued me. ⁵⁰ Therefore I will praise you, LORD, among the nations; I will sing the praises of your name.
⁵¹ He gives his king great victories; he shows unfailing love to his anointed, to David and his descendants forever.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 23
paragraphs: ¹ These are the last words of David. The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man exalted by the Most High, the man anointed by the God of Jacob, Israel's beloved singer of songs: ² "The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; his word was on my tongue. ³ The God of Israel spoke, the Rock of Israel said to me: 'When one rules over people in righteousness, when he rules in the fear of God, ⁴ he is like the light of morning at sunrise on a cloudless morning, like the brightness after rain that brings grass from the earth.' ⁵ Although my house is not right with God in this way, yet he has made with me an everlasting covenant, arranged and secured in every part. Surely he will bring to fruition my salvation and grant me my every desire.

⁶ But evil men are all to be cast aside like thorns, which cannot be taken by hand. ⁷ Whoever touches them uses a tool of iron or the shaft of a spear; they are burned up where they lie." ⁸ These are the names of David's mighty warriors: Josheb-Basshebeth, a Tahkemonite, was chief of the Three; he raised his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed in one encounter. ⁹ Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodai the Ahohite. As one of the three mighty warriors, he was with David when they taunted the Philistines gathered there for battle. Then the Israelites retreated, ¹⁰ but Eleazar stood his ground and struck down the Philistines till his hand grew tired and froze to the sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day. The troops returned to Eleazar, but only to strip the dead.

¹¹ Next was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. When the Philistines banded together at a place where there was a field full of lentils, Israel's troops fled from them. ¹² But Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field. He defended it and struck the Philistines down, and the LORD brought about a great victory. ¹³ During harvest time, three of the thirty chief warriors came down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a band of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim. ¹⁴ At that time David was in the stronghold, and the Philistine garrison was at Bethlehem. ¹⁵ David longed for water and said, "Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!"

¹⁶ So the three mighty warriors broke through the Philistine lines, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem, and carried it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out before the LORD. ¹⁷ "Far be it from me, LORD, to do this!" he said. "Is it not the blood of men who risked their lives?" So he would not drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty warriors. ¹⁸ Abishai the brother of Joab son of Zeruiah was chief of the Three. He raised his spear against three hundred men, whom he killed, and he became as famous as the Three. ¹⁹ Was he not held in greater honor than the Three? He became their commander, even though he was not included among them. ²⁰ Benaiah son of Jehoiada, a valiant fighter from Kabzeel, performed great exploits. He struck down Moab's two mightiest warriors. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

²¹ And he struck down a huge Egyptian. Although the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, Benaiah went against him with only a staff. He snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear. ²² Such were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada; he too became as famous as the three mighty warriors. ²³ He was held in greater honor than any of the Thirty, but he was not included among the Three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard. ²⁴ Among the Thirty were: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem, ²⁵ Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,

²⁶ Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa, ²⁷ Abiezer from Anathoth, Sibbekai the Hushathite, ²⁸ Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite, ²⁹ Heleb son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin, ³⁰ Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the ravines of Gaash,

³¹ Abi-Albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite, ³² Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan, ³³ Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite, ³⁴ Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maakathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite, ³⁵ Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,

³⁶ Igal son of Nathan from Zobah, Bani the Gadite, ³⁷ Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah, ³⁸ Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite, ³⁹ and Uriah the Hittite. Thirty-seven in all.

chapters.title: 2 Samuel 24
paragraphs: ¹ Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, "Go and count Israel and Judah." ² So the king said to Joab and the army commanders with him, "Go throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and enroll the fighting men, so that I may know how many there are." ³ But Joab replied to the king, "May the LORD your God multiply the troops a hundred times over, and may your own eyes see it. But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?" ⁴ The king's word overruled Joab and the army commanders, so they left the king's presence to enroll the fighting men of Israel. ⁵ After crossing the Jordan, they camped near Aroer, south of the town in the gorge, and then went through Gad and on to Jazer.

⁶ They went on to Gilead and to the region of Tahtim Hodshi, and on to Dan Jaan and around toward Sidon. ⁷ Then they went toward the fortress of Tyre and all the towns of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally, they went on to Beersheba in the Negev of Judah. ⁸ After going through the entire land, they came back to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days. ⁹ Joab reported the number of the fighting men to the king: In Israel there were eight hundred thousand able-bodied men who could handle a sword, and in Judah five hundred thousand. ¹⁰ David was conscience-stricken after he had counted the fighting men, and he said to the LORD, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, LORD, I beg you, take away the guilt of your servant. I have done a very foolish thing."

¹¹ Before David got up the next morning, the word of the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David's seer: ¹² "Go and tell David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am giving you three options. Choose one of them for me to carry out against you.'" ¹³ So Gad went to David and said, "Shall there come on you three years of famine in your land? Or three months of fleeing from your enemies while they pursue you? Or three days of plague in your land? Now think it over and decide how I should answer the one who sent me." ¹⁴ David said to Gad, "I am in deep distress. Let us fall into the hands of the LORD, for his mercy is great; but do not let me fall into human hands." ¹⁵ So the LORD sent a plague on Israel from that morning until the end of the time designated, and seventy thousand people from Dan to Beersheba died.

¹⁶ When the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented concerning the disaster and said to the angel who was afflicting the people, "Enough! Withdraw your hand." The angel of the LORD was then at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite. ¹⁷ When David saw the angel who was striking down the people, he said to the LORD, "I have sinned; I, the shepherd, have done wrong. These are but sheep. What have they done? Let your hand fall on me and my family." ¹⁸ On that day Gad went to David and said, "Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite." ¹⁹ So David went up, as the LORD had commanded through Gad. ²⁰ When Araunah looked and saw the king and his officials coming toward him, he went out and bowed down before the king with his face to the ground.

²¹ Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" "To buy your threshing floor," David answered, "so I can build an altar to the LORD, and the plague on the people may be stopped." ²² Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take whatever he wishes and offer it up. Here are oxen for the burnt offering, and here are threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood. ²³ Your Majesty, Araunah gives all this to the king." Araunah also said to him, "May the LORD your God accept you." ²⁴ But the king replied, "No, I insist on buying it from you at a price. I will not sacrifice to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen and paid fifty shekels of silver for them. ²⁵ David built an altar to the LORD there and sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. Then the LORD answered his prayer on behalf of the land, and the plague on Israel was stopped.

chapters.title: 1 Kings 1
paragraphs: ¹ King David was old and advanced in years. His servants wrapped him in blankets, but he could not get warm. ² So his servants said to him, "Let us find a young virgin for my lord the king. She can attend him and care for him, and sleep beside him so that my lord the king may stay warm." ³ They searched throughout all Israel for a beautiful young woman and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king. ⁴ The young woman was very beautiful. She cared for the king and attended to his needs, but the king did not sleep with her. ⁵ Meanwhile Adonijah, the son of Haggith, began promoting himself, saying, "I will be king." He acquired chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.

⁶ His father had never once corrected him, never said, "Why do you behave this way?" Adonijah was also very handsome, and his mother had given birth to him after Absalom. ⁷ He conspired with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they supported his claim. ⁸ But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's elite warriors did not side with Adonijah. ⁹ Adonijah held a great sacrifice of sheep, oxen, and fattened cattle at the Stone of Zoheleth, near En Rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah who served the king. ¹⁰ But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the king's elite warriors, or his brother Solomon.

¹¹ Nathan went to Bathsheba, the mother of Solomon, and asked, "Have you not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has made himself king, and our lord David doesn't even know it? ¹² Let me give you advice so that you can save your own life and the life of your son Solomon. ¹³ Go in to King David and say to him, 'Didn't you, my lord the king, swear to me your servant that my son Solomon would reign after you and sit on your throne? Why then is Adonijah king?' ¹⁴ While you are still speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm what you have said." ¹⁵ Bathsheba went to the king in his room. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was caring for him.

¹⁶ Bathsheba bowed down and knelt before the king. "What do you want?" the king asked. ¹⁷ She said to him, "My lord, you swore to me your servant by the LORD your God: 'Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.' ¹⁸ But now, without your knowledge, Adonijah has become king. ¹⁹ He has sacrificed oxen, fattened cattle, and sheep in great numbers. He has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army — but he has not invited Solomon your servant. ²⁰ And now, my lord the king, all Israel is looking to you to tell them who will sit on the throne after you.

²¹ Otherwise, when you, my lord the king, die and lie with your ancestors, my son Solomon and I will be treated as criminals." ²² While she was still speaking with the king, the prophet Nathan arrived. ²³ They told the king, "Nathan the prophet is here." He came in before the king and bowed with his face to the ground. ²⁴ "My lord the king," Nathan said, "have you declared that Adonijah shall reign after you and sit on your throne? ²⁵ For he has gone down today and sacrificed vast numbers of oxen, fattened cattle, and sheep. He has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest — and right now they are eating and drinking with him and shouting, 'Long live King Adonijah!'

²⁶ But me, your servant — he has not invited me, nor Zadok the priest, nor Benaiah son of Jehoiada, nor your servant Solomon. ²⁷ Has this been done by my lord the king without telling your servants who should sit on the throne after you?" ²⁸ King David then said, "Call Bathsheba to me." She came before the king and stood in his presence. ²⁹ The king swore an oath: "As the LORD lives — who has delivered me from every trouble — ³⁰ I will do this very day what I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel: Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place."

³¹ Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and knelt before the king. "May my lord King David live forever!" she said. ³² King David then said, "Summon Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." They came before the king, ³³ and the king said to them, "Take your lord's servants with you, put my son Solomon on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon. ³⁴ There let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel. Sound the trumpet and shout, 'Long live King Solomon!' ³⁵ Then come back up with him, and he will sit on my throne and reign in my place. I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah."

³⁶ Benaiah son of Jehoiada replied to the king, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, declare it so. ³⁷ As the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he make Solomon's throne even greater than the throne of my lord King David." ³⁸ Then Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and Pelethites set out. They put Solomon on King David's own mule and brought him to Gihon. ³⁹ Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. Then they sounded the trumpet, and all the people shouted, "Long live King Solomon!" ⁴⁰ All the people came up behind him, playing flutes and celebrating with great joy. The noise was so great that the ground shook with the sound.

⁴¹ Adonijah and all his guests heard it just as they were finishing their meal. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, "What is all that noise in the city?" ⁴² Even as he was speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. "Come in," said Adonijah, "for you are a man of good standing and you bring good news." ⁴³ But Jonathan replied, "No — our lord King David has made Solomon king. ⁴⁴ The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites. They put him on the king's mule, ⁴⁵ and Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon. They have come back up rejoicing, and the whole city is in an uproar. That is the noise you heard.

⁴⁶ Solomon has now taken his seat on the royal throne. ⁴⁷ Moreover, the king's servants have come to bless our lord King David, saying, 'May God make Solomon's name even greater than yours, and may his throne be greater than your throne.' And the king bowed in worship on his bed. ⁴⁸ The king also said, 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has today given someone to sit on my throne while I can still see it with my own eyes.'" ⁴⁹ At that, all Adonijah's guests got up in terror and scattered. ⁵⁰ Adonijah himself was terrified of Solomon. He went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

⁵¹ Word reached Solomon: "Adonijah is afraid of you. He has taken hold of the horns of the altar and says, 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not kill his servant with the sword.'" ⁵² Solomon replied, "If he proves himself a man of character, not one hair of his head will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die." ⁵³ So King Solomon sent for Adonijah, and they brought him down from the altar. He came and bowed down before King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, "Go home."

chapters.title: 1 Kings 2
paragraphs: ¹ As the time drew near for David to die, he gave these instructions to his son Solomon: ² "I am about to go the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man. ³ Keep the charge of the LORD your God, walking in his ways and keeping his statutes, his commandments, his rules, and his testimonies, as written in the law of Moses. Then you will succeed in everything you do and wherever you turn — ⁴ so that the LORD may fulfill his promise to me: 'If your sons take care how they walk before me in faithfulness with all their heart and soul, you shall never lack a man on the throne of Israel.' ⁵ You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me — what he did to the two commanders of Israel's armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them both, shedding the blood of war in peacetime, staining his belt and his sandals with the blood of men he murdered.

⁶ Act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to the grave in peace. ⁷ But deal loyally with the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite and let them be among those who eat at your table, because they came to help me when I was fleeing from your brother Absalom. ⁸ You also have with you Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me with a bitter curse the day I went to Mahanaim, but then he came down to meet me at the Jordan and I swore to him by the LORD that I would not kill him with the sword. ⁹ Do not let him go unpunished. You are a wise man and you know what to do — bring his gray head down to the grave with blood." ¹⁰ Then David rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David.

¹¹ David had reigned over Israel for forty years — seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem. ¹² Solomon then sat on the throne of his father David, and his rule was firmly established. ¹³ Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, the mother of Solomon. "Do you come in peace?" she asked. "Yes, in peace," he said. ¹⁴ "I have something to say to you." "Go ahead," she said. ¹⁵ He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel expected me to be king. But things turned around, and the kingdom went to my brother instead — because it was the LORD's doing.

¹⁶ Now I have one request to make of you — don't refuse me." "What is it?" she asked. ¹⁷ He said, "Please speak to King Solomon — he won't refuse you — and ask him to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife." ¹⁸ "Very well," Bathsheba said, "I will speak to the king for you." ¹⁹ So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak on Adonijah's behalf. The king rose to meet her and bowed to her. Then he sat back down on his throne and had a throne set for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand. ²⁰ "I have one small request to make of you," she said. "Don't refuse me." "Ask, my mother," the king replied, "for I will not refuse you."

²¹ She said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife." ²² King Solomon answered his mother, "Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? You might as well ask for the kingdom for him — he is my older brother, and Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah are on his side." ²³ Then King Solomon swore by the LORD: "May God deal with me severely if Adonijah does not pay with his life for this request. ²⁴ Now, as the LORD lives — who has established me and placed me on the throne of my father David and built a dynasty for me just as he promised — Adonijah will be put to death today." ²⁵ King Solomon gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who struck Adonijah down, and he died.

²⁶ To Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to your estate in Anathoth. You deserve to die, but I will not put you to death now, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and you shared in all the hardships my father endured." ²⁷ So Solomon dismissed Abiathar from serving as priest to the LORD, fulfilling the word the LORD had spoken at Shiloh concerning the house of Eli. ²⁸ When Joab heard this — Joab had sided with Adonijah, though not with Absalom — he fled to the tent of the LORD and grabbed hold of the horns of the altar. ²⁹ King Solomon was told that Joab had fled to the tent of the LORD and was beside the altar. So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada with orders to strike him down. ³⁰ Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to Joab, "The king says to come out." But Joab replied, "No — I will die here." Benaiah reported this back to the king.

³¹ The king said to Benaiah, "Do what he says. Strike him down and bury him. Take away from me and from my father's house the guilt of the blood Joab shed without cause. ³² The LORD will repay him for the blood he shed — he killed two men who were more righteous and better than he, cutting them down with the sword when my father David knew nothing of it: Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah's army. ³³ Their blood will rest on Joab's head and on his descendants' heads forever. But on David, and on his descendants, his house and his throne, may there be peace from the LORD forever." ³⁴ Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and struck Joab down and killed him, and he was buried at his own property in the wilderness. ³⁵ The king then appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada as commander of the army in Joab's place, and put Zadok the priest in place of Abiathar.

³⁶ The king also summoned Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there. Do not go anywhere else. ³⁷ The day you leave and cross the Kidron Valley, you can be certain you will die. Your blood will be on your own head." ³⁸ "What my lord the king says is fair," Shimei replied. "Your servant will do what you say." And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time. ³⁹ But three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to Achish son of Maacah, the king of Gath. Shimei was told, "Your servants are in Gath." ⁴⁰ So Shimei saddled his donkey and went to Gath to Achish in search of his servants. He went and brought them back from Gath.

⁴¹ Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and returned. ⁴² The king summoned Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you clearly: 'On the day you leave and go anywhere, you can be certain you will die'? And you said to me, 'What you say is fair, and I accept it.' ⁴³ Why then did you not keep the oath you swore to the LORD and the command I gave you?" ⁴⁴ The king also said to Shimei, "You know in your own heart all the wrong you did to my father David. The LORD will now repay you for it. ⁴⁵ But King Solomon will be blessed, and David's throne will remain established before the LORD forever."
⁴⁶ The king gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who went out and struck Shimei down. He died. The kingdom was now firmly in Solomon's hands.

chapters.title: 1 Kings 3
paragraphs: ¹ Solomon made an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt by marrying his daughter. He brought her to the City of David while he was still finishing his palace, the temple of the LORD, and the wall around Jerusalem. ² The people, however, were still sacrificing at the high places, because no temple had yet been built for the name of the LORD. ³ Solomon showed his love for the LORD by living according to the statutes of his father David, except that he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places. ⁴ The king went to Gibeon to offer sacrifices, for that was the most important high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar. ⁵ At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream at night and said, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you."

⁶ Solomon said, "You showed great faithfulness to your servant David my father, because he walked before you in truth, in righteousness, and with an undivided heart. And you have continued to show him this great kindness by giving him a son to sit on his throne today. ⁷ Now, LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of my father David, yet I am just a young man and don't know how to carry out my duties. ⁸ Your servant is among your chosen people, a great people too numerous to count or number. ⁹ Give your servant a discerning heart to govern your people and to distinguish between right and wrong — for who is able to govern this great people of yours?" ¹⁰ It pleased the LORD that Solomon had asked for this.

¹¹ God said to him, "Since you have asked for this — since you have not asked for long life or wealth for yourself, or for the death of your enemies, but have asked for discernment in administering justice — ¹² I will do what you have asked. I am giving you a wise and discerning heart, so that there has never been anyone like you before, and there never will be after you. ¹³ Moreover, I am giving you what you did not ask for — both riches and honor — so that in your lifetime no other king will compare with you. ¹⁴ And if you walk in my ways and obey my statutes and commands as your father David did, I will give you a long life." ¹⁵ Then Solomon woke up and realized it had been a dream. He returned to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then he gave a feast for all his servants.

¹⁶ Now two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him. ¹⁷ One of them said, "Pardon me, my lord. This woman and I live in the same house, and I had a baby while she was there with me. ¹⁸ The third day after my child was born, she gave birth too. We were alone in the house — just the two of us, no one else. ¹⁹ During the night this woman's son died because she rolled over on him. ²⁰ She got up in the middle of the night and took my son from my side while I was sleeping. She put him at her breast and put her dead son next to me.

²¹ When I got up in the morning to nurse my son, he was dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning light, I could see he was not the son I had given birth to." ²² The other woman said, "No! The living child is mine, and the dead one is yours." The first retorted, "No, the dead one is yours and the living one is mine." They argued back and forth before the king. ²³ The king said, "One of you claims, 'My son is alive and your son is dead,' while the other claims, 'No, your son is dead and mine is alive.'" ²⁴ He then said, "Bring me a sword." A sword was brought to him. ²⁵ "Cut the living child in two," the king ordered, "and give half to one woman and half to the other."

²⁶ At this, the woman whose son was alive was overcome with grief for her child and cried out to the king, "Please, my lord, give her the living baby! Don't kill him!" But the other said, "Neither of us will have him — go ahead and cut him in two." ²⁷ Then the king gave his ruling: "Give the living baby to the first woman. Don't kill him. She is his mother." ²⁸ When all Israel heard the verdict the king had given, they held the king in great awe. They saw that he had wisdom from God to administer justice.

chapters.title: 1 Kings 4
paragraphs: ¹ King Solomon ruled over all Israel. ² These were his chief officials: Azariah son of Zadok — the priest; ³ Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha — secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud — recorder; ⁴ Benaiah son of Jehoiada — commander of the army; Zadok and Abiathar — priests; ⁵ Azariah son of Nathan — in charge of the district governors; Zabud son of Nathan — a priest and personal adviser to the king;

⁶ Ahishar — palace administrator; Adoniram son of Abda — in charge of forced labor. ⁷ Solomon also had twelve district governors over all Israel who supplied provisions for the king and the royal household. Each man was responsible for one month of the year. ⁸ These were their names: Ben-Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim; ⁹ Ben-Deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Bethhanan; ¹⁰ Ben-Hesed, in Aruboth — he had Socoh and all the land of Hepher;

¹¹ Ben-Abinadab, in the whole region of Dor — he was married to Taphath, Solomon's daughter; ¹² Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, and in all of Beth Shean beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth Shean to Abel Meholah as far as Jokmeam; ¹³ Ben-Geber, in Ramoth Gilead — he had the settlements of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead, and the region of Argob in Bashan, sixty large walled cities with bronze gate bars; ¹⁴ Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim; ¹⁵ Ahimaaz, in Naphtali — he too had married a daughter of Solomon, Basemath;

¹⁶ Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Aloth; ¹⁷ Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar; ¹⁸ Shimei son of Elah, in Benjamin; ¹⁹ Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead — the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and the country of Og king of Bashan — and he was the only governor over the district. ²⁰ The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They ate and drank and were happy.

²¹ Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. These kingdoms paid tribute and were subject to Solomon all his life. ²² Solomon's daily provisions were thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal, ²³ ten head of stall-fed cattle, twenty head of pasture-fed cattle, and a hundred sheep and goats — plus deer, gazelles, roebucks, and choice poultry. ²⁴ For he ruled over all the region west of the Euphrates, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings west of the river. He had peace on all sides. ²⁵ Throughout Solomon's lifetime, Judah and Israel lived in safety, everyone under their own vine and fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba.

²⁶ Solomon had four thousand stalls for chariot horses and twelve thousand horsemen. ²⁷ These district governors supplied provisions for King Solomon and for all who came to the king's table, each in his assigned month. They made sure nothing was lacking. ²⁸ They also brought the required amounts of barley and straw for the horses and other animals to the places where they were stationed, each doing his part. ²⁹ God gave Solomon wisdom and very great insight, and a breadth of understanding as measureless as the sand on the seashore. ³⁰ Solomon's wisdom surpassed that of all the people of the East and all the wisdom of Egypt.

³¹ He was wiser than anyone — wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and than Heman, Kalkol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. His fame spread to all the surrounding nations. ³² He composed three thousand proverbs and his songs numbered a thousand and five. ³³ He spoke about plant life, from the cedar of Lebanon to the hyssop growing out of walls. He also spoke about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish. ³⁴ People came from all nations to listen to Solomon's wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.

chapters.title: 1 Kings 5
paragraphs: ¹ When Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king in place of his father David, he sent his envoys to Solomon, because Hiram had always been on friendly terms with David. ² Solomon sent back this message to Hiram: ³ "You know that my father David was unable to build a temple for the name of the LORD his God because of the wars waged against him on all sides, until the LORD put his enemies under his feet. ⁴ But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side, with no adversary and no misfortune. ⁵ I intend to build a temple for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD told my father David when he said: 'Your son, whom I will put on your throne in your place, will build the temple for my name.'"

⁶ "So now give orders to have cedar logs cut for me from Lebanon. My workers will work alongside yours, and I will pay your workers whatever rate you set. As you know, we have no one as skilled in felling timber as the Sidonians." ⁷ When Hiram heard Solomon's message, he was very pleased, and said, "Praise the LORD today, for he has given David a wise son to rule over this great nation." ⁸ So Hiram sent Solomon this reply: "I have received your message. I will do everything you want — I will supply you with all the cedar and pine logs you need. ⁹ My men will haul them down from Lebanon to the Mediterranean Sea, and I will float them as rafts to whatever place you specify. There I will have them separated, and you can take them. In return, I ask that you provide food for my household." ¹⁰ So Hiram kept Solomon supplied with as much cedar and pine as he desired.

¹¹ Solomon in turn gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of pure olive oil. Solomon gave Hiram this amount year by year. ¹² The LORD gave Solomon wisdom, just as he had promised, and there was peaceful relations between Hiram and Solomon, and they made a treaty. ¹³ King Solomon conscripted laborers from all Israel — thirty thousand men in all. ¹⁴ He sent them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month — one month in Lebanon, two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor. ¹⁵ Solomon had seventy thousand men who carried loads and eighty thousand who quarried stone in the hills,

¹⁶ besides three thousand three hundred foremen who supervised the workers. ¹⁷ At the king's command they quarried large blocks of high-quality stone to give the temple a foundation of dressed stone. ¹⁸ The craftsmen of Solomon and Hiram, along with the men of Gebal, cut and prepared the timber and stone for the building of the temple.

chapters.title: 1 Kings 6
paragraphs: ¹ In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt — in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, the second month — he began to build the temple of the LORD. ² The temple King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high. ³ The portico at the front of the main hall was twenty cubits wide, matching the width of the temple, and extended ten cubits out from the front. ⁴ He made narrow clerestory windows in the temple. ⁵ Against the walls of the main hall and the inner sanctuary he built a structure around the temple, in which there were side rooms:

⁶ The lowest floor of the side rooms was five cubits wide, the middle floor was six cubits wide, and the third floor was seven cubits wide. The temple had a ledge built around the outside so that the beams of the side rooms would not be set into the walls. ⁷ In building the temple, only blocks dressed at the quarry were used, and no hammer, chisel, or any other iron tool was heard at the temple site while it was being built. ⁸ The entrance to the lowest floor was on the south side of the temple. A stairway led up to the middle level and then to the third. ⁹ So he built the temple and completed it, roofing it with beams and cedar planks. ¹⁰ He built the side rooms all along the temple — each room five cubits high, attached to the temple by cedar beams.

¹¹ The word of the LORD came to Solomon: ¹² "As for this temple you are building — if you follow my decrees, observe my laws, and keep all my commands and obey them, I will fulfill through you the promise I gave to your father David. ¹³ I will live among the Israelites and will not abandon my people Israel." ¹⁴ So Solomon built the temple and completed it. ¹⁵ He lined the interior walls of the temple with cedar boards, paneling them from the floor to the ceiling. He covered the floor with planks of pine.

¹⁶ He partitioned off twenty cubits at the rear of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling to form within the temple an inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place. ¹⁷ The main hall in front of this room was forty cubits long. ¹⁸ The cedar of the interior was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; no stone was visible. ¹⁹ He prepared the inner sanctuary within the temple to set the ark of the covenant of the LORD there. ²⁰ The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold, and he also overlaid the cedar altar.

²¹ Solomon overlaid the inside of the temple with pure gold, and he extended gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was overlaid with gold. ²² He overlaid the whole interior with gold. He also overlaid with gold the altar belonging to the inner sanctuary. ²³ For the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim out of olive wood, each ten cubits high. ²⁴ One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing was also five cubits — ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other. ²⁵ The second cherub also measured ten cubits: both cherubim were identical in size and shape.

²⁶ Each cherub stood ten cubits tall. ²⁷ Solomon placed the cherubim inside the inner sanctuary, and they spread their wings so that one wing of the first cherub touched one wall while a wing of the second cherub touched the opposite wall — and their inner wings touched each other in the middle of the room. ²⁸ He overlaid the cherubim with gold. ²⁹ He carved the walls of the entire house with figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers — all the way around, inside and out. ³⁰ He covered the floors with gold, inside and out.

³¹ For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood; the lintel and doorposts were a fifth of the wall's width. ³² Both doors were olive wood, and he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on them, then overlaid them with gold, hammering the gold onto the cherubim and the palm trees. ³³ He made the same for the doorposts of the main hall — olive wood, a quarter of the wall's width. ³⁴ The two doors themselves were of cypress wood, each door having two folding leaves. ³⁵ He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on them and covered them with gold laid evenly over the carved work.

³⁶ He built the inner courtyard with three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams. ³⁷ The foundation of the LORD's house had been laid in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv. ³⁸ In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul — the eighth month — the house was finished in every detail, exactly as it had been designed. Solomon had spent seven years building it.

chapters.title: 1 Kings 7
paragraphs: ¹ Solomon also built his own palace, which took him thirteen years to complete. ² He built the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon — a hundred cubits long, fifty wide, and thirty high — supported by four rows of cedar columns with cedar beams across the tops. ³ The ceiling above the beams rested on forty-five pillars, fifteen per row, and was covered with cedar. ⁴ There were three rows of windows facing each other in sets of three, ⁵ and all the doors and doorframes were square — again, windows facing windows in three tiers.

⁶ He built a colonnade fifty cubits long and thirty wide, with a covered porch in front supported by pillars and a canopy overhead. ⁷ He also built the throne room — the Hall of Justice, where he would hear cases — and he paneled it with cedar from floor to ceiling. ⁸ His own living quarters, behind the hall in the inner courtyard, were built the same way. He also built a palace for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married, just like this hall. ⁹ All these buildings, from foundation to roofline and from the outside to the great courtyard, were built of fine dressed stone cut to measure and sawed smooth on all sides. ¹⁰ The foundations were laid with great stones — slabs of eight and ten cubits.

¹¹ Above the foundation were more dressed stones cut to size, and cedar beams. ¹² The great outer courtyard had three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams all the way around, just like the inner courtyard of the LORD's house and the entrance hall of the palace. ¹³ King Solomon sent to Tyre and brought a man named Hiram. ¹⁴ He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father had been a craftsman from Tyre who worked in bronze. Hiram was brilliant — a master of all kinds of bronze work — and he came to King Solomon and carried out all the bronze work assigned to him. ¹⁵ He cast two bronze pillars, each eighteen cubits tall and twelve cubits in circumference.

¹⁶ He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on top of the pillars, each one five cubits tall. ¹⁷ He decorated the capitals with lattice netting and twisted chains — seven strands of chainwork for each capital. ¹⁸ He made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates running around each network to cover the capitals at the top, and he did the same for both capitals. ¹⁹ The capitals on top of the pillars in the porch were shaped like lilies, four cubits tall. ²⁰ Above the rounded part beside the network, pomegranates ran in rows all the way around — two hundred pomegranates encircling each capital.

²¹ He erected the pillars at the porch of the temple. The right pillar he named Jachin, and the left pillar he named Boaz. ²² The tops of both pillars were shaped like lilies. And so the work on the pillars was finished. ²³ He made the great bronze basin — the Sea — ten cubits across, perfectly round, five cubits deep, and thirty cubits in circumference. ²⁴ All around the rim, just below the brim, were two rows of gourds encircling it — ten gourds per cubit, cast as part of the basin. ²⁵ The Sea rested on twelve bronze oxen — three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east — with the Sea mounted on top of them and all their haunches turned inward.

²⁶ The basin was a handsbreadth thick, and its rim was shaped like a cup — like the petals of a lily. It held two thousand baths. ²⁷ Hiram also made ten bronze stands, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits tall. ²⁸ The stands were built with side panels set in frames, ²⁹ and on those panels — between the rails — were carved lions, oxen, and cherubim. Above and below the lions and oxen were decorative wreaths of hammered work. ³⁰ Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles. At the four corners were supports cast as part of the stand, and the supports beneath the basin were also cast with decorative wreaths at each side.

³¹ The opening at the top of each stand — inside the capital — was a cubit deep. The opening itself was round, a cubit and a half across, and around its edges were carvings and panels — square, not round. ³² Below the opening were four wheels fitted with bronze axles connected to the body of the stand. Each wheel was a cubit and a half in diameter. ³³ The wheels were crafted like chariot wheels — their axles, hubs, spokes, and rims all cast in bronze. ³⁴ Each of the four corners had a cast support that was part of the stand itself. ³⁵ At the top of each stand was a round collar half a cubit high, and the panels and frames at the top were cast as part of the stand.

³⁶ On the surfaces of the panels and frames he engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees, with decorative borders all around. ³⁷ This is how he made all ten stands — all poured from the same mold, the same size, the same design. ³⁸ He also made ten bronze basins, one for each stand. Each basin was four cubits across and held forty baths. ³⁹ He placed five stands on the south side of the temple and five on the north, and he set the Sea on the southeast corner. ⁴⁰ Hiram finished the basins, the shovels, and the bowls. With that, all the bronze work he had been doing for King Solomon on the LORD's house was complete.
