¹⁶ Men from Benjamin and Judah came to David at the stronghold. ¹⁷ David went out to meet them and said, "If you have come to me in peace to help me, then my heart will be united with yours. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies when I have done no wrong, then may the God of our fathers see it and judge you." ¹⁸ Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the thirty, and he said, "We are yours, David — we are on your side, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to all who help you, for your God helps you." David welcomed them and made them leaders of his raiding bands. ¹⁹ Some men of Manasseh also defected to David when he came with the Philistines to fight against Saul — though they did not help the Philistines, because the Philistine lords, after deliberation, sent David away. They said, "He will defect back to his master Saul, and it will cost us our heads." ²⁰ As David returned to Ziklag, these men of Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zilthai — all commanders of units in Manasseh.

²¹ They helped David against the raiding bands, for they were all valiant warriors and became commanders in his army. ²² Day after day men kept coming to help David, until his force was as vast as the army of God. ²³ These are the numbers of the armed troops who came to David at Hebron to hand over Saul's kingdom to him, just as the LORD had said. ²⁴ The men of Judah who carried shield and spear: six thousand eight hundred armed and ready for battle. ²⁵ Of the men of Simeon, valiant warriors for war: seven thousand one hundred.

²⁶ Of the descendants of Levi: four thousand six hundred. ²⁷ Jehoiada was the leader of the Aaronites, and with him were three thousand seven hundred. ²⁸ Zadok, a young warrior of great ability, came with twenty-two commanders from his own family. ²⁹ Of the men of Benjamin, kinsmen of Saul: three thousand — for until then most of them had remained loyal to the house of Saul. ³⁰ Of the men of Ephraim: twenty thousand eight hundred valiant warriors, famous men throughout their clans.

³¹ Of the half-tribe of Manasseh: eighteen thousand, who were designated by name to come and make David king. ³² Of the men of Issachar, who had understanding of the times and knew what Israel should do: two hundred chiefs, with all their kinsmen under their command. ³³ Of Zebulun: fifty thousand seasoned troops equipped for battle with every weapon of war, all ready to fight with a single purpose of heart. ³⁴ Of Naphtali: one thousand commanders, with thirty-seven thousand men carrying shield and spear. ³⁵ Of the Danites, battle-ready troops: twenty-eight thousand six hundred.

³⁶ Of Asher: forty thousand experienced troops ready for battle. ³⁷ From the east side of the Jordan, men of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh: one hundred and twenty thousand equipped with every kind of weapon. ³⁸ All these warriors, lined up in battle formation, came to Hebron with a single heart to make David king over all Israel. And all the rest of Israel also shared this one purpose — to make David king. ³⁹ They spent three days there with David, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had made provision for them. ⁴⁰ Moreover, their neighbors from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen — supplies of flour, figs, raisins, wine, olive oil, and oxen and sheep in abundance, for there was joy in Israel.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 13
paragraphs: ¹ David consulted with his officers over thousands and hundreds — with every leader. ² He said to the whole assembly of Israel, "If it seems good to you, and if this is the will of the LORD our God, let us send word to our brothers who remain in all the territories of Israel, and to the priests and Levites in their towns and pasturelands, and ask them to join us. ³ Then let us bring the ark of our God back to us, for we neglected it during the days of Saul." ⁴ The whole assembly agreed to do this, for it seemed right in the eyes of all the people. ⁵ So David assembled all Israel, from the Shihor River in Egypt to Lebo Hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath Jearim.

⁶ David went up with all Israel to Baalah — that is, Kiriath Jearim in Judah — to bring up from there the ark of God, who is enthroned between the cherubim, the ark that bears his name. ⁷ They moved the ark of God from Abinadab's house on a new cart, with Uzzah and Ahio guiding it. ⁸ David and all Israel were celebrating before God with all their might — with songs, harps, lyres, timbrels, cymbals, and trumpets. ⁹ When they reached the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzzah reached out his hand to steady the ark, because the oxen stumbled. ¹⁰ The LORD's anger burned against Uzzah, and he struck him down because he had put his hand on the ark. He died there before God.

¹¹ David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah; so that place was called Perez Uzzah to this day. ¹² David was afraid of God that day and asked, "How can I ever bring the ark of God to me?" ¹³ He did not take the ark to the city of David but took it aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite. ¹⁴ The ark of God remained with the household of Obed-Edom in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed his household and everything he had.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 14
paragraphs: ¹ Hiram king of Tyre sent envoys to David, along with cedar logs, stonemasons, and carpenters to build a palace for him. ² David knew that the LORD had confirmed him as king over Israel and that his kingdom had been exalted for the sake of his people Israel. ³ In Jerusalem David took more wives and fathered more sons and daughters. ⁴ These are the names of the children born to him there: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, ⁵ Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,

⁶ Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, ⁷ Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet. ⁸ When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they came out in full force to search for him. David heard of this and went out to meet them. ⁹ Now the Philistines had come and raided the Valley of Rephaim. ¹⁰ David inquired of God, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hands?" The LORD answered him, "Go up, I will deliver them into your hands."

¹¹ So they went up to Baal Perazim, and David defeated them there. He said, "God has broken through my enemies by my hand like a flood breaking through." So that place was named Baal Perazim. ¹² The Philistines abandoned their gods there, and David gave orders to burn them in the fire. ¹³ Once more the Philistines raided the valley. ¹⁴ David inquired of God again, and God answered, "Do not go up directly after them; circle around them and attack them in front of the balsam trees. ¹⁵ When you hear a sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then go out to battle, for God has gone out before you to strike down the Philistine army."
¹⁶ David did as God commanded him, and they struck down the Philistine army all the way from Gibeon to Gezer. ¹⁷ David's fame spread throughout every land, and the LORD made all the nations fear him.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 15
paragraphs: ¹ David built houses for himself in the city of David and prepared a place for the ark of God, pitching a tent for it. ² Then he said, "No one may carry the ark of God except the Levites, for the LORD chose them to carry the ark of God and to minister before him forever." ³ David assembled all Israel in Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the LORD to the place he had prepared for it. ⁴ He gathered together the descendants of Aaron and the Levites: ⁵ From the descendants of Kohath, Uriel the chief, with a hundred and twenty of his relatives.

⁶ From the descendants of Merari: Asaiah the chief, with two hundred and twenty of his relatives. ⁷ From the descendants of Gershom: Joel the chief, with a hundred and thirty of his relatives. ⁸ From the descendants of Elizaphan: Shemaiah the chief, with two hundred of his relatives. ⁹ From the descendants of Hebron: Eliel the chief, with eighty of his relatives. ¹⁰ From the descendants of Uzziel: Amminadab the chief, with a hundred and twelve of his relatives.

¹¹ David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab. ¹² He said to them, "You are the heads of the Levitical families. You and your fellow Levites must consecrate yourselves, so that you may bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I have prepared for it. ¹³ It was because you Levites did not carry it the first time that the LORD our God broke out in anger against us. We did not inquire of him about how to do it in the proper way." ¹⁴ So the priests and Levites consecrated themselves in order to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel. ¹⁵ And the Levites carried the ark of God with the poles on their shoulders, just as Moses had commanded in accordance with the word of the LORD.

¹⁶ David told the leaders of the Levites to appoint some of their fellow Levites as musicians to play joyful music on instruments — harps, lyres, and cymbals. ¹⁷ So the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel, and from his relatives, Asaph son of Berechiah, and from the descendants of Merari, their relatives, Ethan son of Kushaiah. ¹⁸ Along with them were their relatives next in rank: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel — the gatekeepers. ¹⁹ The musicians Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were to sound bronze cymbals. ²⁰ Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah were to play harps according to Alamoth.

²¹ Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to play lyres, leading in the Sheminith. ²² Kenaniah was the head Levite in charge of the music, because he was skilled at it. ²³ Berechiah and Elkanah were to be doorkeepers for the ark. ²⁴ Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer the priests were to blow the trumpets before the ark of God. Obed-Edom and Jehiah were also doorkeepers for the ark. ²⁵ David and the elders of Israel and the commanders of thousands went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-Edom with great rejoicing.

²⁶ And because God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams. ²⁷ Now David was dressed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who carried the ark, and as were the musicians and Kenaniah the director of the music. David also wore a linen ephod. ²⁸ So all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with shouts, with the sounding of rams' horns and trumpets, with the playing of cymbals and harps and lyres. ²⁹ As the ark of the covenant of the LORD was entering the city of David, Michal daughter of Saul watched from a window. When she saw King David dancing and celebrating, she despised him in her heart.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 16
paragraphs: ¹ They brought the ark of God and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and they presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings before God. ² When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD. ³ He distributed to each Israelite man and woman a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins. ⁴ He appointed certain Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, to make petition, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel. ⁵ Asaph was the chief, and second to him were Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel — they played the harps and lyres. Asaph sounded the cymbals,

⁶ and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests blew the trumpets regularly before the ark of the covenant of God. ⁷ That day David first gave Asaph and his associates this psalm of thanks to the LORD: ⁸ Give praise to the LORD, proclaim his name; make known among the nations what he has done. ⁹ Sing to him, sing praise to him; tell of all his wonderful acts. ¹⁰ Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.

¹¹ Look to the LORD and his strength; seek his face always. ¹² Remember the wonders he has done, his miracles, and the judgments he pronounced, ¹³ you his servants, the descendants of Israel, his chosen ones, the children of Jacob. ¹⁴ He is the LORD our God; his judgments are in all the earth. ¹⁵ He remembers his covenant forever, the promise he made, for a thousand generations,

¹⁶ the covenant he made with Abraham, the oath he swore to Isaac. ¹⁷ He confirmed it to Jacob as a decree, to Israel as an everlasting covenant: ¹⁸ "To you I will give the land of Canaan as the portion you will inherit." ¹⁹ When they were but few in number, few indeed, and strangers in it, ²⁰ they wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another.

²¹ He allowed no one to oppress them; for their sake he rebuked kings: ²² "Do not touch my anointed ones; do my prophets no harm." ²³ Sing to the LORD, all the earth; proclaim his salvation day after day. ²⁴ Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous deeds among all peoples. ²⁵ For great is the LORD and most worthy of praise; he is to be feared above all gods.

²⁶ For all the gods of the nations are idols, but the LORD made the heavens. ²⁷ Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and joy fill his dwelling place. ²⁸ Ascribe to the LORD, all you families of nations, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength. ²⁹ Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name; bring an offering and come before him. Worship the LORD in the splendor of his holiness. ³⁰ Tremble before him, all the earth! The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved.

³¹ Let the heavens be glad, let the earth rejoice; let them say among the nations, "The LORD reigns!" ³² Let the sea resound, and all that is in it; let the fields be jubilant, and everything in them! ³³ Let the trees of the forest sing, let them sing for joy before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth. ³⁴ Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his love endures forever. ³⁵ Cry out, "Save us, God our Savior; gather us and deliver us from the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise." ³⁶ Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Then all the people said, "Amen," and praised the LORD.

³⁶ Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. And all the people said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. ³⁷ David left Asaph and his associates before the ark of the covenant of the LORD to minister there regularly, each day doing whatever was required. ³⁸ He also left Obed-Edom and his sixty-eight associates, including Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah, as gatekeepers. ³⁹ He left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place in Gibeon ⁴⁰ to present burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, in accordance with everything written in the Law of the LORD, which he had given to Israel.

⁴¹ With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the LORD — "for his love endures forever." ⁴² Heman and Jeduthun had with them trumpets and cymbals for the music, and instruments for the sacred songs. And the sons of Jeduthun were stationed at the gate. ⁴³ Then all the people went home, and David returned to bless his own family.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 17
paragraphs: ¹ After David had settled in his palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, "Here I am, living in a house of cedar, while the ark of the covenant of the LORD is under a tent." ² Nathan replied, "Whatever you have in mind, do it, for God is with you." ³ But that night the word of God came to Nathan, saying: ⁴ "Go and tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD says: You are not the one to build me a house to dwell in. ⁵ I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought Israel up out of Egypt to this day. I have moved from one tent site to another, from one dwelling place to another.

⁶ Wherever I have traveled with all the Israelites, did I ever say to any of their leaders whom I commanded to shepherd my people, "Why have you not built me a house of cedar?"' ⁷ Now then, tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD Almighty says: I took you from the pasture, from tending the flock, to be ruler over my people Israel. ⁸ I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make your name like the names of the greatest men on earth. ⁹ And I will provide a place for my people Israel and will plant them so that they can have a home of their own and no longer be disturbed. Wicked people will not oppress them anymore, as they did at the beginning, ¹⁰ and have done ever since the time I appointed leaders over my people Israel. I will also subdue all your enemies. I declare to you that the LORD will build a house for you.

¹¹ When your days are over and you go to be with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring to succeed you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingdom. ¹² He is the one who will build a house for me, and I will establish his throne forever. ¹³ I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will never take my love away from him, as I took it away from your predecessor. ¹⁴ I will set him over my house and my kingdom forever; his throne will be established forever.'" ¹⁵ Nathan reported to David all the words of this entire revelation.

¹⁶ Then King David went in and sat before the LORD, and he said: "Who am I, LORD God, and what is my family, that you have brought me this far? ¹⁷ And as if this were not enough in your sight, God, you have spoken about the future of the house of your servant. You have looked on me as though I were the most exalted of men, LORD God. ¹⁸ What more can David say to you for honoring your servant? For you know your servant, LORD. ¹⁹ For the sake of your servant and according to your will, you have done this great thing and made known all these great promises. ²⁰ There is no one like you, LORD, and there is no God but you, as we have heard with our own ears.

²¹ And who is like your people Israel — the one nation on earth whose God went out to redeem a people for himself, and to make a name for yourself, and to perform great and awesome wonders by driving out nations from before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt? ²² You made your people Israel your very own forever, and you, LORD, have become their God. ²³ And now, LORD, let the promise you have made concerning your servant and his house be established forever. Do as you promised, ²⁴ so that it will be established and that your name will be great forever. Then people will say, "The LORD Almighty, the God over Israel, is Israel's God!" And the house of your servant David will be established before you. ²⁵ You, my God, have revealed to your servant that you will build a house for him. So your servant has found courage to pray to you.

²⁶ And now, LORD, you are God, and you have promised these good things to your servant. ²⁷ Now you have been pleased to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever in your sight; for you, LORD, have blessed it, and it will be blessed forever.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 18
paragraphs: ¹ In the course of time, David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, taking Gath and its surrounding villages from their control. ² He also defeated the Moabites, and they became subject to David and brought him tribute. ³ Moreover, David fought against Hadadezer king of Zobah, in the region of Hamath, when Hadadezer went to establish his control along the Euphrates River. ⁴ David captured a thousand of his chariots, seven thousand charioteers, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He hamstrung all but a hundred of the chariot horses. ⁵ When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of them.

⁶ David then put garrisons in Aram Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to him and brought tribute. The LORD gave David victory everywhere he went. ⁷ David took the gold shields carried by Hadadezer's officers and brought them to Jerusalem. ⁸ From Tibhath and Cun, towns that belonged to Hadadezer, David took a great quantity of bronze, which Solomon later used to make the bronze Sea, the pillars, and various bronze articles. ⁹ When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer king of Zobah, ¹⁰ he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and congratulate him on his victory in battle over Hadadezer, who had been at war with Tou. Hadoram brought all kinds of articles of gold, silver, and bronze.

¹¹ King David dedicated these articles to the LORD, as he had done with the silver and gold he had taken from all these nations: from Edom and Moab, the Ammonites and the Philistines, and Amalek. ¹² Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. ¹³ He put garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became subject to David. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went. ¹⁴ David reigned over all Israel, doing what was just and right for all his people. ¹⁵ Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

¹⁶ Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were the priests; Shavsha was the secretary; ¹⁷ Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and Pelethites; and David's sons were chief officials at the king's side.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 19
paragraphs: ¹ Some time later, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son succeeded him as king. ² David thought, "I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me." So David sent a delegation to express his sympathy to Hanun about his father. When David's envoys came to Hanun in the land of Ammon to comfort him, ³ the Ammonite commanders said to Hanun, "Do you think David is honoring your father by sending envoys to comfort you? Haven't his envoys come to you only to explore and spy out the country and overthrow it?" ⁴ So Hanun seized David's envoys, shaved them, cut off their garments at the buttocks, and sent them away. ⁵ When David was told what had happened to his envoys, he sent messengers to meet them, for they were greatly humiliated. The king said, "Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then come back."

⁶ When the Ammonites realized they had become a stench to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and charioteers from Aram Naharaim, Aram Maakah, and Zobah. ⁷ They hired thirty-two thousand chariots and charioteers, as well as the king of Maakah and his troops, who came and camped near Medeba, while the Ammonites came together from their towns and marched to battle. ⁸ When David heard of this, he sent Joab out with the entire army of fighting men. ⁹ The Ammonites came out and drew up in battle formation at the entrance to their city, while the kings who had come were by themselves in the open country. ¹⁰ Joab saw that there were battle lines in front of him and behind him, so he selected some of the best troops in Israel and deployed them against the Arameans.

¹¹ He put the rest of the men under the command of Abishai his brother, and they were deployed against the Ammonites. ¹² Joab said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you are to rescue me; but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will rescue you. ¹³ Be strong, and let us fight bravely for our people and the cities of our God. The LORD will do what is good in his sight." ¹⁴ Then Joab and the troops with him advanced to fight the Arameans, and they fled before him. ¹⁵ When the Ammonites realized that the Arameans were fleeing, they too fled before his brother Abishai and went inside the city. So Joab went back to Jerusalem.

¹⁶ After the Arameans saw that they had been routed by Israel, they sent messengers and had Arameans brought from beyond the Euphrates River, with Shophach the commander of Hadadezer's army leading them. ¹⁷ When David was told of this, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and advanced against them. David deployed his forces to fight the Arameans, and battle was joined. ¹⁸ But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven thousand of their charioteers and forty thousand of their foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach the commander of their army. ¹⁹ When the vassals of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and became subject to him. So the Arameans were not willing to help the Ammonites anymore.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 20
paragraphs: ¹ In the spring, at the time when kings go off to war, Joab led out the armed forces. He laid waste the land of the Ammonites and went to Rabbah and besieged it, but David stayed in Jerusalem. Joab attacked Rabbah and left it in ruins. ² David took the crown from the head of their king — its weight was found to be a talent of gold, and it was set with precious stones — and it was placed on David's head. He took a great quantity of plunder from the city ³ and brought out the people who were there, consigning them to labor with saws and with iron picks and axes. David did this to all the Ammonite towns. Then David and his entire army returned to Jerusalem.

⁶ In another battle, which took place at Gath, there was a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot — twenty-four in all. He also was descended from Rapha. ⁷ When he taunted Israel, Jonathan son of Shimea, David's brother, killed him. ⁸ These were descendants of Rapha in Gath, and they fell at the hands of David and his men.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 21
paragraphs: ¹ Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to take a census of Israel. ² David said to Joab and the commanders of the troops, "Go and count the Israelites from Beersheba to Dan. Then report back to me so I may know how many there are." ³ But Joab replied, "May the LORD multiply his troops a hundred times over. My lord the king, are they not all my lord's subjects? Why does my lord want to do this? Why should he bring guilt on Israel?" ⁴ The king's word, however, overruled Joab; so Joab left and went throughout Israel and then came back to Jerusalem. ⁵ Joab reported the number of the fighting men to David: In all Israel there were one million one hundred thousand men who could handle a sword, including four hundred and seventy thousand in Judah.

⁶ But Joab did not include Levi and Benjamin in the numbering, because the king's command was repulsive to him. This matter was also evil in the sight of God; so he punished Israel. ⁷ Then David said to God, "I have sinned greatly by doing this. Now, I beg you, take away the guilt of your servant. I have done a very foolish thing." ⁸ The LORD said to Gad, David's seer, ⁹ "Go and tell David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am giving you three options. Choose one of them for me to carry out against you.'" ¹⁰ So Gad went to David and said to him, "This is what the LORD says:

¹¹ "Choose for yourself: ¹² three years of famine, or three months of being swept away before your enemies, with their swords overtaking you, or three days of the sword of the LORD — plagues in the land, with the angel of the LORD ravaging every part of Israel. Now then, decide how I should answer the one who sent me." ¹³ David said to Gad, "I am in deep distress. Let me fall into the hands of the LORD, for his mercy is very great; but do not let me fall into human hands." ¹⁴ So the LORD sent a plague on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell dead. ¹⁵ And God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem. But as the angel was doing so, the LORD saw it and relented concerning the disaster and said to the angel who was destroying the people, "Enough! Withdraw your hand." The angel of the LORD was then standing at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

¹⁶ David looked up and saw the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand extended over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell facedown. ¹⁷ David said to God, "Was it not I who ordered the fighting men to be counted? I, the shepherd, have sinned and done wrong. These are but sheep. What have they done? LORD my God, let your hand fall on me and my family, but do not let this plague remain on your people."

²¹ As David approached, Ornan looked up and saw him. He left the threshing floor and bowed down before David with his face to the ground. ²² David said to him, "Let me have the site of your threshing floor so I can build an altar to the LORD there. Sell it to me at the full price. Then the plague on the people will be stopped." ²³ Ornan said to David, "Take it! Let my lord the king do whatever pleases him. Look, I will give the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I will give all this." ²⁴ But King David replied to Ornan, "No, I insist on paying the full price. I will not take for the LORD what is yours, or sacrifice a burnt offering that costs me nothing." ²⁵ So David paid Ornan six hundred shekels of gold for the site.

²⁶ David built an altar to the LORD there and sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. He called on the LORD, and the LORD answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering. ²⁷ Then the LORD spoke to the angel, and he put his sword back into its sheath. ²⁸ At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he offered sacrifices there. ²⁹ The tabernacle of the LORD, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time on the high place at Gibeon. ³⁰ But David could not go before it to inquire of God, because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 22
paragraphs: ¹ Then David said, "The house of the LORD God is to be here, and also the altar of burnt offering for Israel." ² So David gave orders to assemble the foreigners living in Israel, and from among them he appointed stonecutters to prepare dressed stone for building the house of God. ³ He provided a large amount of iron to make nails for the doors of the gateways and for the clamps, and more bronze than could be weighed. ⁴ He also provided more cedar logs than could be counted, for the Sidonians and Tyrians had brought large numbers of cedar logs to David.

⁶ Then he summoned his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel. ⁷ David said to Solomon, "My son, I had it in my heart to build a house for the name of the LORD my God. ⁸ But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 'You have shed much blood and waged great wars. You shall not build a house for my name, because you have shed so much blood on the earth before me. ⁹ Listen — a son will be born to you, a man of peace. I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side; his name will be Solomon, and I will grant Israel peace and quiet during his reign. ¹⁰ He is the one who will build a house for my name. He will be my son, and I will be his father. I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'"

¹¹ "Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, so that you may succeed and build the house of the LORD your God, as he has promised concerning you. ¹² Only may the LORD give you wisdom and understanding, and commission you over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God. ¹³ You will succeed if you are careful to follow the statutes and ordinances that the LORD gave Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous — do not be afraid or discouraged. ¹⁴ Now, with great effort I have provided for the house of the LORD a hundred thousand talents of gold, a million talents of silver, and quantities of bronze and iron too great to weigh, along with timber and stone. You may add to them. ¹⁵ You have plenty of craftsmen — stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and every kind of skilled worker.

¹⁶ Gold and silver, bronze and iron — it is all beyond counting. Get up and get to work, and may the LORD be with you." ¹⁷ David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help Solomon his son: ¹⁸ "Is not the LORD your God with you? Has he not given you rest on every side? He has handed the inhabitants of this land over to me, and the land is subdued before the LORD and before his people. ¹⁹ Now devote your heart and soul to seeking the LORD your God. Rise up and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that you may bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy vessels of God into the house that will be built in honor of the LORD's name."

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 23
paragraphs: ¹ When David was old and had lived a full life, he made his son Solomon king over Israel. ² He gathered together all the leaders of Israel, along with the priests and the Levites. ³ The Levites were counted from the age of thirty and upward; the total number, counted man by man, came to thirty-eight thousand. ⁴ Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of the house of the LORD; six thousand were officers and judges; ⁵ four thousand were gatekeepers; and four thousand were to praise the LORD with the instruments David had made for that purpose.

⁶ David divided them into groups according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. ⁷ The sons of Gershon were Laadan and Shimei. ⁸ The sons of Laadan: Jehiel the chief, then Zetham and Joel — three in all. ⁹ The sons of Shimei: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran — three. These were the heads of the families of Laadan. ¹⁰ The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah — these four were the sons of Shimei.

¹¹ Jahath was the chief and Zizah was second. Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as a single family. ¹² The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel — four in all. ¹³ The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart to consecrate the most holy things — he and his descendants forever — to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to him, and to pronounce blessings in his name forever. ¹⁴ As for Moses, the man of God, his sons were reckoned as part of the tribe of Levi. ¹⁵ The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.

¹⁶ Of the descendants of Gershom, Shebuel was the chief. ¹⁷ Of the descendants of Eliezer, Rehabiah was the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah's descendants were very numerous. ¹⁸ Of the sons of Izhar, Shelomith was the chief. ¹⁹ Of the sons of Hebron: Jeriah was the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth. ²⁰ Of the sons of Uzziel: Micah was the first and Isshiah the second.

²¹ The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish. ²² Eleazar died leaving no sons, only daughters. Their kinsmen, the sons of Kish, married them. ²³ The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth — three in all. ²⁴ These were the descendants of Levi, listed by family — the heads of families as registered by name, counted individually. They performed the work of the service in the house of the LORD from the age of twenty years and upward. ²⁵ For David said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people, and he has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever.

²⁶ And since the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of its equipment for its service — ²⁷ for by David's final instructions the Levites were counted from twenty years old and upward — ²⁸ their duty is to assist the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD, caring for the courts and chambers, purifying all the holy things, and performing every task involved in the service of God's house; ²⁹ also to handle the rows of bread, the fine flour for grain offerings, the wafers of unleavened bread, the baked goods, and the fried offerings, as well as all the measures of quantity and size; ³⁰ and to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and likewise in the evening;

³¹ and to offer all the burnt sacrifices to the LORD on the Sabbaths, the new moon festivals, and the appointed feasts, in the proper number and prescribed manner, continually before the LORD. ³² They were also to be in charge of the tent of meeting and the holy place, and to assist their kinsmen the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD."

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 24
paragraphs: ¹ These were the divisions of the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. ² But Nadab and Abihu died before their father and had no sons, so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests. ³ David, together with Zadok from among the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech from among the sons of Ithamar, organized them according to their appointed duties in the service. ⁴ Since there proved to be more leaders among the sons of Eleazar than among the sons of Ithamar, they were divided accordingly — sixteen heads of families from the sons of Eleazar and eight from the sons of Ithamar. ⁵ They were assigned by lot, equally, for there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God among both the sons of Eleazar and the sons of Ithamar.

⁶ Shemaiah son of Nethaneel, a Levite scribe, recorded the assignments before the king, the princes, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the priestly and Levite families — one family being drawn for Eleazar and then one for Ithamar. ⁷ The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah, ⁸ the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim, ⁹ the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin, ¹⁰ the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,

¹¹ the ninth to Jeshuah, the tenth to Shecaniah, ¹² the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim, ¹³ the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab, ¹⁴ the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer, ¹⁵ the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Aphses,

¹⁶ the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezekel, ¹⁷ the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul, ¹⁸ the twenty-third to Delaiah, the twenty-fourth to Maaziah. ¹⁹ This was the order in which they were to carry out their service when entering the house of the LORD, as their ancestor Aaron had directed them, following the command of the LORD, the God of Israel. ²⁰ As for the remaining descendants of Levi: from the sons of Amram came Shubael, and from the sons of Shubael came Jehdeiah.

²¹ Concerning Rehabiah: from his sons, Isshiah was the chief. ²² Of the Izharites: Shelomoth, and from his sons came Jahath. ²³ The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth. ²⁴ Of the sons of Uzziel: Michah; and from Michah's sons came Shamir. ²⁵ Michah's brother was Isshiah, and from Isshiah's sons came Zechariah.

²⁶ The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. And from the sons of Jaaziah came Beno. ²⁷ The sons of Merari through Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri. ²⁸ From Mahli came Eleazar, who had no sons. ²⁹ As for Kish, his son was Jerahmeel. ³⁰ The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the descendants of the Levites by their families.

³¹ Like their kinsmen the sons of Aaron, these also cast lots before King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the priestly and Levite families — senior family heads alongside their younger relatives.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 25
paragraphs: ¹ David and the army commanders set apart for the ministry the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, those who were to prophesy with harps, lyres, and cymbals. The list of those who carried out this service was as follows: ² From the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah — the sons of Asaph, under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied at the king's command. ³ From the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah — six — under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the harp, giving thanks and praise to the LORD. ⁴ From the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth. ⁵ All of these were sons of Heman, the king's seer, given to him through God's promises to exalt him. God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

⁶ All of them served under their father's direction in the music ministry of the house of the LORD, with cymbals, lyres, and harps, as the king had commanded through Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman. ⁷ The total number of them, along with their kinsmen who were trained in music for the LORD — all who were skilled — was two hundred and eighty-eight. ⁸ They cast lots for their duties, young and old alike, teacher and student together. ⁹ The first lot, which went to the family of Asaph, fell to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, together with his brothers and sons — twelve in all; ¹⁰ the third to Zaccur, with his sons and brothers — twelve;

¹¹ the fourth to Izri, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ¹² the fifth to Nethaniah, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ¹³ the sixth to Bukkiah, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ¹⁴ the seventh to Jesharelah, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ¹⁵ the eighth to Jeshaiah, with his sons and brothers — twelve;

¹⁶ the ninth to Mattaniah, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ¹⁷ the tenth to Shimei, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ¹⁸ the eleventh to Azareel, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ¹⁹ the twelfth to Hashabiah, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ²⁰ the thirteenth to Shubael, with his sons and brothers — twelve;

²¹ the fourteenth to Mattithiah, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ²² the fifteenth to Jeremoth, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ²³ the sixteenth to Hananiah, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ²⁴ the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ²⁵ the eighteenth to Hanani, with his sons and brothers — twelve;

²⁶ the nineteenth to Mallothi, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ²⁷ the twentieth to Eliathah, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ²⁸ the twenty-first to Hothir, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ²⁹ the twenty-second to Giddalti, with his sons and brothers — twelve; ³⁰ the twenty-third to Mahazioth, with his sons and brothers — twelve;
³¹ the twenty-fourth to Romamti-ezer, with his sons and brothers — twelve.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 26
paragraphs: ¹ These were the divisions of the gatekeepers: From the Korahites, Meshelemiah son of Kore, one of the sons of Asaph. ² Meshelemiah's sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth, ³ Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Elioenai the seventh. ⁴ Obed-edom's sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethaneel the fifth, ⁵ Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peulthai the eighth — for God had blessed Obed-edom.

⁶ Obed-edom's son Shemaiah also had sons who were leaders in their father's family, for they were men of great ability. ⁷ The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad — along with their brothers Elihu and Semachiah, who were capable men. ⁸ All of these were descendants of Obed-edom — they and their sons and brothers, sixty-two capable and strong men in the service. ⁹ Meshelemiah also had sons and brothers — eighteen capable men in all. ¹⁰ Hosah of the Merarites also had sons: Simri was the chief, although he was not the firstborn, his father had appointed him chief.

¹¹ Hilkiah was the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Hosah numbered thirteen. ¹² These divisions of gatekeepers, through their leaders, had assignments for service in the house of the LORD, just as their kinsmen did. ¹³ They cast lots by family for each gate, young and old alike. ¹⁴ The lot for the East Gate fell to Shelemiah. Then lots were cast for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and his lot came out for the North Gate. ¹⁵ The lot for Obed-edom fell to the South Gate, and to his sons fell the storehouse.

¹⁶ Shuppim and Hosah drew the West Gate along with the Shallecheth Gate on the upper road — guard station against guard station. ¹⁷ There were six Levites stationed each day at the east side, four at the north, four at the south, and two at a time at the storehouse. ¹⁸ At the court on the west side there were four at the road and two at the court itself. ¹⁹ These were the divisions of the gatekeepers among the Korahites and Merarites. ²⁰ Ahijah, a fellow Levite, was in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated gifts.

²¹ Among the sons of Laadan the Gershonite — the family heads of Laadan the Gershonite — Jehieli was chief. ²² The sons of Jehieli, Zetham and his brother Joel, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD. ²³ From among the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites: ²⁴ Shebuel son of Gershom, son of Moses, was chief officer in charge of the treasuries. ²⁵ Through his kinsman Eliezer came Rehabiah his son, then Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.

²⁶ This Shelomith and his brothers had charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated things — those which King David, the family heads, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the army commanders had dedicated. ²⁷ They had dedicated part of the plunder from their campaigns to maintain the house of the LORD. ²⁸ Everything that Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah had dedicated — along with anything dedicated by anyone else — was under the care of Shelomith and his brothers. ²⁹ From the Izharites: Chenaniah and his sons handled the administrative work outside the sanctuary as officers and judges over Israel. ³⁰ From the Hebronites: Hashabiah and his kinsmen, seventeen hundred capable men, were officials over Israel west of the Jordan in everything pertaining to the LORD and the king's service.

³¹ Among the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief, according to the genealogical records of his family. In the fortieth year of David's reign, a search was made and capable men were found among them at Jazer in Gilead. ³² His kinsmen were twenty-seven hundred capable men, heads of families, and King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in every matter concerning God and the king.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 27
paragraphs: ¹ This is the list of the Israelites — heads of families, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and their officers who served the king in all military matters. Each division served for one month of the year and consisted of twenty-four thousand men. ² In charge of the first division for the first month was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel; his division had twenty-four thousand men. ³ He was a descendant of Perez and was chief of all the army commanders for the first month. ⁴ In charge of the division for the second month was Dodai the Ahohite; his division had twenty-four thousand men, with Mikloth as his deputy. ⁵ The third army commander, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the chief priest; his division had twenty-four thousand men.

⁶ This is the Benaiah who was a mighty warrior among the Thirty and was their commander; his son Ammizabad was in charge of his division. ⁷ The fourth commander, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, with his son Zebadiah succeeding him; his division had twenty-four thousand men. ⁸ The fifth commander, for the fifth month, was Shamhuth the Izrahite; his division had twenty-four thousand men. ⁹ The sixth commander, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; his division had twenty-four thousand men. ¹⁰ The seventh commander, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite from the tribe of Ephraim; his division had twenty-four thousand men.

¹¹ The eighth commander, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, a Zerahite; his division had twenty-four thousand men. ¹² The ninth commander, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, a Benjamite; his division had twenty-four thousand men. ¹³ The tenth commander, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, a Zerahite; his division had twenty-four thousand men. ¹⁴ The eleventh commander, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite from the tribe of Ephraim; his division had twenty-four thousand men. ¹⁵ The twelfth commander, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, from the family of Othniel; his division had twenty-four thousand men.

¹⁶ The officers over the tribes of Israel: over the Reubenites, Eliezer son of Zichri; over the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah; ¹⁷ over the Levites, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; over the Aaronites, Zadok; ¹⁸ over Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers; over Issachar, Omri son of Michael; ¹⁹ over Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; over Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel; ²⁰ over the Ephraimites, Hoshea son of Azaziah; over the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;

²¹ over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; over Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner; ²² over Dan, Azareel son of Jeroham. These were the commanders of the tribes of Israel. ²³ David did not count those twenty years old and under, because the LORD had promised to make Israel as numerous as the stars of the sky. ²⁴ Joab son of Zeruiah began the census but never completed it, because God's wrath fell on Israel on account of it, and the final count was never entered in the chronicles of King David. ²⁵ Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the royal storehouses. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses in the fields, the towns, the villages, and the towers.

²⁶ Ezri son of Chelub was in charge of the field workers who farmed the land. ²⁷ Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards. Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the wine cellars. ²⁸ Baalhanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the western foothills. Joash was in charge of the olive oil stores. ²⁹ Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the herds grazing in Sharon. Shaphat son of Adlai was in charge of the herds in the valleys. ³⁰ Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels. Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys.

³¹ Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flocks. All these were the officials responsible for King David's property. ³² Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor — a wise man and a scribe. Jehiel son of Hacmoni looked after the king's sons. ³³ Ahithophel was the king's counselor. Hushai the Arkite was the king's trusted friend. ³⁴ After Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah, and then Abiathar. And the commander of the king's army was Joab.

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 28
paragraphs: ¹ David assembled all the leaders of Israel in Jerusalem — the tribal commanders, the commanders of the divisions that served the king, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the officials over all the king's property and livestock, the palace officials, the soldiers and warriors, every man of standing. ² King David rose to his feet and said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I had my heart set on building a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD — a footstool for our God — and I made preparations for building it. ³ But God said to me, 'You shall not build a house for my name, because you have been a warrior and have shed blood.' ⁴ Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from my whole family to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah as the leading tribe, and from Judah he chose my father's family, and from among my father's sons he was pleased to make me king over all Israel. ⁵ Of all my sons — for the LORD has given me many — he has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.

⁶ "He said to me, 'Your son Solomon will build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father. ⁷ I will establish his kingdom forever, if he holds firmly to carrying out my commands and ordinances, as he does now.' ⁸ So in the sight of all Israel, the LORD's assembly, and in the hearing of our God: keep and seek out all the commands of the LORD your God, so that you may hold this good land and pass it on as an inheritance to your descendants forever. ⁹ And you, my son Solomon, know the God of your father and serve him with wholehearted devotion and a willing spirit, for the LORD searches every heart and understands every intention behind every thought. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you abandon him, he will reject you forever. ¹⁰ Consider carefully now, for the LORD has chosen you to build a house as the sanctuary. Be strong and do the work."

¹¹ Then David gave Solomon the plans for the vestibule of the temple, its buildings, its storerooms, its upper rooms, its inner rooms, and the room for the mercy seat. ¹² He also gave him the plans for everything he had in mind for the courts of the house of the LORD, all the surrounding rooms, the treasuries of God's house, and the treasuries for the dedicated gifts. ¹³ He gave him instructions for the divisions of the priests and Levites, for all the work of serving in the house of the LORD, and for all the articles used in the service. ¹⁴ He specified the weight of gold for each gold article used in various kinds of service, the weight of silver for each silver article used in various kinds of service, ¹⁵ the weight of gold for the golden lampstands and their lamps, with the weight for each lampstand and its lamps; and the weight of silver for the silver lampstands, with the weight for each lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each.

¹⁶ He also specified the weight of gold for each table of consecrated bread, and the weight of silver for the silver tables; ¹⁷ the weight of pure gold for the forks, sprinkling bowls, and pitchers; the weight of gold for each gold dish and the weight of silver for each silver dish; ¹⁸ and the weight of refined gold for the altar of incense. He also gave David the plan for the golden chariot — the cherubim that spread their wings and shelter the ark of the covenant of the LORD. ¹⁹ "All this is in writing," said David, "because the hand of the LORD was on me, guiding me in all the details of the plan." ²⁰ David also said to his son Solomon, "Be strong and courageous, and do the work. Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not fail you or abandon you until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.

²¹ The divisions of the priests and Levites are ready for all the service of God's house. Every willing and skilled person will serve with you in all the work, and the commanders and all the people will obey your every command."

chapters.title: 1 Chronicles 29
paragraphs: ¹ Then King David said to the whole assembly, "My son Solomon — the one whom God has chosen — is young and inexperienced, and the work is enormous, for this palace is not being built for a human being but for the LORD God. ² With all my resources I have provided for the temple of my God: gold for the gold work, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron, wood for the wood, onyx for the settings, turquoise, stones of various colors, all kinds of fine stone, and marble — great quantities of it. ³ Besides all this, in my devotion to the temple of my God I give from my personal treasury of gold and silver — over and above everything I have already provided — ⁴ three thousand talents of gold from Ophir and seven thousand talents of refined silver for overlaying the walls of the buildings; ⁵ gold for the gold work and silver for the silver — everything that will be made by craftsmen. Now, who is willing to consecrate himself today to the LORD?"

⁶ Then the family heads and officers of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king's work gave willingly. ⁷ They donated toward the work on God's temple: five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron. ⁸ Those who had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD in the care of Jehiel the Gershonite. ⁹ The people rejoiced because these offerings were given freely and wholeheartedly. King David also rejoiced greatly. ¹⁰ David praised the LORD in the presence of the whole assembly, saying, "Praise be to you, LORD, the God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.

¹¹ "Yours, LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the splendor and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth is yours. Yours, LORD, is the kingdom; you are exalted as head over all. ¹² Wealth and honor come from you; you are the ruler of all things. In your hands are strength and power to exalt and give strength to all. ¹³ Now, our God, we give you thanks and praise your glorious name. ¹⁴ But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what comes from your hand. ¹⁵ We are foreigners and strangers in your sight, as were all our ancestors. Our days on earth are like a shadow, without hope.

¹⁶ "LORD our God, all this abundance that we have provided for building you a temple for your holy name comes from your hand, and it all belongs to you. ¹⁷ I know, my God, that you test the heart and are pleased with integrity. All these things I have given willingly and with honest intent. And now I have seen with joy how willingly your people who are here have given to you. ¹⁸ LORD, the God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, keep these desires and thoughts in the hearts of your people forever, and keep their hearts loyal to you. ¹⁹ And give my son Solomon the wholehearted devotion to keep your commands, statutes, and decrees, and to do everything to build the palace for which I have made provision." ²⁰ Then David said to the whole assembly, "Praise the LORD your God." And the whole assembly praised the LORD, the God of their fathers, bowing low and prostrating themselves before the LORD and the king.

²¹ The next day they brought sacrifices and burnt offerings to the LORD: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, along with their drink offerings, and other sacrifices in abundance for all Israel. ²² They ate and drank before the LORD that day with great joy. Then they acknowledged Solomon son of David as king a second time, anointing him before the LORD as ruler and Zadok as priest. ²³ So Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of his father David. He prospered and all Israel obeyed him. ²⁴ All the officers and warriors, and even all of King David's other sons, pledged their submission to King Solomon. ²⁵ The LORD highly exalted Solomon in the sight of all Israel and bestowed on him royal splendor such as no king over Israel had ever had before.

²⁶ So David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel. ²⁷ He ruled over Israel for forty years — seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem. ²⁸ He died at a ripe old age, having enjoyed long life, wealth, and honor. His son Solomon succeeded him as king. ²⁹ As for the events of King David's reign, from beginning to end, they are written in the records of Samuel the seer, the records of Nathan the prophet, and the records of Gad the seer, ³⁰ together with the full account of his reign and power, and the circumstances that surrounded him and Israel and the kingdoms of all the other lands.

chapters.title: 2 Chronicles 1
paragraphs: ¹ Solomon son of David established himself firmly in his kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great. ² Solomon spoke to all Israel — to the commanders of thousands and hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader and head of family throughout Israel. ³ Then Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon, for that was where the tent of meeting stood — the tabernacle that Moses the LORD's servant had built in the wilderness. ⁴ David had already brought the ark of God up from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, having pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem. ⁵ The bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made stood before the tabernacle of the LORD, and Solomon and the assembly went there to seek God.

⁶ Solomon went up to the bronze altar before the LORD at the tent of meeting and offered a thousand burnt offerings on it. ⁷ That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you." ⁸ Solomon answered God, "You showed great kindness to my father David and have made me king in his place. ⁹ Now, LORD God, let your promise to my father David hold true, for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth. ¹⁰ Give me wisdom and knowledge so that I may lead this people — for who could possibly govern this great nation of yours?"

¹¹ God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart — because you did not ask for wealth, riches, or honor, and you did not ask for the death of your enemies or for a long life, but instead asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern my people over whom I have made you king — ¹² wisdom and knowledge are granted to you. And I will also give you wealth, riches, and honor beyond anything any king before you has ever had, and no king after you will match it." ¹³ Solomon returned from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, and went to Jerusalem, where he reigned over Israel. ¹⁴ He gathered chariots and horsemen — fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen — and stationed them in the chariot cities and with himself in Jerusalem. ¹⁵ The king made silver and gold as plentiful in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as common as the fig trees in the foothills.

¹⁶ Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt, and his merchants bought linen yarn at a set price. ¹⁷ They would acquire a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty — and in this way they also exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

chapters.title: 2 Chronicles 2
paragraphs: ¹ Solomon decided to build a temple for the name of the LORD and a royal palace for himself. ² He conscripted seventy thousand men as laborers, eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hills, and three thousand six hundred as foremen over them. ³ Solomon sent a message to Huram king of Tyre: "Deal with me as you dealt with my father David when you sent him cedar to build a palace to live in. ⁴ I am now building a temple for the name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to him, to burn fragrant incense before him, to set out the bread of the Presence, and to present burnt offerings every morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, at the new moon feasts, and at the appointed festivals of the LORD our God — this is a lasting obligation for Israel. ⁵ The temple I am building will be great, because our God is greater than all gods."

⁶ "But who can build a house worthy of him, when the heavens — even the highest heavens — cannot contain him? Who am I to build him a house, except to burn offerings before him? ⁷ Send me now a skilled craftsman who can work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, and in purple, crimson, and blue yarn, and who knows how to engrave — to work with the skilled craftsmen I have here in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided. ⁸ Send me also cedar, pine, and algum logs from Lebanon, for I know your servants are expert at cutting timber in Lebanon. My servants will work alongside yours ⁹ to prepare plenty of timber for me, because the temple I am going to build must be large and magnificent. ¹⁰ As wages for your woodsmen who cut the timber, I will give twenty thousand cors of crushed wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of olive oil."

¹¹ Huram king of Tyre replied in a letter he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you their king." ¹² Huram added, "Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth! He has given King David a wise son with good sense and discernment, who will build a temple for the LORD and a palace for his own kingdom. ¹³ I am sending you a skilled craftsman, Huram-Abi, a man of great ability. ¹⁴ His mother was from the daughters of Dan and his father was a man of Tyre. He is experienced in working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and timber, and in purple, blue, and crimson yarn and fine linen. He can also execute all kinds of engraving and carry out any design that is given to him. He will work alongside your craftsmen and the craftsmen of my lord, your father David. ¹⁵ Now let my lord send his servants the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine he promised —

¹⁶ and we will cut as much timber from Lebanon as you need and bring it down to you as rafts by sea to Joppa, and you can take it up to Jerusalem." ¹⁷ Solomon counted all the foreigners living in Israel, following the census his father David had taken, and found there were one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred of them. ¹⁸ He assigned seventy thousand of them as carriers, eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hills, and three thousand six hundred as foremen to keep the people working.

chapters.title: 2 Chronicles 3
paragraphs: ¹ Solomon began building the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David, at the place David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. ² He began building on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign. ³ These were the foundations Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length was sixty cubits by the older standard, and the width was twenty cubits. ⁴ The porch at the front of the temple was twenty cubits wide, matching the width of the building, and twenty cubits high, and he overlaid it on the inside with pure gold. ⁵ The main hall he paneled with pine and covered it with fine gold, decorating it with palm trees and interwoven chains.

⁶ He adorned the temple with precious stones for beauty, and the gold he used was gold from Parvaim. ⁷ He overlaid the beams, thresholds, walls, and doors of the temple with gold, and carved cherubim on the walls. ⁸ He built the Most Holy Place, which was twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide — matching the width of the temple — and he covered it with six hundred talents of fine gold. ⁹ The gold nails weighed fifty shekels. He also covered the upper rooms with gold. ¹⁰ In the Most Holy Place he made two sculptured cherubim and overlaid them with gold.

¹¹ The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits in total span: one wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, reaching to the wall of the temple, while the other wing was five cubits long, reaching to the wing of the second cherub. ¹² One wing of the second cherub was five cubits, reaching to the other wall, and the other wing was also five cubits, meeting the wing of the first cherub. ¹³ The wings of these cherubim spread out twenty cubits altogether. They stood upright, facing the main hall. ¹⁴ He made the curtain of blue, purple, and crimson yarn and fine linen, and embroidered cherubim on it. ¹⁵ In front of the temple he erected two pillars thirty-five cubits tall, with a capital of five cubits on top of each.

¹⁶ He made interwoven chains and put them on top of the pillars, and he made a hundred pomegranates and fastened them to the chains. ¹⁷ He set up the pillars in front of the temple — one on the south side and one on the north — and named the one on the south Jachin and the one on the north Boaz.

chapters.title: 2 Chronicles 4
paragraphs: ¹ He also made a bronze altar, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high. ² He made the bronze basin — the Sea — ten cubits across from rim to rim, perfectly round, five cubits high, and thirty cubits in circumference. ³ Below the rim, images of bulls encircled it all the way around, ten to a cubit, arranged in two rows cast as one piece with the basin. ⁴ It rested on twelve bulls, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east, with their hindquarters toward the center. The Sea was set on top of them. ⁵ The basin was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was shaped like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.

⁶ He also made ten basins for washing and placed five on the south side and five on the north; the things used for the burnt offerings were rinsed in them. The Sea was for the priests to wash in. ⁷ He made ten gold lampstands according to the prescribed design and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. ⁸ He also made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the south and five on the north. And he made a hundred gold bowls. ⁹ He built the priests' courtyard and the large court, and made doors for the court and overlaid the doors with bronze. ¹⁰ He placed the Sea on the south side, toward the southeast.

¹¹ Huram also made the pots, shovels, and bowls. With that, Huram finished the work he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of God: ¹² the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two sets of interwoven chains to adorn the capitals; ¹³ the four hundred pomegranates for the two chains — two rows of pomegranates for each chain — to adorn the bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars. ¹⁴ He also made the stands with their basins, ¹⁵ and the Sea with the twelve bulls beneath it.

¹⁶ Huram-Abi made all these things — the pots, shovels, meat forks, and all the related articles — for King Solomon for the house of the LORD, out of burnished bronze. ¹⁷ The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan, between Succoth and Zeredah. ¹⁸ Solomon made all these furnishings in such great quantity that the weight of the bronze was beyond calculating. ¹⁹ Solomon also made all the furnishings for the house of God: the golden altar; the tables on which the bread of the Presence was set; ²⁰ the lampstands with their lamps, to burn before the inner sanctuary according to the prescribed pattern, all of pure gold;

²¹ the gold flower decorations, lamps, and tongs — all of solid gold; ²² the wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and incense pans — all of pure gold. The entrance to the temple, including the inner doors leading to the Most Holy Place and the doors of the main hall, were all gold.

chapters.title: 2 Chronicles 5
paragraphs: ¹ At last all the work Solomon had done for the house of the LORD was finished. He brought in everything his father David had dedicated — the silver, the gold, and all the furnishings — and placed them in the treasuries of God's house. ² Then Solomon summoned to Jerusalem the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes and the family leaders of the Israelites, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the city of David. ³ All the Israelite men came together to the king at the festival in the seventh month. ⁴ When all the elders had arrived, the Levites took up the ark. ⁵ The priests and Levites carried the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the sacred furnishings that were in the tent.

⁶ King Solomon and the entire assembly of Israel gathered before the ark and sacrificed so many sheep and cattle that they could not be recorded or counted. ⁷ The priests carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple — the Most Holy Place — and set it beneath the wings of the cherubim. ⁸ The cherubim spread their wings over the spot where the ark rested, covering it and its carrying poles from above. ⁹ The poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the Holy Place just in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside; and they are still there to this day. ¹⁰ There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.

¹¹ When the priests withdrew from the Holy Place — for all the priests present had consecrated themselves, regardless of their assigned divisions — ¹² all the Levite singers, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun and their sons and relatives, stood on the east side of the altar, dressed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres. They were joined by a hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets. ¹³ The trumpeters and singers joined together as one voice to praise and thank the LORD. Accompanied by trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments, they raised their voices in praise to the LORD, singing: "He is good; his faithful love endures forever." At that moment the temple — the house of the LORD — was filled with a cloud. ¹⁴ The priests could not perform their service because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.

chapters.title: 2 Chronicles 6
paragraphs: ¹ Then Solomon declared, "The LORD has said he would dwell in a dark cloud. ² But I have built you a magnificent temple, a place where you will live forever." ³ The king turned to face the whole assembly of Israel, who were standing there, and blessed them. ⁴ He said: "Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, who with his own hands has fulfilled what he promised with his own mouth to my father David. For he said, ⁵ 'From the day I brought my people out of Egypt, I have not chosen any city in any tribe of Israel to have a temple built so that my name would be there, nor have I chosen anyone to be ruler over my people Israel.'"

⁶ "But now I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I have chosen David to rule my people Israel. ⁷ My father David had it in his heart to build a temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel. ⁸ But the LORD told my father David, 'You had it in your heart to build a temple for my name, and you did well to have this desire in your heart. ⁹ Nevertheless, you will not build the temple, but your son, your own flesh and blood — he will build the temple for my name.' ¹⁰ The LORD has kept the promise he made. I have succeeded my father David and I sit on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised, and I have built the temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel."

¹¹ "In it I have placed the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that he made with the people of Israel." ¹² Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the entire assembly of Israel and spread out his hands. ¹³ He had made a bronze platform, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and had placed it in the middle of the outer court. He stood on it, then knelt down before the whole assembly of Israel and spread his hands toward heaven. ¹⁴ He said: "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth — you who keep your covenant and show faithful love to your servants who walk before you wholeheartedly. ¹⁵ You have kept the promise you made to your servant, my father David. With your own mouth you promised it, and with your own hands you have carried it out — as it is today."

¹⁶ "Now, LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant, my father David, the promise you made to him when you said, 'You shall never fail to have a successor before me to sit on the throne of Israel — if only your sons are careful about what they do, walking in my law as you have walked before me.' ¹⁷ And now, LORD, God of Israel, let your word that you spoke to your servant David come true. ¹⁸ But will God really dwell with humans on earth? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain you — how much less this temple I have built! ¹⁹ Yet, LORD my God, hear the prayer and plea your servant is making in your presence today. ²⁰ May your eyes be open toward this temple day and night, toward the place where you said you would put your name. May you hear the prayer your servant directs toward this place."

²¹ "Hear the requests of your servant and your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, your dwelling place; and when you hear, forgive. ²² When a man wrongs his neighbor and is required to take an oath and comes to swear before your altar in this temple, ²³ then hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants — punishing the guilty by bringing the consequences of their actions on their own heads, and vindicating the innocent by treating them in accordance with their innocence. ²⁴ When your people Israel have been defeated by an enemy because they have sinned against you, and they then repent and confess your name, and pray and plead before you in this temple, ²⁵ then hear from heaven, forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave to them and their ancestors."

²⁶ "When the sky is closed and there is no rain because your people have sinned against you, and they pray toward this place and confess your name and turn from their sin when you afflict them, ²⁷ then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel — teach them the good way to live — and send rain on the land you gave your people as an inheritance. ²⁸ When famine or plague strikes the land, or blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers, or when enemies besiege any of the towns of the land — whatever disaster or sickness there may be — ²⁹ then whatever prayer or plea any person among your people Israel makes, each one aware of their own suffering and grief, stretching out their hands toward this temple, ³⁰ hear from heaven, your dwelling place. Forgive, and repay each person according to all their ways, since you know their hearts — for you alone know the hearts of every human being —"

³¹ "so that they will fear you and walk in obedience to you all the time they live in the land you gave our ancestors. ³² As for the foreigner who does not belong to your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of your great name, your mighty hand, and your outstretched arm — when they come and pray toward this temple, ³³ then hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, just as your own people Israel do, and may know that this temple I have built is called by your name. ³⁴ When your people go to war against their enemies, wherever you send them, and they pray to you toward this city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your name, ³⁵ then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause."

³⁶ "When they sin against you — for there is no one who does not sin — and you become angry with them and give them over to the enemy, who takes them captive to a far or near country, ³⁷ and if they come to their senses in the land where they are held captive and repent and plead with you in the land of their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned; we have done wrong and acted wickedly,' ³⁸ and if they turn back to you with all their heart and soul in the land of their captivity where they were taken, and pray toward their land which you gave their ancestors — toward the city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your name — ³⁹ then from heaven, your dwelling place, hear their prayer and their pleas. Uphold their cause, and forgive your people who have sinned against you. ⁴⁰ Now, my God, may your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer offered in this place."

⁴¹ "Now arise, LORD God, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your might.
