⁶ For hardship does not grow from the soil, nor does trouble spring from the ground. ⁷ Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward. ⁸ But if I were you, I would appeal to God and lay my cause before him — ⁹ the one who does great things beyond our understanding, wonders beyond all counting, ¹⁰ who gives rain to the earth and sends water on the fields,

¹¹ who sets the lowly on high and lifts the mourners to safety. ¹² He foils the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands accomplish nothing. ¹³ He catches the wise in their own cunning, and the plans of the devious are swept away. ¹⁴ Darkness overtakes them in broad daylight; at noon they grope as though it were night. ¹⁵ He saves the needy from the sword in their mouths and from the clutches of the powerful.

¹⁶ So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth. ¹⁷ Blessed is the one whom God corrects — so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty. ¹⁸ For he wounds, and he binds up; he injures, and his hands also heal. ¹⁹ From six calamities he will rescue you; in seven no harm will touch you. ²⁰ In famine he will deliver you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.

²¹ You will be sheltered from the lash of the tongue, and need not fear when destruction comes. ²² You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not be afraid of the beasts of the earth. ²³ For you will have an agreement with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you. ²⁴ You will know that your tent is secure; you will take stock of your property and find nothing missing. ²⁵ You will know that your children will be many, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.
²⁶ You will come to the grave in full vigor, like grain that is gathered in season. ²⁷ We have examined this thoroughly, and it is true. Hear it, and apply it to yourself.

chapters.title: Job 6
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job replied: ² "If only my anguish could be weighed and all my misery placed on the scales! ³ It would surely outweigh the sand of the seas — no wonder my words have been rash. ⁴ The arrows of the Almighty have pierced me; my spirit drinks in their poison; God's terrors are marshaled against me. ⁵ Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass? Does an ox bellow when it has feed?

⁶ Can bland food be eaten without salt? Is there any taste in the white of an egg? ⁷ My appetite refuses to touch such things; they are like disgusting food to me. ⁸ Oh, that I might have what I ask for, that God would grant what I hope for — ⁹ that he would be willing to crush me, to let loose his hand and cut me off! ¹⁰ Then I would still have this comfort, this joy even in relentless pain: that I had not denied the words of the Holy One.

¹¹ What strength do I have to go on hoping? What future awaits me that I should be patient? ¹² Is my strength the strength of stone? Is my body made of iron? ¹³ Do I have any power to help myself, now that every resource has been driven from me? ¹⁴ A desperate man should have the devotion of his friends, even if he abandons the fear of the Almighty. ¹⁵ But my brothers have been as treacherous as a seasonal stream, as the courses of streams that run dry,

¹⁶ dark from melting ice and swollen with snowmelt, ¹⁷ but that vanish in the heat and disappear in the warmth. ¹⁸ Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go up into the wasteland and perish. ¹⁹ The caravans of Tema look for water; the traveling merchants of Sheba hope to find it. ²⁰ They are disappointed because they had been confident; they arrived there only to be let down.

²¹ Now you too have proved to be nothing — you see something dreadful and you pull back in fear. ²² Have I ever said, 'Give me something'? Have I asked you, 'Pay a bribe on my behalf'? ²³ Or, 'Rescue me from the hand of the enemy'? Or, 'Deliver me from the grip of ruthless men'? ²⁴ Teach me, and I will be silent; show me where I have been wrong. ²⁵ How painful honest words can be! But what do your arguments prove?

²⁶ Do you think you can reprove my words as though they were just wind? You would even cast lots for the fatherless and make merchandise of your own friend. ²⁷ Are you plotting to criticize me? Would you even cast lots over an orphan and barter away your friend? ²⁸ But now please look at me — would I lie to your face? ²⁹ Relent, do not be unjust; reconsider, for my integrity is at stake. ³⁰ Is there any injustice on my tongue? Can my mouth not discern wickedness?

chapters.title: Job 7
paragraphs: ¹ Is not a person forced to labor on earth? Are not their days like those of a hired worker? ² Like a slave longing for shade, like a hired worker waiting to be paid, ³ so I have been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of misery have been measured out for me. ⁴ When I lie down I think, 'How long before I get up?' The night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn. ⁵ My body is clothed in worms and scabs; my skin is cracked and covered with sores.

⁶ My days fly by faster than a weaver's shuttle and come to an end without hope. ⁷ Remember, O God, that my life is but a breath; my eyes will never see happiness again. ⁸ The eye that now sees me will see me no more; your eyes will look for me, but I will be gone. ⁹ As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so one who goes down to the grave does not return. ¹⁰ He will never come home again; his place will know him no more.

¹¹ Therefore I will not keep silent; I will speak out in the anguish of my spirit, I will complain in the bitterness of my soul. ¹² Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that you put me under guard? ¹³ When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaints, ¹⁴ you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions, ¹⁵ so that I prefer strangling — death itself rather than this body of mine.

¹⁶ I despise my life; I would not live forever. Leave me alone — my days mean nothing. ¹⁷ What is mankind that you make so much of them, that you give them so much attention? ¹⁸ That you examine them every morning and test them every moment? ¹⁹ Will you never look away from me, or let me alone even for an instant? ²⁰ If I have sinned, what have I done to you, O watcher of all humanity? Why have you made me your target? Have I become a burden to you?
²¹ Why do you not pardon my offenses and forgive my sins? For I will soon lie down in the dust; you will search for me, but I will be no more."

chapters.title: Job 8
paragraphs: ¹ Then Bildad the Shuhite replied: ² "How long will you go on talking like this? Your words are a blustering wind. ³ Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty distort what is right? ⁴ When your children sinned against him, he gave them over to the penalty of their sin. ⁵ But if you seek God earnestly and plead with the Almighty,

⁶ if you are pure and upright, even now he will rouse himself on your behalf and restore you to your rightful place. ⁷ Your beginnings will seem humble, so prosperous will your future be. ⁸ Ask the former generation; pay attention to what their ancestors learned — ⁹ for we were born only yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow. ¹⁰ Will they not instruct you and tell you? Will they not bring forth words from their understanding?

¹¹ Can papyrus grow tall where there is no marsh? Can reeds thrive without water? ¹² While still growing and uncut, they wither more quickly than grass. ¹³ Such is the fate of all who forget God; so perishes the hope of the godless. ¹⁴ What they trust in is fragile; what they rely on is a spider's web. ¹⁵ They lean on the web, but it gives way; they cling to it, but it does not hold.

¹⁶ They are like a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden. ¹⁷ It entwines its roots around a pile of rocks and looks for a place among the stones. ¹⁸ But when it is torn from its spot, that place disowns it and says, 'I never saw you.' ¹⁹ Surely its life withers away, and from the soil other plants grow. ²⁰ Surely God does not reject one who is blameless, nor does he lend his support to the wicked.
²¹ He will yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy. ²² Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tents of the wicked will be no more."

chapters.title: Job 9
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job replied: ² "Yes, I know what you say is true — but how can mere mortals prove their innocence before God? ³ Though they wished to dispute with him, they could not answer him one time out of a thousand. ⁴ His wisdom is profound, his power is vast. Who has resisted him and come out unscathed? ⁵ He moves mountains without their knowing it and overturns them in his anger.

⁶ He shakes the earth from its place and makes its pillars tremble. ⁷ He speaks to the sun and it does not shine; he seals off the light of the stars. ⁸ He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea. ⁹ He made the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades and the constellations of the south. ¹⁰ He performs wonders that cannot be fathomed, miracles that cannot be counted.

¹¹ When he passes me, I cannot see him; when he goes by, I cannot perceive him. ¹² If he snatches something away, who can stop him? Who can say to him, 'What are you doing?' ¹³ God does not restrain his anger; even the allies of Rahab cowered at his feet. ¹⁴ How then can I dispute with him? How can I find words to argue with him? ¹⁵ Even if I were innocent, I could not answer him; I could only plead with my Judge for mercy.

¹⁶ Even if I summoned him and he responded, I do not believe he would give me a hearing. ¹⁷ He would crush me with a storm and multiply my wounds for no reason. ¹⁸ He would not let me catch my breath but would overwhelm me with misery. ¹⁹ If it is a matter of strength, he is mighty! And if it is a matter of justice, who can challenge him? ²⁰ Even if I were innocent, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would prove me guilty.

²¹ Although I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life. ²² It is all the same — that is why I say, 'He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.' ²³ When a plague brings sudden death, he mocks the despair of the innocent. ²⁴ When a land falls into the hands of the wicked, he blindfolds its judges. If it is not he, then who is it? ²⁵ My days are swifter than a runner; they flee away without a glimpse of joy.

²⁶ They are gone like swift ships, like an eagle diving on its prey. ²⁷ If I say, "I will put my grief aside, I will set down my sorrow and find some comfort" — ²⁸ I am terrified by all my suffering, for I know you will not clear me of guilt. ²⁹ If I am already condemned, why should I struggle for nothing? ³⁰ Even if I scrubbed myself with snow and cleansed my hands with lye, ³¹ you would plunge me into a pit, and my own clothes would recoil from me.

³² He is not a man like me, that I could answer him, that we could stand together before a court. ³³ There is no one to mediate between us, no one who could lay his hand on us both. ³⁴ Let him take his rod away from me, let his terror no longer overwhelm me — ³⁵ then I would speak without fear, for that is not how I am in myself.

chapters.title: Job 10
paragraphs: ¹ My soul is sick of life. I will pour out my complaint freely; I will speak from the bitterness of my soul. ² I will say to God, "Do not condemn me — show me why you are contending with me. ³ Does it please you to oppress me, to despise the work of your own hands, while you smile on the schemes of the wicked? ⁴ Do you see as a mortal sees? Do you look on things the way humans do? ⁵ Are your days like the days of a man, your years like a man's years,

⁶ that you must search out my sin and seek out my wrongdoing? ⁷ You know that I am not guilty, and no one can rescue me from your hand. ⁸ Your own hands shaped me and made me — and now you turn and destroy me? ⁹ Remember that you formed me like clay. Will you return me to dust? ¹⁰ Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?

¹¹ You clothed me with skin and flesh, you knit me together with bones and sinews. ¹² You gave me life and showed me steadfast love, and your care has preserved my spirit. ¹³ Yet these things you hid in your heart — I know this was your purpose all along. ¹⁴ If I sinned, you would be watching, and you would not let my guilt go unpunished. ¹⁵ If I am wicked, then woe to me; and even if I am righteous, I dare not lift my head — I am so filled with shame, soaked in my own misery.

¹⁶ And if I hold my head up, you hunt me like a fierce lion, and turn your power against me once more. ¹⁷ You bring fresh witnesses against me, and your anger toward me grows — blow after blow, wave after wave of assault. ¹⁸ Then why did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I had died before any eye had seen me, ¹⁹ that I had been carried from the womb to the grave, as though I had never existed. ²⁰ The few days of my life are almost spent — leave me alone, let me have a little comfort

²¹ before I go to the place I will never return from — the land of darkness and the shadow of death, ²² a land as dark as the darkness itself, where the shadow of death covers all, where there is no order, and where the light is as dark as night.

chapters.title: Job 11
paragraphs: ¹ Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said: ² "Should all these words go unanswered? Should a man who talks so much be proved right? ³ Should your empty words silence everyone? Should you mock, and no one call you out? ⁴ You claim your beliefs are sound, that you are pure in God's eyes. ⁵ But if only God would speak, if only he would open his lips against you,

⁶ and tell you the secrets of wisdom — for true wisdom has two sides. Know this: God is not even holding you fully accountable for all your wrongdoing. ⁷ Can you fathom the depths of God? Can you probe the limits of the Almighty? ⁸ They are higher than the heavens — what can you do? Deeper than the grave — what can you know? ⁹ Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea. ¹⁰ If he passes through and puts someone in prison, or calls a court to order, who can stop him?

¹¹ For he knows who is hollow — when he sees wickedness, does he not take note of it? ¹² An empty-headed person will no more become wise than a wild donkey's colt can be born human. ¹³ But if you set your heart right, and stretch out your hands to him — ¹⁴ if you put away the sin that is in your hands, and let no wrong dwell in your tent, ¹⁵ then you will be able to lift your face without shame; you will stand firm and without fear.

¹⁶ You will forget your misery; you will remember it only as water that has flowed past. ¹⁷ Your life will be brighter than noon; even the darkness will be like morning. ¹⁸ You will feel secure, because there is hope; you will look around and rest in safety. ¹⁹ You will lie down with no one to make you afraid, and many will come seeking your favor. ²⁰ But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and their escape will be cut off, and their hope will be nothing but their last breath."

chapters.title: Job 12
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job answered and said: ² "No doubt you are the people who matter, and wisdom will die with you. ³ But I have a mind as well as you — I am no less than you. Who does not know these things? ⁴ I have become a laughingstock to my friends — I, who called on God and he answered me, a just and blameless man who has become a laughingstock. ⁵ The one who is comfortable has contempt for misfortune — it is the fate of those whose feet are slipping.

⁶ The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke God live securely — those whom God has given everything they want. ⁷ But ask the animals, and they will teach you; ask the birds of the sky, and they will tell you; ⁸ ask the earth, and it will teach you; let the fish of the sea explain it to you. ⁹ Which of all these does not know that the hand of the Lord has done this? ¹⁰ In his hand is the life of every living creature, and the breath of all mankind.

¹¹ Does the ear not test words, just as the tongue tastes food? ¹² Wisdom belongs to the aged, and understanding to those who have lived long. ¹³ But with God are wisdom and power; he has both counsel and understanding. ¹⁴ What he tears down cannot be rebuilt; whoever he shuts in cannot get out. ¹⁵ If he holds back the waters, they dry up; if he unleashes them, they overwhelm the land.

¹⁶ With him are strength and sound wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver both belong to him. ¹⁷ He leads counselors away stripped bare, and makes fools of judges. ¹⁸ He breaks off the chains that kings put on others, and ties a loincloth around their own waists. ¹⁹ He leads priests away stripped bare, and overthrows those who have stood firm for ages. ²⁰ He silences the lips of trusted advisors, and takes away the discernment of the elders.

²¹ He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong. ²² He uncovers deep things from the darkness and brings into the light the shadow of death. ²³ He makes nations great, then destroys them; he enlarges nations, then drives them away. ²⁴ He strips the understanding away from the leaders of the nations and makes them wander in a trackless waste. ²⁵ They grope in the dark without light, and he makes them stagger like drunkards.

chapters.title: Job 13
paragraphs: ¹ All of this my eye has seen; my ear has heard and understood it. ² What you know, I know also — I am not less than you. ³ But I want to speak to the Almighty; I want to argue my case before God. ⁴ You, however, are smearing things with lies — you are worthless doctors, all of you. ⁵ If only you would keep silent — that would be your wisdom.

⁶ Hear now my argument; listen to the case I will make with my lips. ⁷ Will you speak falsely on God's behalf? Will you speak deceitfully for him? ⁸ Will you show him partiality? Will you make his case for him? ⁹ Will it go well when he examines you? Can you deceive him as one deceives a man? ¹⁰ He will surely rebuke you if you secretly show partiality.

¹¹ Will not his majesty strike terror into you? Will not the dread of him fall upon you? ¹² Your wise sayings are proverbs of ash; your defenses are defenses of clay. ¹³ Keep silent before me — let me speak, and let whatever comes, come. ¹⁴ Why should I put myself at risk and take my life into my own hands? ¹⁵ Even if he kills me, I will hope in him — I will still defend my ways to his face.

¹⁶ This very thing will be my salvation — that a godless person cannot come before him. ¹⁷ Listen carefully to my words; let my declaration ring in your ears. ¹⁸ I have set out my case — I know that I will be vindicated. ¹⁹ Who would bring charges against me? If anyone can, I will fall silent and die. ²⁰ Only grant me two things, O God, and then I will not hide myself from you:

²¹ withdraw your hand far from me, and let your terror no longer dismay me. ²² Then call out, and I will answer — or let me speak first, and you reply. ²³ How many wrongs and sins have I committed? Show me my offense; tell me my sin. ²⁴ Why do you hide your face and treat me as your enemy?

²⁶ For you write bitter things against me, and force me to inherit the sins of my youth. ²⁷ You put my feet in stocks; you stand watch over all my paths; you set a limit on the soles of my feet. ²⁸ And I, like a rotten thing, am wasting away — like a garment that moths have eaten.

chapters.title: Job 14
paragraphs: ¹ A person born of woman has few days and much trouble. ² They come up like a flower, then wither; they flee like a shadow and do not last. ³ Do you really open your eyes on such a person? Do you really bring me into judgment with you? ⁴ Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? No one. ⁵ A person's days are determined; you know the number of their months; you have set limits they cannot go beyond.

⁶ Look away from them and let them rest, until — like a hired worker — they have completed their day. ⁷ There is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its new shoots will keep coming. ⁸ Though its root grows old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil, ⁹ at the scent of water it will bud again and put out branches like a young plant. ¹⁰ But a person dies and lies still; they breathe their last, and then where are they?

¹¹ As water vanishes from a lake, and a river drains away and dries up, ¹² so a person lies down and does not rise again; until the heavens are no more, they will not awake, and they will not be roused from their sleep. ¹³ Oh, that you would hide me in the grave, that you would conceal me until your anger has passed, and set a time for me and then remember me! ¹⁴ If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard labor I would wait, hoping for my release.

¹⁶ For now you count my every step; you watch over my sin. ¹⁷ My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and you sew up my guilt. ¹⁸ Yet as a mountain crumbles away and falls, and as a rock shifts from its place, ¹⁹ as water wears away stones, as floods sweep away the topsoil of the ground — so you destroy a person's hope. ²⁰ You overpower them once and for all, and they are gone; you change their appearance and send them away.

²¹ Their children come to honor, and they do not know it; their children are brought low, and they do not see it. ²² Only this do they feel: their own body's pain; only this do they mourn: themselves.

chapters.title: Job 15
paragraphs: ¹ Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said: ² "Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge and fill himself up with the east wind? ³ Should he argue with useless talk, with words that do no good? ⁴ But you are undermining the fear of God and hindering devotion before him. ⁵ Your own guilt teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.

⁶ Your own mouth condemns you, not I — your own lips testify against you. ⁷ Were you the first person ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills? ⁸ Were you listening in on God's council? Do you have a monopoly on wisdom? ⁹ What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that we do not understand? ¹⁰ Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us — men older even than your father.

¹¹ Are God's consolations not enough for you? Is the word spoken gently to you not sufficient? ¹² Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash, ¹³ so that you turn your spirit against God and let such words pour from your mouth? ¹⁴ What is a mortal, that they should be clean? What is one born of woman, that they should be righteous? ¹⁵ If God puts no trust even in his holy ones, and even the heavens are not pure in his sight,

¹⁶ how much more corrupt and depraved is a person who drinks in evil like water! ¹⁷ I will show you — listen to me — and I will tell you what I have seen; ¹⁸ what wise men have declared without hiding, passed down from their fathers, ¹⁹ to whom the land was given while no stranger moved among them. ²⁰ The wicked are in torment all their days, and the years that have been stored up for the ruthless are few.

²¹ Terrifying sounds fill their ears; in the midst of peace, the destroyer comes upon them. ²² They do not believe they will return from darkness, and they are destined for the sword. ²³ They wander about, asking, "Where can I find bread?" — knowing that a day of darkness is ready at hand. ²⁴ Distress and anguish terrify them; they overpower them, like a king ready for battle.

²⁵ Because they have stretched out their hand against God and defied the Almighty, ²⁶ charging at him with a stiff neck, with the thick bosses of their shields — ²⁷ because they covered their face with fat and made their waist thick with flesh, ²⁸ they live in desolate cities, in houses that no one else inhabits, houses crumbling into ruins. ²⁹ They will no longer be rich; their wealth will not endure, and their possessions will not spread over the earth. ³⁰ They will not escape the darkness; flames will wither their shoots, and they will depart by the breath of God's mouth.

³¹ Let them not trust in emptiness and deceive themselves — emptiness will be their reward. ³² Their branch will wither before its time, and their shoots will not be green. ³³ They will be like a vine that shakes off its unripe grapes, like an olive tree casting off its blossoms. ³⁴ For the company of the godless will produce nothing, and fire will consume the tents of those who take bribes. ³⁵ They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb brings forth deception."

chapters.title: Job 16
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job answered and said: ² "I have heard all of this before. You are miserable comforters, every one of you. ³ Will your windy words never end? What is driving you to keep answering? ⁴ I could speak just as you do — if you were in my place, I could heap words together against you and shake my head at you. ⁵ I could strengthen you with my mouth and move my lips to ease your pain.

⁶ But when I speak, my pain is not relieved; and when I hold back, it does not leave me. ⁷ Surely he has worn me out now; he has made my whole community desolate. ⁸ He has shriveled me up — and this is evidence against me; my wasting body rises up and testifies to my face. ⁹ He tears me apart in his anger and hates me; he gnashes his teeth at me; my enemy pierces me with his eyes. ¹⁰ People gape at me with open mouths; they strike my cheek with contempt; they mass together against me.

¹¹ God has handed me over to the ungodly and thrown me into the hands of the wicked. ¹² I was living in peace, but he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and smashed me to pieces, then set me up as his target. ¹³ His archers surround me; he pierces my kidneys without mercy and pours out my bile on the ground. ¹⁴ He breaks through me, breach after breach; he charges at me like a warrior. ¹⁵ I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and buried my brow in the dust.

¹⁶ My face is red from weeping, and dark shadows ring my eyes — ¹⁷ though there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is sincere. ¹⁸ O earth, do not cover my blood; let my cry find no resting place. ¹⁹ Even now, my witness is in heaven; my advocate is on high. ²⁰ My friends scorn me, but my eyes pour out tears to God.
²¹ Oh, that someone would plead with God on behalf of a person, as one pleads for a friend! ²² For only a few years will pass before I go down the path from which I will not return.

chapters.title: Job 17
paragraphs: ¹ My spirit is broken; my days are snuffed out; the grave is waiting for me. ² I am surrounded by mockers — my eyes rest on their hostility. ³ Put up a pledge for me with yourself — who else is there to put up security for me? ⁴ For you have closed their minds to understanding; therefore you will not let them triumph.

⁶ He has made me a byword among the people; I have become someone people spit in the face of. ⁷ My eye has grown dim with grief, and all my limbs are like a shadow. ⁸ Upright people are appalled at this; the innocent are stirred up against the godless. ⁹ But the righteous hold to their path, and those with clean hands grow stronger.

¹¹ My days are past; my plans are torn apart, the very desires of my heart. ¹² They turn night into day, saying the light is near when darkness is all around me. ¹³ If my only hope is to go to the grave, if I have made my bed in the darkness, ¹⁴ if I have said to the pit, "You are my father," and to the worm, "You are my mother" and "my sister" — ¹⁵ where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?
¹⁶ Will hope go down with me to the gates of death? Will we descend together into the dust?

chapters.title: Job 18
paragraphs: ¹ Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said: ² "How long before you stop making speeches? Think carefully, and then we will speak. ³ Why do you treat us as animals — as stupid in your eyes? ⁴ You who tear yourself apart in your anger — shall the earth be abandoned for your sake? Shall rocks be moved from their place?

⁶ The light in his tent will grow dark, and the lamp beside him will be snuffed out. ⁷ His strong stride will falter, and his own schemes will bring him down. ⁸ His own feet throw him into a net; he walks right into the trap. ⁹ A snare catches him by the heel and holds him fast. ¹⁰ A noose is hidden in the ground for him, a trap lies across his path.

¹¹ Terrors beset him on every side and chase him at every step. ¹² Calamity is hungry for him, and disaster stands ready at his side. ¹³ Disease devours his skin; death's firstborn eats away his limbs. ¹⁴ He is torn from the security he trusted in and marched off to the king of terrors.

¹⁶ His roots will wither below, and his branches be cut off above. ¹⁷ His memory will vanish from the earth; no one will know his name in the streets. ¹⁸ He will be driven from light into darkness, chased out of the world. ¹⁹ He will leave no child, no descendant among his people, no survivor in the places where he lived. ²⁰ Those in the west will be appalled at his fate, and those in the east will be seized with horror.
²¹ Surely these are the dwellings of the wicked — this is the place of those who do not know God.

chapters.title: Job 19
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job answered and said, ² How long will you torment me and crush me with your words? ³ Ten times now you have reproached me — you are not ashamed to attack me like this. ⁴ And even if I have truly gone wrong, my error is my own concern. ⁵ If you want to make yourselves look important at my expense and use my humiliation as proof against me —

⁶ then know that it is God who has wronged me, who has cast his net around me. ⁷ I cry out, 'Violence!' but no one answers. I call for justice, but there is none. ⁸ He has walled off my path so I cannot pass, and covered my roads in darkness. ⁹ He has stripped me of my honor and taken the crown from my head. ¹⁰ He tears me down on every side until I am gone; he uproots my hope like a tree.

¹¹ His fury blazes against me; he counts me among his enemies. ¹² His troops advance together, building their siege ramp against me, encamping all around my tent. ¹³ He has driven my brothers far from me; everyone who knew me has turned away. ¹⁴ My relatives have abandoned me; my close friends have forgotten me. ¹⁵ The guests in my house and my serving women treat me as a stranger — I am a foreigner in their eyes.

¹⁶ I call my servant, but he does not answer — I must beg him with my own mouth. ¹⁷ My breath is repulsive to my wife; I am loathsome to my own family. ¹⁸ Even young children scorn me; when I get up, they mock me to my face. ¹⁹ All my closest friends detest me; those I loved have turned against me. ²⁰ My bones cling to my skin and my flesh, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.

²¹ Have pity on me, have pity on me, O my friends — for the hand of God has struck me. ²² Why do you pursue me as God does? Why are you never satisfied with my suffering? ²³ Oh, that my words were written down! Oh, that they were inscribed in a book! ²⁴ That with an iron pen and lead they were carved into rock forever! ²⁵ For I know that my Redeemer lives, and at the last he will stand upon the earth.

²⁶ And even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God — ²⁷ I will see him myself; my own eyes will behold him, and not a stranger's. How my heart aches within me! ²⁸ But if you say, 'How shall we pursue him?' and 'The root of the trouble lies in him' — ²⁹ then be afraid of the sword yourselves, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, so that you may know there is a judgment.

chapters.title: Job 20
paragraphs: ¹ Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said, ² My troubled thoughts urge me to reply — I am stirred within me. ³ I have heard a rebuke that dishonors me, and my understanding compels me to answer. ⁴ Surely you know how it has been from ancient times, since humans were first placed upon the earth — ⁵ that the triumph of the wicked is brief, and the joy of the godless lasts only a moment.

⁶ Though his greatness rises to the heavens and his head touches the clouds, ⁷ he will perish forever like his own dung. Those who once saw him will ask, 'Where has he gone?' ⁸ He will fly away like a dream and not be found; he will be chased off like a vision of the night. ⁹ The eye that saw him will see him no more; his own place will never look upon him again. ¹⁰ His children will beg from the poor; his own hands will give back his wealth.

¹¹ His bones are full of the sins of his youth, which will lie down with him in the dust. ¹² Though evil is sweet in his mouth, though he hides it under his tongue, ¹³ though he savors it and will not let it go, keeping it on his palate — ¹⁴ yet his food will turn sour in his stomach; it will become viper's venom inside him. ¹⁵ He has swallowed down riches and will vomit them up again; God will flush them out of his stomach.

¹⁶ He will suck the poison of serpents; the viper's tongue will kill him. ¹⁷ He will never see the rivers, the streams flowing with honey and cream. ¹⁸ He will give back what he worked for without enjoying it; he will gain no profit from his trade. ¹⁹ For he has oppressed the poor and left them with nothing; he has seized houses he did not build. ²⁰ He knew no rest in his greed; nothing he treasured could save him.

²¹ Nothing will be left for him to eat; his prosperity will not last. ²² In the midst of his plenty he will be in want — the full force of misery will come upon him. ²³ Just as he is filling his belly, God will unleash his burning anger upon him, raining it down on him in full force. ²⁴ He may flee from an iron weapon, but a bronze arrow will pierce him through. ²⁵ He pulls it out of his back, the gleaming point out of his liver — terrors overwhelm him.

²⁶ Total darkness is stored up for him; a fire that needs no fanning will consume him; what remains in his tent will be destroyed. ²⁷ The heavens will expose his guilt; the earth will rise up against him. ²⁸ The flood will sweep his house away; it will be carried off in the day of God's anger. ²⁹ Such is the fate God has laid up for the wicked — the inheritance appointed for them by God.

chapters.title: Job 21
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job answered and said, ² Listen carefully to what I am saying; let this be the comfort you offer me. ³ Bear with me while I speak, and after I have spoken, go ahead and mock. ⁴ Is my complaint directed at a human being? Should I not be impatient? ⁵ Look at me and be appalled — lay your hand over your mouth.

⁶ When I think about it I am terrified, and shuddering seizes my body. ⁷ Why do the wicked go on living, growing old and increasing in power? ⁸ They see their children established around them, their offspring before their very eyes. ⁹ Their homes are safe and free from fear; God's rod does not fall on them. ¹⁰ Their bulls breed without fail; their cows calve and do not miscarry.

¹¹ They send out their children like a flock; their little ones dance about. ¹² They sing to the tambourine and lyre and make merry at the sound of the flute. ¹³ They spend their days in prosperity and go down to the grave in peace. ¹⁴ Yet they say to God, 'Leave us alone! We don't want to know your ways. ¹⁵ What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain by praying to him?'

¹⁶ But their prosperity is not of their own doing — the counsel of the wicked is far from me. ¹⁷ How often does the lamp of the wicked go out? How often does disaster come upon them? How often does God mete out pain in his anger? ¹⁸ They are like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm. ¹⁹ You may say, 'God stores up a man's punishment for his children,' but let him repay the man himself, so he can know it. ²⁰ Let his own eyes see his ruin; let him drink of the Almighty's wrath.

²¹ For what does he care about his household after him, when his months are cut short? ²² Can anyone teach God knowledge, since he judges even those on high? ²³ One person dies in the fullness of his strength, completely secure and at ease, ²⁴ his body well nourished, the marrow of his bones moist. ²⁵ Another dies in bitterness of soul, never having tasted anything good.

²⁶ They lie down alike in the dust, and worms cover them both. ²⁷ I know exactly what you are thinking, and the schemes you devise against me. ²⁸ You say, 'Where is the great man's house? Where are the tents where the wicked lived?' ²⁹ Have you never questioned those who travel the roads? Have you not paid attention to their accounts? ³⁰ The wicked man is spared when disaster comes; he is delivered on the day of wrath.

³¹ Who will confront him to his face about his deeds? Who will repay him for what he has done? ³² He is carried to his grave, and watch is kept over his tomb. ³³ The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows after him, and those who went before him are beyond counting. ³⁴ So how can you offer me such empty comfort? Your answers are nothing but lies.

chapters.title: Job 22
paragraphs: ¹ Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said, ² Can a man be of any use to God? Can even the wisest person benefit him? ³ Does it please the Almighty when you are righteous? Does he gain anything if you make your ways blameless? ⁴ Is it out of reverence for you that he rebukes you and enters into judgment with you? ⁵ Is it not because your wickedness is great and your sins have no end?

⁶ For you have taken pledges from your brothers without cause and left the naked stripped of their clothing. ⁷ You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the hungry. ⁸ You handed the land over to the powerful and let the favored dwell in it. ⁹ You sent widows away empty-handed and crushed the arms of orphans. ¹⁰ That is why snares surround you, why sudden terror overwhelms you,

¹¹ why you cannot see through the darkness, and why a flood of water engulfs you. ¹² Is not God high in the heavens? See how lofty are the highest stars! ¹³ Yet you say, 'What does God know? Can he see through the thick darkness to judge? ¹⁴ Clouds are a curtain to him; he cannot see as he walks along the vault of heaven.' ¹⁵ Will you keep to the ancient path that the wicked have walked?

¹⁶ They were snatched away before their time, their foundations swept away by a flood. ¹⁷ They said to God, 'Leave us alone! What can the Almighty do to us?' ¹⁸ Yet it was he who filled their houses with good things — but I want nothing to do with the counsel of the wicked. ¹⁹ The righteous see their ruin and rejoice; the innocent mock them: ²⁰ 'Surely our enemies are destroyed, and fire has consumed what they left behind.'

²¹ Submit to God and be at peace with him; in this way prosperity will come to you. ²² Accept instruction from his mouth and store up his words in your heart. ²³ If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored — if you remove wickedness far from your tent. ²⁴ Throw your gold into the dust, your finest gold among the rocks of the ravines, ²⁵ and the Almighty himself will be your gold, your choicest silver.

²⁶ Then you will find your delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God. ²⁷ You will pray to him and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows to him. ²⁸ Whatever you decide will be done, and light will shine on your ways. ²⁹ When others are brought low, you will say, 'Lift them up!' and God will save the downcast. ³⁰ He will deliver even the guilty — he will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.

chapters.title: Job 23
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job answered and said, ² Even today my complaint is bitter; his hand is heavy despite my groaning. ³ Oh, that I knew where I might find him — that I could come before his seat of judgment! ⁴ I would lay out my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments. ⁵ I would learn what he would say to me and understand what he would tell me.

⁶ Would he plead against me with great power? No — he would surely hear me out. ⁷ There an upright person could reason with him, and I would be acquitted by my judge forever. ⁸ I go east, but he is not there; west, and I cannot find him. ⁹ When he is at work in the north, I catch no sight of him; when he turns south, I cannot see him. ¹⁰ But he knows the path I take — when he tests me, I will come out like gold.

¹¹ My feet have followed closely in his steps; I have kept to his way without turning aside. ¹² I have not departed from the command of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my daily bread. ¹³ But he is unchangeable — who can oppose him? He does whatever he pleases. ¹⁴ He carries out his decree against me, and he has many such plans in store. ¹⁵ That is why I am terrified in his presence; when I think on this, I am afraid of him.
¹⁶ God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has filled me with dread. ¹⁷ I have not been silenced by the darkness, nor by the thick darkness that covers my face.

chapters.title: Job 24
paragraphs: ¹ Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment? Why do those who know him never see his days of reckoning? ² There are those who move boundary stones; they steal flocks and pasture them for themselves. ³ They drive off the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow's ox as a pledge. ⁴ They shove the needy off the road; the poor of the land are all forced into hiding. ⁵ Like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go about their labor of scavenging food; the wasteland provides for their children.

⁶ They harvest grain in the fields of others; they glean in the vineyards of the wicked. ⁷ They spend the night naked, without clothing, and have no covering in the cold. ⁸ Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks with no shelter. ⁹ The fatherless child is snatched from the breast; the infant of the poor is taken as a pledge. ¹⁰ They go about naked, lacking clothing; hungry, they carry another man's sheaves.

¹¹ They press out oil among the olive terraces; they tread the winepresses while they themselves go thirsty. ¹² In the city the dying groan; the wounded cry out for help — but God charges no one with wrongdoing. ¹³ There are those who rebel against the light; they do not know its ways or stay in its paths. ¹⁴ The murderer rises before dawn to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief. ¹⁵ The eye of the adulterer watches for dusk; he thinks, 'No eye will see me,' and keeps his face covered.

¹⁶ In the dark they break into houses; by day they shut themselves in, wanting nothing to do with the light. ¹⁷ For deep darkness is their morning; they are friends with the terrors of the darkness. ¹⁸ He is swift as foam on the water; their portion of the land is cursed, and no one turns toward their vineyards. ¹⁹ As drought and heat snatch away the snow, so the grave takes away those who have sinned. ²⁰ The womb forgets them; the worm devours them; they are remembered no more. Wickedness is broken like a tree.

²¹ He preys on the childless woman who has no son and brings no good to the widow. ²² Yet God, by his power, drags away the mighty; they may rise, but no one can be sure of their life. ²³ Though God gives them security, they rest in it — yet his eyes are always on their ways. ²⁴ They are exalted for a little while, then they are gone — brought low, gathered up like everything else, cut down like heads of grain.

chapters.title: Job 25
paragraphs: ¹ Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said, ² Dominion and awe belong to God; he establishes peace in the heights of heaven. ³ Can his armies be counted? On whom does his light not rise? ⁴ How then can a human being be righteous before God? How can anyone born of a woman be pure? ⁵ Even the moon is not bright and the stars are not pure in his eyes —
⁶ how much less a human being, who is a maggot — a mortal, who is only a worm!

chapters.title: Job 26
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job answered and said, ² How you have helped the powerless! What strength you have given to the feeble arm! ³ What counsel you have offered to one without wisdom! What sound insight you have so abundantly declared! ⁴ To whom have you been speaking these words? And whose breath came out of your mouth?

⁶ The dead tremble beneath the waters, and so do those who dwell there. ⁷ He spreads out the northern skies over empty space; he hangs the earth over nothing. ⁸ He wraps up the waters in his clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their weight. ⁹ He covers the face of the full moon, spreading his clouds over it. ¹⁰ He marks out the horizon on the face of the waters as the boundary between light and darkness.

¹¹ The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke. ¹² By his power he stilled the sea; by his wisdom he struck down Rahab. ¹³ By his breath the skies became fair; his hand pierced the gliding serpent. ¹⁴ And these are only the outer fringes of his work — how faint a whisper we hear of him! Who can understand the thunder of his full power?

chapters.title: Job 27
paragraphs: ¹ And Job continued his discourse and said, ² As God lives — who has denied me justice, and the Almighty, who has embittered my soul — ³ as long as I have breath within me and the breath of God is in my nostrils, ⁴ my lips will not speak falsehood and my tongue will not utter deceit. ⁵ God forbid that I should agree with you — till I die I will not renounce my integrity.

⁶ I hold fast to my righteousness and will not let it go; my conscience does not reproach me for any of my days. ⁷ May my enemy be as the wicked, and my adversary as the unrighteous. ⁸ For what hope does the godless man have when he is cut off, when God takes away his life? ⁹ Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him? ¹⁰ Will he take delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at any time?

¹¹ I will teach you about the power of God; I will not hide what the Almighty has in store. ¹² You have all seen this yourselves — why then do you talk such empty nonsense? ¹³ This is the portion of a wicked man before God, the inheritance the Almighty gives to ruthless men: ¹⁴ If his children multiply, it is only for the sword; his offspring will never have enough to eat. ¹⁵ Those who survive him will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not mourn for them.

¹⁶ Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothing like clay, ¹⁷ what he stores up, the righteous will wear, and the innocent will divide his silver. ¹⁸ The house he builds is as flimsy as a moth's cocoon, like a shelter made by a watchman. ¹⁹ He lies down rich but will rise no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone. ²⁰ Terror overtakes him like a flood; a tempest snatches him away in the night.

²¹ The east wind carries him off and he is gone, sweeping him away from his place. ²² It hurls itself at him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power. ²³ People clap their hands at him and hiss him away from his place.

chapters.title: Job 28
paragraphs: ¹ Surely there are mines where silver is found, and places where gold is refined. ² Iron is smelted from the earth, and copper is poured from stone. ³ Miners push back the darkness, searching the deepest shafts — rock in the shadow of death. ⁴ They sink a shaft far from where people live, forgotten by those who walk above; they hang there, swaying away from the rest. ⁵ As for the earth — bread comes from its surface, but underneath it is churned up as if by fire.

⁶ Its rocks hold sapphires, and its dust is flecked with gold. ⁷ No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon's eye has ever seen it. ⁸ No proud beast has walked it, no lion has ever crossed it. ⁹ The miner reaches into the hardest rock and overturns mountains at the root. ¹⁰ He cuts channels through the stone; his eyes catch every gleaming thing.

¹¹ He dams up the streams so they don't trickle through, and brings hidden things into the light. ¹² But where can wisdom be found? Where does understanding dwell? ¹³ No living person knows what it is worth; it cannot be found in the land of the living. ¹⁴ The deep says, "It is not in me," and the sea says, "It is not with me." ¹⁵ It cannot be bought with gold, and no amount of silver can pay its price.

¹⁶ It cannot be weighed against the gold of Ophir, nor against precious onyx or sapphire. ¹⁷ Gold and glass cannot match it, nor can it be traded for vessels of fine gold. ¹⁸ Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies. ¹⁹ The topaz of Ethiopia cannot equal it, and it cannot be valued against pure gold. ²⁰ Where, then, does wisdom come from? Where does understanding live?

²¹ It is hidden from the eyes of every living creature, concealed even from the birds of the sky. ²² Destruction and Death say, "We have heard only rumors of it." ²³ God alone knows the way to it; only he knows where it dwells. ²⁴ For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under heaven. ²⁵ He determined the weight of the wind and measured out the waters.

²⁶ When he set a limit for the rain and marked a path for the thunderstorm, ²⁷ then he saw wisdom and examined it; he confirmed it and tested it thoroughly. ²⁸ And to humanity he said, "The fear of the LORD — that is wisdom. To turn away from evil is understanding."

chapters.title: Job 29
paragraphs: ¹ Job continued speaking. ² "How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me — ³ when his lamp shone above my head, and by his light I walked through darkness. ⁴ Those were the days of my prime, when God's friendship rested on my house, ⁵ when the Almighty was still with me and my children were all around me.

⁶ When my path ran thick with cream and the rock poured out rivers of olive oil. ⁷ When I walked out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square, ⁸ the young men saw me and stepped aside, and the elders rose to their feet. ⁹ The princes stopped talking and covered their mouths; ¹⁰ the voices of the nobles fell silent and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.

¹¹ Every ear that heard me praised me, and every eye that saw me gave witness in my favor. ¹² For I rescued the poor who cried out, and the fatherless who had no one to help. ¹³ The dying blessed me; I made the widow's heart sing for joy. ¹⁴ I put on righteousness like a garment, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my crown. ¹⁵ I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.

¹⁶ I was a father to the poor; I took up the case of the stranger I did not know. ¹⁷ I broke the fangs of the wicked and snatched the prey from their teeth. ¹⁸ I thought, 'I will die in my own house, my days as many as the grains of sand.' ¹⁹ My roots reached down to the water; the dew lay fresh on my branches all night. ²⁰ My glory was new in me, and the bow in my hand was always strong.

²¹ Men listened to me and waited; they held their silence at my counsel. ²² After I spoke they did not speak again; my words fell upon them like gentle rain. ²³ They waited for me as for rain, and opened their mouths as if drinking in the spring showers. ²⁴ If I smiled at them, they could hardly believe it; the light of my face was precious to them. ²⁵ I set their course and sat at their head; I lived among them like a king among his army, like one who comforts the grieving.

chapters.title: Job 30
paragraphs: ¹ "But now men younger than I mock me — men whose fathers I would not have trusted to guard my dogs. ² What good was the strength of their hands to me? They were men in whom all vigor had wasted away. ³ Gaunt with want and hunger, they gnawed the dry ground in the dark wastelands. ⁴ They picked saltwort from the bushes and dined on the roots of broom trees. ⁵ They were outcasts from the community — people shouted after them as after a thief.

⁶ They were driven to live in the gullies and ravines, in holes in the earth and among the rocks. ⁷ They brayed among the bushes and huddled together under the nettles. ⁸ They were senseless, nameless men, driven out of the land. ⁹ And now I have become their taunt, their byword. ¹⁰ They detest me and keep their distance, yet they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

¹¹ Now that God has unstrung me and brought me low, they have thrown off all restraint. ¹² On my right the mob rises up; they set traps for my feet and build their siege ramps against me. ¹³ They tear up my path; they advance to finish me off without anyone to stop them. ¹⁴ They rush in through a wide breach; they roll in amid the ruins. ¹⁵ Terrors crash over me; my dignity is swept away like the wind and my safety vanishes like a cloud.

¹⁶ And now my life drains away; days of suffering grip me. ¹⁷ At night my bones ache with pain that never sleeps; ¹⁸ in the grip of my sickness my garment is disfigured; it binds around me like the collar of my robe. ¹⁹ He has cast me into the mud; I have become like dust and ashes. ²⁰ I cry out to you, but you do not answer; I stand up, but you only stare at me.

²¹ You have turned on me without mercy; with the strength of your hand you attack me. ²² You snatch me up and drive me before the wind; you toss me about in the storm. ²³ I know you will bring me to my death — to the place appointed for everyone who lives. ²⁴ Yet surely no one raises a hand against the broken when they cry out for help in their ruin. ²⁵ Have I not wept for those in trouble? Was my heart not grieved for the poor?

²⁶ Yet when I looked for good, evil came; when I hoped for light, darkness fell. ²⁷ My heart churns without rest; days of suffering rise up to meet me. ²⁸ I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help. ²⁹ I am a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches. ³⁰ My skin has turned black and peeling; my bones burn with fever.
³¹ My harp is tuned to mourning, and my flute to the sound of weeping.

chapters.title: Job 31
paragraphs: ¹ "I made a covenant with my eyes — how then could I look with desire on a young woman? ² For what is God's portion from above, his inheritance from the Almighty on high? ³ Is it not ruin for the wicked and disaster for those who do evil? ⁴ Does he not see my ways and count every step I take? ⁵ If I have walked in falsehood or if my feet have rushed toward deceit —

⁶ then let God weigh me in honest scales and he will know my integrity. ⁷ If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, if any stain has clung to my hands, ⁸ then let me sow and another eat, and let my crops be uprooted. ⁹ If my heart has been seduced by a woman and I have lurked at my neighbor's door, ¹⁰ then let my wife be another man's slave, and let others sleep with her.

¹¹ For that would have been a wicked crime, an offense worthy of judgment. ¹² It is a fire that burns down to destruction and would consume everything I have planted. ¹³ If I have dismissed the claims of my servants when they brought a grievance against me, ¹⁴ what then will I do when God confronts me? What will I answer when he calls me to account? ¹⁵ Did not the one who made me make them too? Did not the same God form us both in the womb?

¹⁶ If I have denied what the poor desired, or let the widow's eyes grow dim with weeping, ¹⁷ if I have eaten my food alone without sharing it with the fatherless — ¹⁸ but from my youth I raised the orphan like a father, and from birth I guided the widow — ¹⁹ if I have watched someone die for lack of clothing, or left the poor without a coat to wear, ²⁰ and his back has not blessed me for the warmth of my wool —

²¹ if I have raised my hand against the fatherless, knowing that men stood by me in the gate, ²² then let my arm fall from my shoulder and be broken at the joint. ²³ For I dreaded calamity from God; I could not endure his majesty. ²⁴ If I have put my confidence in gold or said to pure gold, "You are my security" — ²⁵ if I rejoiced because my wealth was great or because my own hand had won so much —

²⁶ if I looked at the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor, ²⁷ and my heart was secretly enticed and my hand kissed my lips in worship — ²⁸ that too would have been an iniquity worthy of judgment, for I would have been unfaithful to God above. ²⁹ Have I rejoiced at my enemy's misfortune or gloated when disaster struck him? ³⁰ No — I never let my mouth sin by calling down a curse on him.

³¹ If the men of my household have never said, 'Who has not been filled by Job's generosity?' — ³² no stranger ever had to sleep in the street, for I opened my door to every traveler. ³³ If I have concealed my sin the way Adam did, hiding my guilt in my heart — ³⁴ if I have been so afraid of the crowd or so terrified of what people might think that I kept silent and stayed indoors — ³⁵ Oh, if only someone would listen to me! Here is my plea — let the Almighty answer me. Let my accuser put his charges in writing.

³⁶ I would carry that document on my shoulder; I would wear it like a crown. ³⁷ I would give him a full account of all my steps; I would approach him like a prince. ³⁸ If my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together, ³⁹ if I have eaten its harvest without payment or crushed the life out of those who worked it — ⁴⁰ then let thorns grow where wheat once grew and weeds where barley should stand. The words of Job are ended.

chapters.title: Job 32
paragraphs: ¹ So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes. ² But Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, burned with anger. He was furious with Job for justifying himself rather than God, ³ and angry with the three friends for failing to find an answer and yet condemning Job anyway. ⁴ Elihu had held back from speaking while they talked, because they were older than he. ⁵ But when he saw that the three had nothing more to say, his anger flared.

⁶ So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite said, "I am young, and you are very old; that is why I held back from telling you what I know. ⁷ I thought, 'Let age speak; let many years teach wisdom.' ⁸ But it is the spirit in a person, the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding. ⁹ The wise are not always old, nor do elders always understand what is just. ¹⁰ Therefore I say: Listen to me. I too will tell you what I know.

¹¹ I waited while you searched for the right words; I gave ear while you reasoned things through. ¹² I listened carefully — but not one of you proved Job wrong or answered what he said. ¹³ Do not say, 'We have found wisdom; let God refute him, not man.' ¹⁴ Job has not directed his words at me, and I will not answer him with your arguments. ¹⁵ They are dismayed; they have no more to say — words have left them entirely.

¹⁶ I have waited — and since they stand there in silence with nothing more to say, ¹⁷ I too will have my turn. I will say what I know. ¹⁸ For I am full of words; the spirit inside me compels me. ¹⁹ Inside I am like bottled wine with no outlet, like new wineskins about to burst. ²⁰ I must speak and find relief; I will open my lips and answer.
²¹ I will show no partiality to anyone; I will flatter no one. ²² For I do not know how to flatter — if I did, my Maker would soon take me away.

chapters.title: Job 33
paragraphs: ¹ "And now, Job, listen to my words; pay attention to everything I say. ² I have opened my mouth and the words are ready on my tongue. ³ My words come from an honest heart; my lips will speak only what I know to be true. ⁴ The spirit of God has made me; the breath of the Almighty has given me life. ⁵ If you can, answer me. Take your stand before me and speak.

⁶ Look, before God I am just as you are; I too was formed from clay. ⁷ You need not be frightened of me, and I will not come down hard on you. ⁸ But I have heard you speak with my own ears — I have heard the very words: ⁹ 'I am pure and without sin; I am innocent; there is no guilt in me. ¹⁰ Yet God has found fault with me; he treats me as his enemy.

¹¹ He has put my feet in chains; he watches every path I take.' ¹² But I tell you — in this you are not right. I will answer you: God is greater than any human being. ¹³ Why do you quarrel with him? He does not owe an account of all his actions. ¹⁴ For God speaks in one way, then another, and people do not always notice. ¹⁵ He speaks in dreams and visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, while they slumber in their beds.

¹⁶ Then he opens their ears and fills them with instruction, ¹⁷ turning them away from wrong and keeping pride at bay, ¹⁸ holding the soul back from the pit and keeping life from the sword. ¹⁹ Or a person may be chastened by suffering in bed, with constant pain in every bone, ²⁰ so that even food becomes revolting and every delicacy is loathsome.

²¹ His flesh wastes away until it cannot be seen, and his bones stand out, bare. ²² His soul draws close to the pit; his life to the agents of death. ²³ But if there is an angel at his side, one messenger among a thousand, to reveal to him what is right, ²⁴ then God shows mercy and says, 'Spare him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom.' ²⁵ His flesh becomes fresher than a child's; he returns to the days of his youth.

²⁶ He prays to God and finds favor; he sees God's face and shouts for joy, and God restores him to full standing. ²⁷ He goes before others and says, 'I sinned and twisted what was right, yet it did not profit me.' ²⁸ God has delivered him from going down into the pit, and he will see the light of life. ²⁹ Yes, God does all this — twice, even three times — with a person, ³⁰ to pull their soul back from the pit and let them live in the light.

³¹ "Pay attention, Job — listen to me; stay quiet, and I will speak. ³² If you have anything to say, then answer me; speak up, for I would love to see you vindicated. ³³ But if not, then listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom."

chapters.title: Job 34
paragraphs: ¹ Elihu continued, ² "Hear my words, you wise men; listen to me, you who know. ³ For the ear tests words just as the tongue tastes food. ⁴ Let us discern together what is right; let us learn among ourselves what is good. ⁵ For Job has said, 'I am innocent, and God has denied me justice.'

⁶ 'Should I lie about my rights? My wound is incurable though I have done nothing wrong.' ⁷ Is there another man like Job, who drinks up insults like water, ⁸ who keeps company with evildoers and walks in the way of the wicked? ⁹ For he says, 'A man gains nothing by trying to please God.' ¹⁰ So listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God to do evil, from the Almighty to commit wrong.

¹¹ He repays everyone for what they have done; he brings on each person what their conduct deserves. ¹² It is unthinkable that God would do wrong or that the Almighty would pervert justice. ¹³ Who put him in charge of the earth? Who appointed him over all creation? ¹⁴ If he chose to take back his spirit and breath, ¹⁵ every living thing would perish together, and humanity would return to dust.

¹⁶ "If you have any understanding, then hear this; listen to what I say. ¹⁷ Can a ruler who hates justice be in power? Will you condemn the one who is supremely just? ¹⁸ Is he not the one who says to kings, 'You are worthless,' and to nobles, 'You are wicked'? ¹⁹ How much less does he show favor to princes, or treat the rich better than the poor — for all of them are made by his hands. ²⁰ They die in an instant, in the middle of the night; the mighty are brought down — not by human hands.

²¹ For his eyes are on every person's path; he sees every step they take. ²² There is no darkness deep enough to hide the evildoer from him. ²³ He does not set a time for any person to come before him in judgment. ²⁴ Without inquiry he shatters the mighty and puts others in their place. ²⁵ He knows what they are doing; he sweeps them away in the night and they are crushed.

²⁶ He strikes them down for their wickedness, openly, in plain sight, ²⁷ because they turned away from following him and had no regard for any of his ways. ²⁸ They caused the cry of the poor to rise up to him, so that he heard the cry of the afflicted. ²⁹ When he is silent, who can condemn? When he hides his face, who can see him? Yet he governs both nations and individuals, ³⁰ to keep the godless from ruling and from ensnaring the people.

³¹ Suppose someone says to God, 'I have suffered punishment; I will sin no more. ³² Show me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.' ³³ Should God reward you on your terms, when you reject him? The choice belongs to you, not to me — so say what you know. ³⁴ Men of understanding will tell me, and every wise man who listens to me will agree: ³⁵ 'Job speaks without knowledge; his words have no insight.'
³⁶ I wish that Job would be tested to the limit for answering like a wicked man. ³⁷ For to his sin he adds rebellion; he defies us and speaks more and more against God."

chapters.title: Job 35
paragraphs: ¹ Elihu continued speaking: ² "Do you think it is right when you say, 'My righteousness is greater than God's'? ³ For you ask, 'What does it profit you?' and, 'What do I gain by not sinning?' ⁴ I will answer you, and your friends with you.

⁶ If you sin, what do you do against him? If your transgressions multiply, what does it mean to him? ⁷ If you are righteous, what do you give him? What does he receive from your hand? ⁸ Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself; your righteousness benefits only other human beings. ⁹ People cry out under the weight of oppression; they call for relief from the arm of the powerful. ¹⁰ But no one asks, 'Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

¹¹ who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?' ¹² There they cry out, but he gives no answer — because of the pride of evil men. ¹³ Surely God does not listen to empty cries; the Almighty pays no attention to them. ¹⁴ How much less when you say you cannot see him — yet your case lies before him, and you must wait for him. ¹⁵ And now, because his anger has not punished you, and he seems unaware of your great transgression,
¹⁶ Job opens his mouth with empty words; he piles up words without knowledge.

chapters.title: Job 36
paragraphs: ¹ Elihu went on and said: ² "Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to say on God's behalf. ³ I will draw my knowledge from afar, and ascribe righteousness to my Maker. ⁴ For truly my words are not false; one who is perfect in knowledge stands before you.

⁶ He does not keep the wicked alive, but gives justice to the afflicted. ⁷ He never takes his eyes off the righteous; he sets them on thrones with kings and exalts them forever. ⁸ But if they are bound in chains, caught in cords of affliction, ⁹ then he shows them their deeds — their sins of pride and arrogance. ¹⁰ He opens their ears to correction and commands them to turn from evil.

¹¹ If they obey and serve him, they live out their days in prosperity, their years in contentment. ¹² But if they refuse to listen, they die by the sword, they perish in their ignorance. ¹³ The godless in heart harbor resentment; they do not cry out when he binds them. ¹⁴ They die in their youth, their lives snuffed out among the male cult prostitutes. ¹⁵ But God delivers the afflicted through their affliction; he uses their suffering to open their ears.

¹⁶ He would have drawn you, too, out of the jaws of distress into a spacious place — a place of ease, where your table would overflow with rich food. ¹⁷ But you are filled with the sentence of the wicked; judgment and justice grip you. ¹⁸ Beware that anger does not lead you astray, and do not let a great ransom tempt you to act wrongly. ¹⁹ Will your wealth or all your powerful resources keep you from distress? ²⁰ Do not long for the night, when people vanish from their place.

²¹ Be careful — do not turn to iniquity, for you seem to have chosen this path over your affliction. ²² See how God is exalted in his power; what teacher is there like him? ²³ Who has appointed him his way? Who can say to him, 'You have done wrong'? ²⁴ Remember to extol his work, which people have sung about. ²⁵ All humanity has seen it; mortals gaze at it from afar.

²⁶ How great is God — beyond our knowing; the number of his years is past searching out! ²⁷ He draws up the water droplets; they distill as rain into the streams ²⁸ that the clouds pour down, drenching the multitudes of people. ²⁹ Who can understand how he spreads the clouds or how the thunder rolls from his dwelling? ³⁰ See how he scatters his lightning around him, bathing the depths of the sea in light.

³¹ By these things he governs the peoples; he provides food in abundance. ³² He fills his hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark. ³³ His thunder announces the coming storm; even the cattle sense its approach.

chapters.title: Job 37
paragraphs: ¹ At this, my heart pounds and leaps from its place. ² Listen — listen to the thunder of his voice, to the rumbling that rolls from his mouth. ³ He unleashes it across the whole sky; his lightning strikes to the ends of the earth. ⁴ After it his voice roars; he thunders with his majestic voice, and he does not hold back his bolts when his voice is heard. ⁵ God thunders with his voice marvelously; he does great things we cannot comprehend.

⁶ He says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth,' and to the shower of rain, 'Be a mighty downpour.' ⁷ He stops every person in their tracks, so that all people may know his work. ⁸ The animals find shelter and stay in their dens. ⁹ The storm sweeps in from the south; the cold comes from the driving north winds. ¹⁰ The breath of God produces ice, and the broad waters freeze solid.

¹¹ He loads the clouds with moisture; he scatters his lightning through them. ¹² They swirl around, guided by his purposes, doing all he commands over the face of the whole earth. ¹³ He brings the clouds either to punish the land, or to water it, or to show his love.

¹⁶ Do you know how the clouds are balanced — the wonderful work of him who is perfect in knowledge? ¹⁷ Do you know how your garments are warm when the earth lies still under the south wind? ¹⁸ Can you, with him, spread out the skies, hard as a mirror of polished bronze? ¹⁹ Tell us what we should say to him — we cannot argue our case because of our darkness. ²⁰ Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone dare to ask to be swallowed up?

²¹ No one can look at the light when it blazes in the skies after the wind has swept them clear. ²² Out of the north comes golden splendor; God is clothed in awesome majesty. ²³ The Almighty — we cannot find him; he is great in power. Justice and abundant righteousness he will not violate. ²⁴ Therefore people fear him; he does not regard any who are wise in their own eyes."

chapters.title: Job 38
paragraphs: ¹ Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said: ² "Who is this who darkens counsel with words devoid of knowledge? ³ Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you will answer me. ⁴ Where were you when I laid the earth's foundations? Tell me, if you know so much. ⁵ Who determined its dimensions? Surely you know! Who stretched a measuring line across it?

⁶ On what were its foundations set, or who laid its cornerstone — ⁷ while the morning stars sang together and all the angels shouted for joy? ⁸ Who shut the sea behind its doors when it burst from the womb, ⁹ when I made the clouds its garment and wrapped it in thick darkness, ¹⁰ when I fixed its limits and set its doors and bars in place?

¹¹ And said, 'This far you may come and no farther; here is where your proud waves halt'? ¹² Have you ever commanded the morning, or shown the dawn its place, ¹³ so that it could take hold of the earth's edges and shake the wicked out of it? ¹⁴ The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its features stand out like folds of a garment. ¹⁵ Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.

¹⁶ Have you walked in the recesses of the deep, or explored the springs of the sea? ¹⁷ Have the gates of death been shown to you? Have you seen the gates of the deepest darkness? ¹⁸ Have you comprehended the vast expanse of the earth? Tell me, if you know all this. ¹⁹ What is the way to the dwelling of light? And where does darkness reside? ²⁰ Can you take them to their places? Do you know the paths to their homes?

²¹ Surely you know — you were already born! How many years have you lived? ²² Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or seen the armories of hail, ²³ which I reserve for times of trouble, for days of war and battle? ²⁴ What is the way to the place where lightning is dispersed, or the place where the east wind is scattered over the earth?

²⁶ to send rain on a land where no one lives, on a wilderness where there is no human being, ²⁷ to satisfy a desolate wasteland and make it burst into green life? ²⁸ Does the rain have a father? Who fathers the drops of dew? ²⁹ From whose womb comes the ice? Who gives birth to the frost from the heavens ³⁰ when the waters grow hard as stone, and the surface of the deep is frozen?

³¹ Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades? Can you loosen Orion's belt? ³² Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons, or lead out the Bear with its cubs? ³³ Do you know the laws of heaven? Can you impose them on the earth? ³⁴ Can you raise your voice to the clouds and make a flood of water cover you? ³⁵ Can you send lightning bolts on their way? Will they report back to you, 'Here we are'?

³⁶ Who gave wisdom to the heart, or understanding to the mind? ³⁷ Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Who can tip over the water jars of the heavens ³⁸ when the dust becomes hard as iron and the clods of earth stick together? ³⁹ Can you hunt prey for the lioness and satisfy the hunger of the lions ⁴⁰ when they crouch in their dens, or lie in wait in their lairs?
⁴¹ Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God, wandering about for lack of food?

chapters.title: Job 39
paragraphs: ¹ "Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the deer brings forth her fawn? ² Do you count the months till they give birth? Do you know the time when they drop their young? ³ They crouch, they deliver their young, they are rid of their labor pains. ⁴ Their young grow strong and thrive in the wild; they leave and do not return.

⁶ I made the wilderness his home, the barren salt flats his dwelling. ⁷ He laughs at the commotion of the city; he hears no shouts from the driver. ⁸ He roams the hills as his pasture and searches for any green thing. ⁹ Will the wild ox agree to serve you? Will it spend the night beside your manger? ¹⁰ Can you hold it to the furrow with a harness? Will it plow the valleys behind you?

¹¹ Will you rely on it for its great strength? Will you leave your heavy work to it? ¹² Can you trust it to haul in your grain and bring it to your threshing floor? ¹³ The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, but are they like the feathers of the stork or falcon? ¹⁴ She lays her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand, ¹⁵ unmindful that a foot may crush them, or that some wild animal may trample them.

¹⁶ She treats her young harshly, as if they were not hers; she does not care if her labor was in vain — ¹⁷ for God has made her forget wisdom; he has given her no share of understanding. ¹⁸ Yet when she rises and spreads her wings, she laughs at horse and rider. ¹⁹ Have you given the horse its strength? Have you clothed its neck with a flowing mane? ²⁰ Can you make it leap like a locust? Its proud snorting is terrifying!

²¹ It paws the ground in the valley, exulting in its strength; it charges into battle. ²² It laughs at fear and is not frightened; it does not shy away from the sword. ²³ The quiver rattles against its side, the flashing spear and javelin. ²⁴ With fierce energy it devours the ground; it cannot stand still when the battle trumpet sounds. ²⁵ At each blast of the horn it snorts, 'Aha!' It catches the scent of battle from afar, the thunder of commanders and the battle cry.

²⁶ Is it by your wisdom that the hawk takes flight and spreads its wings toward the south? ²⁷ Does the eagle soar at your command and build its nest on high? ²⁸ It dwells on the rocky crag, on the steep face of rock and cliff. ²⁹ From there it hunts for food; its eyes scan the distant horizon. ³⁰ Its young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there it is."

chapters.title: Job 40
paragraphs: ¹ The LORD said to Job: ² "Will the one who argues with the Almighty correct him? Let the one who accuses God give him an answer." ³ Then Job replied to the LORD: ⁴ "I am unworthy — how can I reply to you? I put my hand over my mouth. ⁵ I spoke once, but I have no answer; twice, but I will say no more."

⁶ Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind: ⁷ "Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you will answer me. ⁸ Would you discredit my justice? Would you condemn me to justify yourself? ⁹ Do you have an arm like God's? Can your voice thunder like his? ¹⁰ Then adorn yourself with glory and splendor; clothe yourself with honor and majesty.

¹¹ Unleash the fury of your wrath; look at all who are proud and bring them low. ¹² Look at all who are proud and humble them; crush the wicked where they stand. ¹³ Bury them all in the dust together; shroud their faces in the grave. ¹⁴ Then I myself will admit to you that your own right hand can save you.

¹⁶ Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you — it feeds on grass like an ox. ¹⁷ What power it has in its loins, what strength in the muscles of its belly! ¹⁸ Its tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of its thighs are tightly knit. ¹⁹ Its bones are like beams of bronze; its limbs like rods of iron. ²⁰ It is the chief of God's works; yet its Maker can approach it with his sword.

²¹ It lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds in the marsh. ²² The lotuses conceal it in their shadow; the poplars along the stream surround it. ²³ When the river rages, it is not alarmed; it remains calm though the Jordan rushes against its mouth. ²⁴ Can anyone capture it by the eyes, or trap it and pierce its nose?

chapters.title: Job 41
paragraphs: ¹ "Can you pull in Leviathan with a fishhook, or tie down its tongue with a rope? ² Can you put a cord through its nose, or pierce its jaw with a hook? ³ Will it keep begging you for mercy? Will it speak gentle words to you? ⁴ Will it make a covenant with you to become your servant for life? ⁵ Can you make it a pet like a bird, or put it on a leash for your girls?

⁶ Will a band of merchants try to buy it? Will they divide it up among the traders? ⁷ Can you fill its hide with harpoons, or its head with fishing spears? ⁸ Lay your hand on it — you will remember the battle and never do it again! ⁹ Look — the hope of attacking it is futile; even the sight of it is overwhelming.

¹¹ Who dares oppose me and come out alive? Everything under heaven is mine. ¹² I will not fail to speak of Leviathan's limbs, its strength, and its graceful proportions. ¹³ Who can strip off its outer coat? Who can penetrate its double coat of armor? ¹⁴ Who can open the doors of its mouth, ringed with fearsome teeth? ¹⁵ Its back has rows of shields locked tightly together as with a seal.

¹⁶ Each is so close to the next that no air can pass between them. ¹⁷ They are joined to one another; they lock together and cannot be pulled apart. ¹⁸ Its snorting flashes with light; its eyes are like the glimmer of dawn. ¹⁹ Flames stream from its mouth; sparks of fire shoot out. ²⁰ Smoke pours from its nostrils as from a boiling pot heated over rushes.

²¹ Its breath sets coals ablaze; flames dart from its mouth. ²² Strength lodges in its neck; dismay goes before it. ²³ The folds of its flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable. ²⁴ Its chest is hard as rock, hard as a lower millstone. ²⁵ When it rises up, the mighty are terrified; they fall back before its thrashing.

²⁶ The sword that strikes it cannot hold; nor can spear, dart, or javelin. ²⁷ Iron it treats like straw and bronze like rotten wood. ²⁸ Arrows do not make it flee; slingstones are like chaff to it. ²⁹ A club seems to it a piece of straw; it laughs at the rattling of the lance. ³⁰ Its underside is jagged shards; it moves across the mud like a threshing sledge.
