¹⁶ None of the sins they have committed will be remembered against them. They have done what is just and right; they will surely live. ¹⁷ Yet your people say, 'The way of the Lord is not just.' But it is their way that is not just. ¹⁸ If a righteous person turns from their righteousness and does evil, they will die for it. ¹⁹ And if a wicked person turns away from their wickedness and does what is just and right, they will live by doing so. ²⁰ Yet you say, 'The way of the Lord is not just.' I will judge each of you according to your own ways, people of Israel.

²¹ In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month on the fifth day, a man who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me and said, "The city has fallen!" ²² Now the evening before the man arrived, the hand of the LORD was on me, and he opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning. My mouth was opened and I was no longer silent. ²³ Then the word of the LORD came to me: ²⁴ "Son of man, the people living in those ruins in the land of Israel are saying, 'Abraham was only one man, yet he possessed the land. But we are many; surely the land has been given to us as our possession.' ²⁵ Therefore say to them: This is what the Sovereign LORD says: Since you eat meat with the blood still in it and look to your idols and shed blood, should you then possess the land?

²⁶ You rely on your sword, you do detestable things, and each of you defiles his neighbor's wife. Should you then possess the land? ²⁷ Say this to them: This is what the Sovereign LORD says — as surely as I live, those who are in the ruins will fall by the sword; those in the open country I will give to the wild animals to be devoured; and those in strongholds and caves will die of a plague. ²⁸ I will make the land desolate and her proud strength will come to an end, and the mountains of Israel will become so desolate that no one will cross them. ²⁹ Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I have made the land a desolate waste because of all the detestable things they have done. ³⁰ Son of man, your people are talking together about you by the walls and at the doors of the houses, saying to each other, 'Come and hear the message that has come from the LORD.'

³¹ My people come to you, as they usually do, and sit before you to hear your words, but they do not put them into practice. Their mouths speak of love, but their hearts are greedy for unjust gain. ³² Indeed, to them you are nothing more than one who sings love songs with a beautiful voice and plays an instrument well, for they hear your words but do not put them into practice. ³³ When all this comes true — and it surely will — then they will know that a prophet has been among them.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 34
paragraphs: ¹ The word of the LORD came to me: ² "Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel; prophesy and say to them: This is what the Sovereign LORD says: Woe to you shepherds of Israel who only take care of yourselves! Should not shepherds take care of the flock? ³ You eat the curds, clothe yourselves with the wool, and slaughter the choice animals, but you do not take care of the flock. ⁴ You have not strengthened the weak or healed the sick or bound up the injured. You have not brought back the strays or searched for the lost. You have ruled them harshly and brutally. ⁵ So they were scattered because there was no shepherd, and when they were scattered they became food for all the wild animals.

⁶ My sheep wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill. They were scattered over the whole earth, and no one searched or looked for them. ⁷ Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD: ⁸ As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign LORD, because my flock lacks a shepherd and so has been plundered and has become food for all the wild animals, and because my shepherds did not search for my flock but cared for themselves rather than for my flock, ⁹ therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD: ¹⁰ This is what the Sovereign LORD says: I am against the shepherds and will hold them accountable for my flock. I will remove them from tending the flock so that the shepherds can no longer feed themselves. I will rescue my flock from their mouths, and it will no longer be food for them.

¹¹ For this is what the Sovereign LORD says: I myself will search for my sheep and look after them. ¹² As a shepherd looks after his scattered flock when he is with them, so will I look after my sheep. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of clouds and darkness. ¹³ I will bring them out from the nations and gather them from the countries, and I will bring them into their own land. I will pasture them on the mountains of Israel, in the ravines and in all the settlements in the land. ¹⁴ I will tend them in a good pasture, and the mountain heights of Israel will be their grazing land. There they will lie down in good grazing land, and there they will feed in a rich pasture on the mountains of Israel. ¹⁵ I myself will tend my sheep and have them lie down, declares the Sovereign LORD.

¹⁶ I will search for the lost and bring back the strays. I will bind up the injured and strengthen the weak, but the sleek and the strong I will destroy. I will shepherd the flock with justice. ¹⁷ As for you, my flock, this is what the Sovereign LORD says: I will judge between one sheep and another, and between rams and goats. ¹⁸ Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture? Must you also trample the rest of your pasture with your feet? Is it not enough for you to drink clear water? Must you also muddy the rest with your feet? ¹⁹ Must my flock feed on what you have trampled and drink what you have muddied with your feet? ²⁰ Therefore this is what the Sovereign LORD says to them: I will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep.

²¹ Because you shove with flank and shoulder, butting all the weak sheep with your horns until you have driven them away, ²² I will save my flock, and they will no longer be plundered. I will judge between one sheep and another. ²³ I will place over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he will tend them; he will tend them and be their shepherd. ²⁴ I the LORD will be their God, and my servant David will be a prince among them. I the LORD have spoken. ²⁵ I will make a covenant of peace with them and rid the land of savage beasts so that they may live in the wilderness and sleep in the forests in safety.

²⁶ I will make them and the places surrounding my hill a blessing. I will send down showers in season; there will be showers of blessing. ²⁷ The trees will yield their fruit and the ground will yield its crops; the people will be secure in their land. They will know that I am the LORD, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hands of those who enslaved them. ²⁸ They will no longer be plundered by the nations, nor will wild animals devour them. They will live in safety, and no one will make them afraid. ²⁹ I will provide for them a land renowned for its crops, and they will no longer be victims of famine in the land or bear the scorn of the nations. ³⁰ Then they will know that I, the LORD their God, am with them and that they, the people of Israel, are my people, declares the Sovereign LORD.
³¹ You are my sheep, the sheep of my pasture, and I am your God, declares the Sovereign LORD.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 35
paragraphs: ¹ The word of the LORD came to me: ² "Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir and prophesy against it. ³ Say to it: This is what the Sovereign LORD says: I am against you, Mount Seir, and I will stretch out my hand against you and make you a desolate waste. ⁴ I will turn your towns into ruins and you will be desolate. Then you will know that I am the LORD. ⁵ Because you harbored an ancient hostility and delivered the Israelites over to the sword at the time of their calamity, the time their punishment reached its climax,

⁶ therefore as surely as I live, declares the Sovereign LORD, I will give you over to bloodshed and it will pursue you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will pursue you. ⁷ I will make Mount Seir a desolate waste and cut off from it all who come and go. ⁸ I will fill your mountains with the slain; those killed by the sword will fall on your hills and in your valleys and in all your ravines. ⁹ I will make you desolate forever; your towns will not be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the LORD. ¹⁰ Because you said, 'These two nations and countries will be ours and we will take possession of them,' even though I the LORD was there,

¹¹ therefore as surely as I live, declares the Sovereign LORD, I will treat you in accordance with the anger and jealousy you showed in your hatred of them and I will make myself known among them when I judge you. ¹² Then you will know that I the LORD have heard all the contemptible things you have said against the mountains of Israel. You said, 'They have been laid waste and have been given over to us to devour.' ¹³ You boasted against me and spoke against me without restraint, and I heard it. ¹⁴ This is what the Sovereign LORD says: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate. ¹⁵ Because you rejoiced when the inheritance of Israel became desolate, that is how I will treat you. You will be desolate, Mount Seir, you and all of Edom. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 36
paragraphs: ¹ "Son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel and say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD. ² This is what the Sovereign LORD says: The enemy said of you, 'Aha! The ancient heights have become our possession.' ³ Therefore prophesy and say: This is what the Sovereign LORD says: Because they ravaged and crushed you from every side so that you became the possession of the rest of the nations and the object of people's malicious talk and slander, ⁴ therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Sovereign LORD: This is what the Sovereign LORD says to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, to the desolate ruins and the deserted towns that have been plundered and ridiculed by the rest of the nations around you — ⁵ this is what the Sovereign LORD says: In my burning zeal I have spoken against the rest of the nations, and against all of Edom, for with glee and with malice in their hearts they made my land their own possession so that they might plunder its pastureland.

⁶ Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel and say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: This is what the Sovereign LORD says: I speak in my jealous wrath because you have suffered the scorn of the nations. ⁷ Therefore this is what the Sovereign LORD says: I swear with uplifted hand that the nations around you will also suffer scorn. ⁸ But you, mountains of Israel, will produce branches and fruit for my people Israel, for they will soon come home. ⁹ I am concerned for you and will look on you with favor; you will be plowed and sown, ¹⁰ and I will multiply the people upon you — yes, all of Israel. The towns will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt.

¹¹ I will increase the number of people and animals living on you, and they will be fruitful and become numerous. I will settle people on you as in the past and will make you prosper more than before. Then you will know that I am the LORD. ¹² I will cause people, my people Israel, to live on you. They will possess you, and you will be their inheritance; you will never again deprive them of their children. ¹³ This is what the Sovereign LORD says: Because people say to you, 'You devour people and deprive your nation of its children,' ¹⁴ therefore you will no longer devour people or make your nation childless, declares the Sovereign LORD. ¹⁵ No longer will I make you hear the taunts of the nations, and no longer will you suffer the scorn of the peoples or cause your nation to fall, declares the Sovereign LORD.

¹⁶ The word of the LORD came to me: ¹⁷ "Son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own land, they defiled it by their conduct and their actions. Their conduct was like a woman's monthly uncleanness in my sight. ¹⁸ So I poured out my wrath on them because of the blood they had shed in the land and because they had defiled it with their idols. ¹⁹ I dispersed them among the nations, and they were scattered through the countries; I judged them according to their conduct and their actions. ²⁰ And wherever they went among the nations they profaned my holy name, for it was said of them, 'These are the LORD's people, and yet they had to leave his land.'

²¹ I had concern for my holy name, which the people of Israel had profaned among the nations where they had gone. ²² Therefore say to the Israelites: This is what the Sovereign LORD says — it is not for your sake, people of Israel, that I am going to do these things, but for the sake of my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations where you have gone. ²³ I will show the holiness of my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, the name you have profaned among them. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Sovereign LORD, when I am proved holy through you before their eyes. ²⁴ For I will take you out of the nations; I will gather you from all the countries and bring you back into your own land. ²⁵ I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean; I will cleanse you from all your impurities and from all your idols.

²⁶ I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in you; I will remove from you your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh. ²⁷ And I will put my Spirit in you and move you to follow my decrees and be careful to keep my laws. ²⁸ Then you will live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God. ²⁹ I will save you from all your uncleanness. I will call for the grain and make it plentiful and will not bring famine upon you. ³⁰ I will increase the fruit of the trees and the crops of the field, so that you will no longer suffer disgrace among the nations because of famine.

³¹ Then you will remember your evil ways and wicked deeds, and you will loathe yourselves for your sins and detestable practices. ³² I want you to know that I am not doing this for your sake, declares the Sovereign LORD. Be ashamed and disgraced for your conduct, people of Israel! ³³ This is what the Sovereign LORD says: On the day I cleanse you from all your sins, I will resettle your towns, and the ruins will be rebuilt. ³⁴ The desolate land will be cultivated instead of lying desolate in the sight of all who pass through it. ³⁵ They will say, 'This land that was laid waste has become like the garden of Eden; the cities that were lying in ruins, desolate and destroyed, are now fortified and inhabited.'

³⁶ Then the nations around you that remain will know that I the LORD have rebuilt what was destroyed and have replanted what was desolate. I the LORD have spoken, and I will do it. ³⁷ This is what the Sovereign LORD says: Once again I will yield to Israel's plea and do this for them: I will make their people as numerous as sheep, ³⁸ as numerous as the flocks for offerings at Jerusalem during her appointed festivals. So will the ruined cities be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 37
paragraphs: ¹ The hand of the LORD was on me, and he brought me out by the Spirit of the LORD and set me in the middle of a valley; it was full of bones. ² He led me back and forth among them, and I saw a great many bones on the floor of the valley — bones that were very dry. ³ He asked me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" I said, "Sovereign LORD, you alone know." ⁴ Then he said to me, "Prophesy to these bones and say to them, 'Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD! ⁵ This is what the Sovereign LORD says to these bones: I will make breath enter you, and you will come to life.

⁶ I will attach tendons to you and make flesh come upon you and cover you with skin; I will put breath in you, and you will come to life. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'" ⁷ So I prophesied as I was commanded. And as I was prophesying, there was a noise, a rattling sound, and the bones came together, bone to bone. ⁸ I looked, and tendons and flesh appeared on them and skin covered them, but there was no breath in them. ⁹ Then he said to me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to it, 'This is what the Sovereign LORD says: Come, breath, from the four winds and breathe into these slain, that they may live.'" ¹⁰ So I prophesied as he commanded me, and breath entered them; they came to life and stood up on their feet — a vast army.

¹¹ Then he said to me: "Son of man, these bones are the people of Israel. They say, 'Our bones are dried up and our hope is gone; we are cut off.' ¹² Therefore prophesy and say to them: This is what the Sovereign LORD says: My people, I am going to open your graves and bring you up from them; I will bring you back to the land of Israel. ¹³ Then you, my people, will know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up from them. ¹⁴ I will put my Spirit in you and you will live, and I will settle you in your own land. Then you will know that I the LORD have spoken, and I have done it, declares the LORD." ¹⁵ The word of the LORD came to me:

¹⁶ "Son of man, take one stick and write on it, 'For Judah and the Israelites associated with him.' Then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph — the stick of Ephraim — and all the house of Israel associated with him.' ¹⁷ Join them together into one stick so they become one in your hand. ¹⁸ When your people ask you, 'Won't you explain to us what you mean by this?' ¹⁹ tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim's hand, along with the tribes of Israel associated with him, and join it to the stick of Judah. I will make them one stick, and they will be one in my hand. ²⁰ Hold before their eyes the sticks you have written on.

²¹ Tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: I am going to take the Israelites from among the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from every side and bring them back to their own land. ²² I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. One king will rule all of them, and they will never again be two nations or divided into two kingdoms. ²³ They will no longer defile themselves with their idols, their detestable practices, or any of their rebellions. I will save them from all the places where they have sinned, and I will cleanse them. They will be my people, and I will be their God. ²⁴ My servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd. They will follow my laws and keep my decrees and observe them. ²⁵ They will live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob, the land where your ancestors lived. They will live there — they, their children, and their children's children — forever. And my servant David will be their prince forever.

²⁶ I will make a covenant of peace with them — an everlasting covenant. I will establish them, multiply them, and set my sanctuary among them forever. ²⁷ My dwelling place will be with them. I will be their God, and they will be my people. ²⁸ Then the nations will know that I the LORD make Israel holy, when my sanctuary stands among them forever.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 38
paragraphs: ¹ The word of the LORD came to me: ² "Son of man, turn your face against Gog, of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him. ³ Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. ⁴ I will turn you around and put hooks in your jaws, and I will bring you out with your whole army — horses and horsemen, all fully armed, a great company with shields and bucklers, all wielding swords — ⁵ with Persia, Cush, and Put among them, all with shields and helmets.

⁶ Also Gomer with all its troops, and Beth-togarmah from the far north with all its troops — and many other peoples with you. ⁷ Get ready; be prepared, you and all the companies gathered around you, and take command of them. ⁸ After many days you will be summoned. In later years you will come against a land recovered from war, a people gathered from many nations to the mountains of Israel, which had long been desolate. These people have been brought out from the nations, and now all of them are living safely. ⁹ You will advance, coming on like a storm — you and all your troops and many other peoples with you, like a cloud covering the land. ¹⁰ This is what the Lord GOD says: On that day, thoughts will come to your mind, and you will devise an evil plan.

¹¹ You will say, "I will march against a land of unwalled villages; I will attack those who are at peace and living in safety — people with no walls, no bars, no gates — ¹² to plunder and loot, to turn your hand against the resettled ruins and against the people gathered from the nations, who now have cattle and goods and live at the center of the land." ¹³ Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish, with all its young lions, will ask you: "Have you come to plunder? Have you assembled your forces to loot, to make off with silver and gold, to take away cattle and goods, to seize a great spoil?" ¹⁴ Therefore, son of man, prophesy and say to Gog: This is what the Lord GOD says: On that day when my people Israel are living safely, will you not take notice? ¹⁵ You will come from your place in the far north, you and many peoples with you — all of them riding horses, a vast army, a mighty force.

¹⁶ You will advance against my people Israel like a cloud covering the land. In the last days this will happen, and I will bring you against my land so that the nations may know me, when I demonstrate my holiness through you before their eyes, O Gog. ¹⁷ This is what the Lord GOD says: Are you the one I spoke of in earlier times through my servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied for years that I would bring you against them? ¹⁸ On that day, when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, my fierce anger will flare up. ¹⁹ In my zeal and fiery wrath I declare that on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel. ²⁰ The fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the beasts of the field, every creature that moves along the ground, and all the people on the face of the earth will tremble at my presence. The mountains will be overturned, the cliffs will crumble, and every wall will fall to the ground.

²¹ I will summon a sword against Gog on all my mountains, declares the Lord GOD. Every man's sword will be turned against his brother. ²² I will punish him with plague and with bloodshed. I will pour down torrents of rain, hailstones, and burning sulfur on him and his troops and on the many nations with him. ²³ In this way I will show my greatness and my holiness, and I will make myself known in the sight of many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 39
paragraphs: ¹ "Son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. ² I will turn you around and drag you along. I will bring you from the far north and send you against the mountains of Israel. ³ I will strike your bow from your left hand and make your arrows drop from your right hand. ⁴ On the mountains of Israel you will fall, you and all your troops and the nations with you. I will give you as food to all kinds of carnivorous birds and to the wild animals. ⁵ You will fall in the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.

⁶ I will send fire on Magog and on those who live in safety in the coastlands, and they will know that I am the LORD. ⁷ I will make my holy name known among my people Israel. I will not let my holy name be profaned anymore. Then the nations will know that I the LORD am the Holy One in Israel. ⁸ It is coming! It will happen, declares the Lord GOD. This is the day I have spoken of. ⁹ Then those who live in the towns of Israel will go out and use the weapons for fuel — the shields and bucklers, the bows and arrows, the war clubs and spears — and they will make fires with them for seven years. ¹⁰ They will not need to gather wood from the fields or cut it from the forests, because they will use the weapons for fuel. They will plunder those who plundered them and loot those who looted them, declares the Lord GOD.

¹¹ On that day I will give Gog a burial place in Israel — the valley of those who travel east of the sea. It will block the path of travelers, because Gog and all his multitude will be buried there. It will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog. ¹² For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land. ¹³ All the people of the land will help with the burial, and it will bring them honor on the day I am glorified, declares the Lord GOD. ¹⁴ They will appoint men to continually search the land and bury any remains left on the ground, in order to cleanse it. After seven months, they will begin the search. ¹⁵ As those who travel through the land survey it, whenever someone sees a human bone, they will set up a marker beside it until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.

¹⁶ A town called Hamonah will also be there. In this way they will cleanse the land. ¹⁷ And you, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: Speak to every kind of bird and to all the wild animals: "Assemble and come together from all around for the sacrifice I am making for you — a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel. There you will eat flesh and drink blood. ¹⁸ You will eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of the princes of the earth — the rams, lambs, goats, and bulls — all of them fattened animals from Bashan. ¹⁹ At my sacrifice, which I will prepare for you, you will eat fat until you are full and drink blood until you are drunk. ²⁰ At my table you will fill yourselves with horses and riders, with mighty men and all kinds of warriors, declares the Lord GOD."

²¹ I will display my glory among the nations, and all the nations will witness my judgment that I execute and my hand that I lay upon them. ²² From that day forward, the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God. ²³ And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile because of their sin — because they were unfaithful to me, I hid my face from them and handed them over to their enemies, and they all fell by the sword. ²⁴ I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and their rebellions, and I hid my face from them. ²⁵ Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be zealous for my holy name.

²⁶ They will forget their shame and all the unfaithfulness they showed toward me when they lived securely in their land with no one to frighten them. ²⁷ When I have brought them back from the peoples and gathered them out of the lands of their enemies, I will be shown holy through them in the sight of many nations. ²⁸ Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, who sent them into exile among the nations, and who gathered them back to their own land. I will not leave any of them behind. ²⁹ I will no longer hide my face from them, for I will pour out my Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 40
paragraphs: ¹ In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month — in the fourteenth year after the city fell — on that very day the hand of the LORD was upon me and he brought me there. ² In visions of God he brought me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain, on whose south side there was a structure that looked like a city. ³ He brought me there, and I saw a man whose appearance was like bronze. He stood at the gate, holding a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand. ⁴ The man said to me, "Son of man, look carefully and listen closely, and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for that is why you have been brought here. Report everything you see to the house of Israel." ⁵ I saw a wall completely surrounding the outside of the temple. The measuring rod in the man's hand was six long cubits, each cubit being a cubit and a handwidth. He measured the thickness of the wall — one rod — and its height — one rod.

⁶ Then he went to the gate that faces east. He climbed its steps and measured the threshold of the gate — one rod wide — and the other threshold — also one rod wide. ⁷ Each alcove was one rod long and one rod wide, with a space of five cubits between the alcoves. The gate threshold near the gate's inner porch was one rod deep. ⁸ He also measured the inner porch of the gate — one rod. ⁹ Then he measured the porch of the gate — eight cubits — and its jambs — two cubits. The gate porch faced inward. ¹⁰ On each side of the east gate were three alcoves. The three on each side were the same size, and the jambs on either side were the same size.

¹¹ He measured the width of the gate entrance — ten cubits — and the total length of the gateway — thirteen cubits. ¹² In front of each alcove was a ledge one cubit wide on each side. Each alcove was six cubits on one side and six cubits on the other. ¹³ He measured the gateway from the top of the rear wall of one alcove to the top of the opposite one — a width of twenty-five cubits from opening to opening. ¹⁴ He measured the jambs — sixty cubits tall — up to the courtyard all around the gate. ¹⁵ From the front of the entrance gateway to the front of the inner porch was fifty cubits.

¹⁶ The alcoves and their jambs had narrow windows all around the inside of the gateway, and the porticos also had windows all around the inside. Palm trees decorated the jambs. ¹⁷ Then he brought me into the outer court. I saw rooms and a pavement that had been made all around the court. Thirty rooms faced onto the pavement. ¹⁸ The pavement on both sides of the gates was as wide as the gates were long — this was the lower pavement. ¹⁹ Then he measured the distance from the front of the lower gateway to the front of the inner court — a hundred cubits on the east side and on the north side. ²⁰ The gate of the outer court that faced north — he measured its length and width.

²¹ It had three alcoves on each side, with jambs and porticos of the same measurements as the first gate — fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ²² Its windows, porticos, and palm trees were the same dimensions as those of the east gate. You went up seven steps to reach it, and its portico faced you as you approached. ²³ There was a gate to the inner court facing the north gate, just as there was one facing the east gate. He measured the distance from gate to gate — a hundred cubits. ²⁴ Then he led me to the south side, where I saw a gate facing south. He measured its jambs and porticos — they had the same dimensions as the others. ²⁵ The gate and its porticos had windows all around, like the previous windows — fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.

²⁶ Seven steps led up to it, and its portico faced the approach, with a palm tree on each side of the jambs. ²⁷ The inner court also had a gate facing south. He measured from that gate to the outer south gate — a hundred cubits. ²⁸ Then he brought me into the inner court through the south gate and measured it — it had the same measurements as the others. ²⁹ Its alcoves, jambs, and porticos all had the same dimensions, with windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ³⁰ The porticos all around were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.

³¹ Its porticos faced the outer court, and palm trees adorned the jambs. Eight steps led up to it. ³² He brought me to the inner court on the east side and measured the gate — it had the same dimensions as the others. ³³ Its alcoves, jambs, and porticos had the same measurements, and it had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ³⁴ Its porticos faced the outer court, with palm trees on both sides of the jambs. Eight steps led up to it. ³⁵ He brought me to the north gate and measured it — it had the same dimensions as the others.

³⁶ Its alcoves, jambs, and porticos were all there, with windows all around. The gate was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ³⁷ Its jambs faced the outer court, and palm trees were on both sides of them. Eight steps led up to it. ³⁸ A room with a doorway opened onto the gateway porticos, where the burnt offerings were washed. ³⁹ Inside the gateway portico there were two tables on each side, where the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings were slaughtered. ⁴⁰ By the outer wall near the north gateway steps were two tables, and on the other side of the porch were two more tables.

⁴¹ So there were four tables inside the gateway and four outside — eight tables in all, on which the sacrifices were slaughtered. ⁴² There were also four tables of dressed stone for the burnt offerings, each one and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one cubit high. The instruments used to slaughter the burnt offerings and other sacrifices were laid on these. ⁴³ Double hooks, each a handbreadth long, were fastened all around the inside walls, and the flesh of the offerings lay on the tables. ⁴⁴ Outside the inner gate, within the inner court, there were two rooms — one beside the north gate facing south, and one beside the east gate facing north. ⁴⁵ He said to me, "The room facing south is for the priests who have charge of the temple.

⁴⁶ The room facing north is for the priests who have charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who are the Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before him." ⁴⁷ He measured the inner court — a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, a perfect square. The altar stood in front of the temple. ⁴⁸ He brought me to the portico of the temple and measured the jambs of the portico — five cubits on each side. The gateway was fourteen cubits wide, with shoulders of three cubits on each side. ⁴⁹ The portico was twenty cubits wide and twelve cubits deep, with ten steps leading up to it, and pillars beside the jambs on both sides.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 41
paragraphs: ¹ Then he brought me to the main hall and measured the doorposts — six cubits wide on each side — the width of the tabernacle. ² The entrance was ten cubits wide, and its side walls were five cubits on each side. He measured the hall — forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. ³ Then he went into the inner room and measured the doorpost — two cubits. The entrance was six cubits wide, and the walls on each side of the entrance were seven cubits. ⁴ He then measured the length — twenty cubits — and the width — twenty cubits — in front of the main hall. He said to me, "This is the Most Holy Place." ⁵ He measured the outer wall of the temple — six cubits thick. The side rooms all around the temple were four cubits wide.

⁶ The side rooms were arranged in three stories, one above another, thirty rooms on each level. There were ledges built into the outer wall of the temple all around to serve as supports for the side rooms, so the supports were not embedded in the temple wall. ⁷ The side rooms became wider as they went higher, since the temple was surrounded by a winding passage that narrowed toward the top. The width of the side rooms increased from the lowest level upward, with the middle level being wider than the lowest and the upper level being wider than the middle. ⁸ I saw that the temple had a raised platform all around. The foundation of the side rooms was a full rod — six cubits — high. ⁹ The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick, and the open area between the side rooms and the inner rooms ¹⁰ was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.

¹¹ The side rooms had doorways opening onto the open area — one doorway facing north and one facing south. The open area was five cubits wide all around. ¹² The building facing the temple courtyard on the west side was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and the building itself was ninety cubits long. ¹³ Then he measured the temple — it was a hundred cubits long. The temple courtyard and the building with its walls were also a hundred cubits long. ¹⁴ The width of the temple facing east, including the courtyard, was a hundred cubits. ¹⁵ He measured the length of the building on the west side, facing the temple courtyard, including its galleries on both sides — a hundred cubits — along with the inner temple and the porticos of the court.

¹⁶ The doorposts, the narrow windows, and the three-story galleries all around — from the ground to the windows, which were covered — the interior from the ground up to the windows was paneled with wood all around. ¹⁷ The space above the outer doorway leading into the inner room, and the walls all the way around inside and outside, were laid out by measurement. ¹⁸ The wall was decorated with carved cherubim and palm trees alternating — a palm tree between each pair of cherubim. Each cherub had two faces: ¹⁹ a human face turned toward the palm tree on one side and the face of a young lion turned toward the palm tree on the other side. These carvings were all around the interior of the temple. ²⁰ From the floor to above the entrance, the walls were decorated with cherubim and palm trees.

²¹ The doorposts of the main hall were squared, and the front of the sanctuary had the same appearance. ²² The wooden altar was three cubits high and two cubits long. It had corners, and its base and sides were of wood. He said to me, "This is the table that stands before the LORD." ²³ Both the main hall and the sanctuary had double doors. ²⁴ Each door had two folding panels — two leaves for each door. ²⁵ The doors of the main hall were carved with cherubim and palm trees, just like those on the walls. Outside, in front of the portico, there was a wooden overhang.
²⁶ There were narrow windows and palm trees on both sides of the portico, on the side walls of the temple, and on the overhangs.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 42
paragraphs: ¹ Then he led me out to the outer court by way of the north and brought me to the rooms that were across from the courtyard and from the outer wall on the north side. ² The building to the north was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide. ³ Facing the twenty-cubit inner court and the outer-court pavement, the galleries ran opposite each other at three levels. ⁴ In front of the rooms was a walkway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long, with their doorways on the north. ⁵ The upper rooms were narrower, because the galleries took more space from them than from the rooms on the lower and middle floors.

⁶ These upper rooms had no pillars like the pillars in the courts, so they were smaller than the lower and middle rooms, going back from the ground level. ⁷ The outer wall ran parallel to the rooms toward the outer court for fifty cubits. ⁸ while the row of rooms facing the outer court was fifty cubits long, and those facing the temple were a hundred cubits long. ⁹ Below the lower rooms was an entrance on the east side as one approached them from the outer court. ¹⁰ Where the outer court wall began, there were rooms along its south side, facing the temple courtyard and the outer wall.

¹¹ There was a walkway in front of them like the walkway of the rooms on the north. Their length and width were the same, and their exits and arrangements were the same. The south rooms were entered the same way as the north rooms — ¹² from the east, at the front of the passage where the inner wall begins. ¹³ Then he said to me, "The north and south rooms facing the temple courtyard are the holy rooms where the priests who approach the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will deposit the most holy offerings — the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings — for the place is holy. ¹⁴ Once the priests have entered, they shall not go out from the holy area into the outer court without first removing the garments in which they minister, for those garments are holy. They shall put on other clothes before approaching the areas open to the people." ¹⁵ When he had finished measuring the inside of the temple area, he led me out through the east gate and measured all around.

¹⁶ He measured the east side with the measuring rod — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ¹⁷ He measured the north side — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ¹⁸ He measured the south side — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ¹⁹ He turned and measured the west side — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ²⁰ He measured the wall on all four sides. It was five hundred cubits long and five hundred cubits wide, creating a separation between what was holy and what was common.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 43
paragraphs: ¹ Then he led me to the gate — the gate facing east. ² And there was the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the roar of rushing waters, and the land was radiant with his glory. ³ The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when he came to destroy the city, and like the vision I had seen by the Chebar River. I fell facedown. ⁴ The glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east. ⁵ The Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.

⁶ I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple, while the man was standing beside me. ⁷ He said to me, "Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place for the soles of my feet. This is where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel will never again defile my holy name — neither they nor their kings — by their prostitution and by the corpses of their kings at their high places. ⁸ When they placed their threshold next to my threshold and their doorpost beside my doorpost, with only a wall between us, they defiled my holy name by their detestable practices. So I destroyed them in my anger. ⁹ Now let them put away their prostitution and the corpses of their kings far from me, and I will dwell among them forever. ¹⁰ You, son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, so they may be ashamed of their sins. Let them study its design.

¹¹ If they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the design of the temple — its arrangement, its exits and entrances, its entire design, and all its regulations and instructions. Write it down in their presence so they may faithfully follow its entire design and all its decrees. ¹² This is the law of the temple: all the surrounding area on top of the mountain is most holy. This is the law of the temple. ¹³ These are the measurements of the altar in cubits — the cubit being a standard cubit plus a handwidth: the base is one cubit high and one cubit wide, with a rim of one span around the edge. This is the base of the altar. ¹⁴ From the base at ground level up to the lower ledge is two cubits high and one cubit wide. From the smaller ledge up to the larger ledge is four cubits high and one cubit wide. ¹⁵ The altar hearth is four cubits high, with four horns projecting upward from the hearth.

¹⁶ The altar hearth is twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide — a perfect square. ¹⁷ The upper ledge is fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide, also square, with a rim of half a cubit and a surrounding channel of one cubit. The steps face east." ¹⁸ Then he said to me, "Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: These are the regulations for the altar when it is built, for sacrificing burnt offerings and splashing blood on it. ¹⁹ You are to give to the Levitical priests of the family of Zadok, who come near to minister before me, declares the Lord GOD, a young bull as a sin offering. ²⁰ You shall take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, the four corners of the upper ledge, and the surrounding rim. In this way you will cleanse it and make atonement for it.

²¹ Take the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the designated part of the temple grounds, outside the sanctuary. ²² On the second day offer a male goat without defect as a sin offering. Cleanse the altar as you cleansed it with the bull. ²³ When you have finished the purification, offer a young bull without defect and a ram from the flock without defect. ²⁴ Present them before the LORD, and the priests shall sprinkle salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD. ²⁵ For seven days you shall prepare a goat for a sin offering each day, as well as a young bull and a ram from the flock — all without defect.

²⁶ For seven days they shall purify the altar and consecrate it, and so dedicate it. ²⁷ When these days are over, then from the eighth day onward the priests shall offer on the altar your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings. I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 44
paragraphs: ¹ Then he brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary facing east, and it was shut. ² The LORD said to me, "This gate is to remain shut. It must not be opened; no one may enter through it. It is to remain shut because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it. ³ The prince himself is the only one who may sit in the gateway to eat in the presence of the LORD. He is to enter by way of the portico of the gateway and go out the same way." ⁴ Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the temple. I looked, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple, and I fell facedown. ⁵ The LORD said to me, "Son of man, pay close attention and look carefully and listen closely to everything I tell you concerning all the regulations and instructions regarding the temple of the LORD. Pay close attention to the entrance of the temple and all the exits of the sanctuary.

⁶ Say to the rebellious house of Israel: This is what the Lord GOD says: Enough of your detestable practices, house of Israel! ⁷ When you brought in foreigners — uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in body — to be in my sanctuary, you desecrated it. While you were offering me food, fat, and blood, they broke my covenant with all your detestable practices. ⁸ Instead of carrying out your duty regarding my holy things, you appointed them to keep charge of my sanctuary for you. ⁹ This is what the Lord GOD says: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and body, shall enter my sanctuary — not even the foreigners who live among the Israelites. ¹⁰ As for the Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray, straying after their idols, they must bear the consequences of their sin.

¹¹ They may serve in my sanctuary as gatekeepers and as workers in the temple. They may slaughter the burnt offerings and other sacrifices for the people and stand before the people to serve them. ¹² But because they served the people before their idols and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel, therefore I swore against them with an uplifted hand, declares the Lord GOD, and they must bear the consequences of their sin. ¹³ They shall not approach me to serve as priests or come near any of my holy things or my most holy offerings. They must bear their shame and the consequences of the detestable things they have done. ¹⁴ Yet I will appoint them to guard the temple and carry out all its maintenance and all the work that is to be done in it. ¹⁵ But the Levitical priests, who are descendants of Zadok and who guarded my sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from me, shall come near to minister before me. They shall stand in my presence to offer me fat and blood, declares the Lord GOD.

¹⁶ They are the ones who shall enter my sanctuary and come near to my table to minister before me. They shall keep my charge. ¹⁷ When they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall wear linen garments. They shall wear no wool while ministering at the gates of the inner court or inside it. ¹⁸ They shall wear linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments around their waists. They shall not wear anything that causes sweat. ¹⁹ When they go out into the outer court to the people, they shall take off the garments in which they were ministering and leave them in the holy rooms. Then they shall put on other clothes so they do not consecrate the people by means of their garments. ²⁰ They shall not shave their heads or let their hair grow long, but shall keep their hair trimmed.

²¹ No priest shall drink wine before entering the inner court. ²² They shall not marry widows or divorced women; they may only marry virgins from the Israelite community or widows of priests. ²³ They shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and show them how to distinguish between the unclean and the clean. ²⁴ When there is a dispute, they shall serve as judges and decide it according to my ordinances. They shall keep my laws and my statutes regarding all my appointed feasts, and they shall keep my Sabbaths holy. ²⁵ A priest shall not make himself ceremonially unclean by going near a dead person. However, he may defile himself for a father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or an unmarried sister.

²⁶ After a priest is cleansed, he must wait seven more days. ²⁷ On the day he enters the inner court of the sanctuary to minister there, he shall offer a sin offering for himself, declares the Lord GOD. ²⁸ The priests shall have no land of their own in Israel — I am their inheritance. You are not to give them any property in Israel; I am their possession. ²⁹ They shall eat the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings. Everything devoted to God in Israel will belong to them. ³⁰ The first of all the firstfruits and all the special contributions of every kind shall belong to the priests. You shall also give the priests the first portion of your ground grain, so that a blessing may rest on your household.
³¹ The priests shall not eat anything — whether bird or animal — that has died naturally or been torn by wild animals.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 45
paragraphs: ¹ "When you divide the land by lot as an inheritance, you shall set apart a sacred portion of the land for the LORD. It shall be twenty-five thousand cubits long and twenty thousand cubits wide, and this entire area shall be holy. ² From this area a section of five hundred by five hundred square cubits shall be set apart for the sanctuary, with fifty cubits of open land around it. ³ From the sacred portion you shall measure off a section twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand cubits wide. In it shall be the sanctuary — the Most Holy Place. ⁴ This sacred portion of the land shall belong to the priests who minister in the sanctuary, who approach the LORD to minister. It shall be a place for their houses as well as a holy area for the sanctuary. ⁵ A section twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand cubits wide shall belong to the Levites who minister in the temple, as their possession for towns to live in.

⁶ Alongside the sacred portion you shall give to the city an area five thousand cubits wide and twenty-five thousand cubits long. It shall belong to the whole house of Israel. ⁷ The prince shall have land on both sides of the sacred portion and the city property — extending westward from the west side and eastward from the east side, running lengthwise alongside one of the tribal portions from the western to the eastern border. ⁸ This will be his land in Israel. My princes shall no longer oppress my people but shall let the house of Israel have the land according to their tribes. ⁹ This is what the Lord GOD says: Enough, you princes of Israel! Stop your violence and oppression. Do what is just and right. Stop seizing my people's property, declares the Lord GOD. ¹⁰ You shall use honest scales, an honest ephah, and an honest bath.

¹¹ The ephah and the bath shall be the same size, with the bath holding one-tenth of a homer and the ephah one-tenth of a homer. The homer shall be the standard unit of measure. ¹² The shekel shall consist of twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels shall make up one mina for you. ¹³ This is the special contribution you are to offer: one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley. ¹⁴ The portion of olive oil — measured by the bath — shall be one-tenth of a bath from each cor, which is ten baths or one homer, since ten baths equal one homer. ¹⁵ One sheep out of every flock of two hundred, from the well-watered pastures of Israel — these are for grain offerings, burnt offerings, and fellowship offerings, to make atonement for the people, declares the Lord GOD.

¹⁶ All the people of the land shall contribute to this offering for the prince of Israel. ¹⁷ The prince's duty will be to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at the festivals, the New Moons, and the Sabbaths — at all the appointed festivals of the house of Israel. He shall provide the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings, and fellowship offerings to make atonement for the house of Israel. ¹⁸ This is what the Lord GOD says: On the first day of the first month you shall take an unblemished young bull and purify the sanctuary. ¹⁹ The priest shall take some of the blood from the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the upper ledge of the altar, and on the posts of the inner court gate. ²⁰ You shall do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins unintentionally or through ignorance. In this way you shall make atonement for the temple.

²¹ In the first month, on the fourteenth day, you shall celebrate the Passover — a festival of seven days with unleavened bread. ²² On that day the prince shall provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land. ²³ Throughout the seven days of the festival, he shall provide seven bulls and seven rams without defect as a daily burnt offering to the LORD, along with a male goat each day as a sin offering. ²⁴ He shall provide as a grain offering an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, along with a hin of oil for each ephah. ²⁵ In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day, he shall do the same at the seven-day festival — providing the same sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and oil.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 46
paragraphs: ¹ This is what the Lord GOD says: The gate of the inner court facing east shall be closed for the six working days, but on the Sabbath it shall be opened, and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened. ² The prince shall enter from outside through the portico of the gateway and stand at the gatepost. The priests shall sacrifice his burnt offering and fellowship offerings. He shall worship at the threshold of the gate and then go out. But the gate shall not be closed until evening. ³ In the same way, the people of the land shall also worship before the LORD at the entrance of that gateway on the Sabbaths and New Moons. ⁴ The burnt offering the prince brings to the LORD on the Sabbath shall be six lambs without defect and one ram without defect. ⁵ The grain offering shall be one ephah with the ram, and the grain offering with the lambs shall be as much as he wishes to give, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.

⁶ On the day of the New Moon the offering shall be a young bull without defect, six lambs, and a ram — all without defect. ⁷ He shall provide a grain offering of one ephah with the bull, one ephah with the ram, and as much as he can afford with the lambs, along with a hin of oil for each ephah. ⁸ When the prince enters, he shall go in through the portico of the gateway, and he shall leave the same way. ⁹ When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to worship shall go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate shall go out by the north gate. No one shall return through the gate by which he entered, but shall leave by the opposite gate. ¹⁰ When the people go in, the prince shall go in with them, and when they go out, he shall go out.

¹¹ At the festivals and appointed feasts the grain offering shall be one ephah with a bull, one ephah with a ram, and as much as the prince wishes with the lambs, along with a hin of oil for each ephah. ¹² Whenever the prince provides a voluntary burnt offering or voluntary fellowship offerings to the LORD, the east gate shall be opened for him. He shall offer his burnt offering and his fellowship offerings just as he does on the Sabbath. Then he shall go out, and after he leaves, the gate shall be closed. ¹³ Each morning you shall provide an unblemished one-year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the LORD. ¹⁴ You shall also provide a grain offering each morning — one-sixth of an ephah and one-third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour. This is a lasting ordinance — a perpetual grain offering to the LORD. ¹⁵ So the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil shall be provided every morning as a regular burnt offering.

¹⁶ This is what the Lord GOD says: If the prince gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his sons, it belongs to that son. It is his property by inheritance. ¹⁷ But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, the servant may keep it only until the year of freedom; then it reverts to the prince. His inheritance belongs to his sons alone. ¹⁸ The prince must not take any of the people's inheritance by forcing them out of their property. He shall give his sons their inheritance from his own property, so that none of my people will be separated from their property." ¹⁹ Then he brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate into the holy rooms facing north that belong to the priests. I saw that there was a space at the far western end. ²⁰ He said to me, "This is the place where the priests will boil the guilt offerings and sin offerings, and where they will bake the grain offerings, so they do not have to bring them into the outer court and risk consecrating the people."

²¹ Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me past the four corners of the court. I saw that in each corner of the outer court there was another enclosed court. ²² Each of these corner courts was forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. All four corner courts were the same size. ²³ Around the inside of each of these courts ran a ledge of stone, with cooking hearths built under the ledge all around. ²⁴ He said to me, "These are the kitchens where the temple servants will cook the sacrifices of the people."

chapters.title: Ezekiel 47
paragraphs: ¹ He brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and I saw water flowing out from under the threshold of the temple toward the east — for the temple faced east. The water flowed down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar. ² He led me out through the north gate and brought me around to the outer gate that faces east. There I saw water trickling from the south side of the gate. ³ As the man went east with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off a thousand cubits and led me through water that was ankle-deep. ⁴ He measured off another thousand cubits and led me through water that was knee-deep. He measured off another thousand and led me through water that was waist-deep. ⁵ He measured off another thousand, but now it was a river that I could not cross, because the water had risen and was deep enough to swim in — a river no one could cross.

⁶ He asked me, "Son of man, do you see this?" Then he brought me back to the bank of the river. ⁷ When I arrived there, I saw a great number of trees on each side of the river. ⁸ He said to me, "This water flows toward the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah, where it enters the Dead Sea. When it empties into the sea, the salty water there becomes fresh. ⁹ Swarms of living creatures will live wherever the river flows. There will be large numbers of fish, because this water flows there and makes the salt water fresh. Wherever the river flows, everything will live. ¹⁰ Fishermen will stand along the shore from En-gedi to En-eglaim. There will be places for spreading nets. The fish will be of many kinds — like the fish of the Mediterranean Sea — very numerous.

¹¹ But the swamps and marshes will not become fresh — they will remain salty. ¹² Fruit trees of all kinds will grow on both banks of the river. Their leaves will not wither, and their fruit will not fail. Every month they will bear fruit, because the water from the sanctuary flows to them. Their fruit will serve as food and their leaves as medicine. ¹³ This is what the Lord GOD says: These are the boundaries by which you shall divide the land among the twelve tribes of Israel, with Joseph receiving two shares. ¹⁴ You shall divide it equally. I swore with an uplifted hand to give it to your ancestors, and this land will become your inheritance. ¹⁵ This is the northern boundary: from the Mediterranean Sea, the road to Hethlon, to Lebo-hamath, Zedad,

¹⁶ Berothah, Sibraim — which lies on the border between Damascus and Hamath — as far as Hazer-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran. ¹⁷ The boundary will run from the sea to Hazar-enon, along the northern border of Damascus, then to Hamath on the north. This is the northern boundary. ¹⁸ The eastern boundary: from Hauran and Damascus, along the Jordan between Gilead and the land of Israel, to the Dead Sea and as far as Tamar. This is the eastern boundary. ¹⁹ The southern boundary: from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-kadesh, then along the brook of Egypt to the Mediterranean Sea. This is the southern boundary. ²⁰ The western boundary: the Mediterranean Sea, northward to a point opposite Lebo-hamath. This is the western boundary.

²¹ You shall divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel. ²² You shall allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the foreigners residing among you who have had children. You are to treat them as native-born Israelites; along with you they shall be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel. ²³ In whatever tribe a foreigner resides, there you shall give him his inheritance, declares the Lord GOD.

chapters.title: Ezekiel 48
paragraphs: ¹ These are the names of the tribes: From the northern end, along the road of Hethlon to Lebo-hamath, all the way to Hazar-enon, on the northern border of Damascus, northward beside Hamath — Dan shall have one portion. Its borders shall run from east to west. ² Adjoining Dan's territory from east to west — Asher shall have one portion. ³ Adjoining Asher's territory from east to west — Naphtali shall have one portion. ⁴ Adjoining Naphtali's territory from east to west — Manasseh shall have one portion. ⁵ Adjoining Manasseh's territory from east to west — Ephraim shall have one portion.

⁶ Adjoining Ephraim's territory from east to west — Reuben shall have one portion. ⁷ Adjoining Reuben's territory from east to west — Judah shall have one portion. ⁸ Adjoining Judah's territory from east to west shall be the sacred portion you are to set apart — twenty-five thousand cubits wide, extending in length from east to west the same as one of the tribal portions. The sanctuary shall be in the center of it. ⁹ The sacred portion you set apart for the LORD shall be twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand cubits wide. ¹⁰ This holy portion shall be divided as follows: the priests shall have a section twenty-five thousand cubits long on the north side, ten thousand cubits wide on the west, ten thousand cubits wide on the east, and twenty-five thousand cubits long on the south, with the LORD's sanctuary in the center.

¹¹ This sacred area shall belong to the consecrated priests — the descendants of Zadok — who were faithful to me and did not go astray as the Levites did when the Israelites went astray. ¹² It shall be a most holy portion for them, set apart from the Levites' territory. ¹³ Alongside the priests' territory, the Levites shall have a portion twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand cubits wide. The total length shall be twenty-five thousand cubits and the width ten thousand. ¹⁴ They must not sell or exchange any of it, nor transfer any of this choice land, because it is holy to the LORD. ¹⁵ The remaining strip of land — five thousand cubits wide and twenty-five thousand cubits long — shall be for common use: for the city, its houses, and its open land. The city shall be in the center.

¹⁶ These shall be the city's measurements: on the north side, four thousand five hundred cubits; on the south side, four thousand five hundred cubits; on the east side, four thousand five hundred cubits; and on the west side, four thousand five hundred cubits. ¹⁷ The city shall have open land: two hundred fifty cubits on the north, two hundred fifty cubits on the south, two hundred fifty cubits on the east, and two hundred fifty cubits on the west. ¹⁸ The remaining land alongside the sacred portion shall be ten thousand cubits on the east side and ten thousand cubits on the west side. Its produce will provide food for the workers of the city. ¹⁹ The workers of the city from all the tribes of Israel shall farm it. ²⁰ The entire sacred portion shall be twenty-five thousand cubits square. Together with the city property, you shall set it apart as the sacred portion.

²¹ What remains on both sides of the sacred portion and the city property shall belong to the prince. This area lies alongside the twenty-five-thousand-cubit portion, extending east to the eastern border and west to the western border, running parallel to the tribal portions. It shall belong to the prince, with the sacred portion and the temple sanctuary in the center of it. ²² The land belonging to the Levites and the land belonging to the city shall lie within the area assigned to the prince, between the borders of Judah and Benjamin. ²³ As for the rest of the tribes: from east to west, Benjamin shall have one portion. ²⁴ Adjoining Benjamin's territory from east to west — Simeon shall have one portion. ²⁵ Adjoining Simeon's territory from east to west — Issachar shall have one portion.

²⁶ Adjoining Issachar's territory from east to west — Zebulun shall have one portion. ²⁷ Adjoining Zebulun's territory from east to west — Gad shall have one portion. ²⁸ Gad's southern border shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-kadesh, then along the brook of Egypt to the Mediterranean Sea. ²⁹ This is the land you shall distribute by lot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these are their allotments, declares the Lord GOD. ³⁰ These are the exits of the city: on the north side, which measures four thousand five hundred cubits,

³¹ the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel. On the north side there will be three gates: one gate for Reuben, one gate for Judah, and one gate for Levi. ³² On the east side, which is four thousand five hundred cubits long, there will be three gates: one gate for Joseph, one gate for Benjamin, and one gate for Dan. ³³ On the south side, which measures four thousand five hundred cubits, there will be three gates: one gate for Simeon, one gate for Issachar, and one gate for Zebulun. ³⁴ On the west side, which is four thousand five hundred cubits long, there will be three gates: one gate for Gad, one gate for Asher, and one gate for Naphtali. ³⁵ The total circumference of the city will be eighteen thousand cubits. And the name of the city from that day on will be: The LORD Is There.

chapters.title: Daniel 1
paragraphs: ¹ In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it. ² The Lord handed Jehoiakim king of Judah over to him, along with some of the vessels from the house of God. Nebuchadnezzar carried them to the land of Shinar, to the temple of his god, and placed them in the treasure house of his god. ³ The king ordered Ashpenaz, chief of his court officials, to bring in some of the Israelites — young men from the royal family and the nobility; ⁴ young men without any defect, handsome, gifted in every kind of wisdom, with knowledge and good judgment, suitable for service in the king's palace. He was to teach them the language and literature of the Babylonians. ⁵ The king assigned them a daily portion of food and wine from his own table and ordered them to be trained for three years, after which they were to enter royal service.

⁶ Among these young men were some from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. ⁷ The chief official gave them new names: Daniel he called Belteshazzar; Hananiah he called Shadrach; Mishael he called Meshach; and Azariah he called Abednego. ⁸ But Daniel made up his mind not to defile himself with the royal food and wine, and he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself this way. ⁹ Now God had caused the chief official to show favor and sympathy to Daniel. ¹⁰ But the chief official told Daniel, "I'm afraid of my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. Why should he see you looking worse than the other young men your age? The king would then have my head because of you."

¹¹ Then Daniel said to Melzar, whom the chief official had assigned to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, ¹² "Please test your servants for ten days: give us nothing but vegetables to eat and water to drink. ¹³ Then compare our appearance with that of the young men who eat the royal food, and treat your servants in accordance with what you see." ¹⁴ He agreed to this and tested them for ten days. ¹⁵ At the end of the ten days they looked healthier and better nourished than any of the young men who had been eating the royal food.

¹⁶ So Melzar took away their portion of food and the wine they were to drink, and gave them vegetables instead. ¹⁷ To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding of all kinds of literature and learning. And Daniel could understand visions and dreams of all kinds. ¹⁸ At the end of the time set by the king to bring them into his service, the chief official presented them to Nebuchadnezzar. ¹⁹ The king talked with them, and he found no one equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; so they entered the king's service. ²⁰ In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his whole kingdom.
²¹ And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.

chapters.title: Daniel 2
paragraphs: ¹ In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams that troubled him so deeply he could not sleep. ² He commanded that the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans be summoned to tell him what he had dreamed. When they came and stood before the king, ³ he said to them, "I have had a dream that troubles me and I want to know what it means." ⁴ Then the Chaldeans answered the king in Aramaic, "O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will interpret it." ⁵ The king replied to the Chaldeans, "This is what I have firmly decided: if you do not tell me what my dream was and interpret it, I will have you cut into pieces and your houses turned into rubble.

⁶ But if you tell me the dream and explain it, you will receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and interpret it for me." ⁷ Once more they replied, "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will interpret it." ⁸ Then the king answered, "I am certain that you are trying to gain time, because you realize that this is what I have firmly decided: ⁹ if you do not tell me the dream, there is only one penalty for you. You have conspired to tell me misleading and wicked things, hoping the situation will change. So then, tell me the dream, and I will know that you can interpret it for me." ¹⁰ The Chaldeans answered the king, "There is not a man on earth who can do what the king asks. No king, however great and mighty, has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean."

¹¹ "What the king asks is too difficult. No one can reveal it to the king except the gods, and they do not live among humans." ¹² This made the king so angry and furious that he ordered the execution of all the wise men of Babylon. ¹³ So the decree was issued to put the wise men to death, and men were sent to look for Daniel and his friends to put them to death. ¹⁴ When Arioch, the commander of the king's guard, had gone out to put to death the wise men of Babylon, Daniel spoke to him with wisdom and tact. ¹⁵ He asked the king's officer, "Why did the king issue such a harsh decree?" Arioch then explained the matter to Daniel.

¹⁶ At this, Daniel went in to the king and asked for time, so that he might interpret the dream for him. ¹⁷ Then Daniel returned to his house and explained the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. ¹⁸ He urged them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that he and his friends might not be executed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon. ¹⁹ During the night the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision. Then Daniel praised the God of heaven ²⁰ and said: "Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and power are his.

²¹ He changes times and seasons; he deposes kings and raises up others. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to the discerning. ²² He reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what lies in darkness, and light dwells with him. ²³ I thank and praise you, God of my ancestors: you have given me wisdom and power, you have made known to me what we asked of you — you have made known to us the dream of the king." ²⁴ Then Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to execute the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, "Do not execute the wise men of Babylon. Take me to the king, and I will interpret his dream for him." ²⁵ Arioch took Daniel to the king at once and said, "I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who can tell the king what his dream means."

²⁶ The king asked Daniel (also called Belteshazzar), "Are you able to tell me what I saw in my dream and interpret it?" ²⁷ Daniel replied, "No wise man, enchanter, magician, or diviner can explain to the king the mystery he has asked about. ²⁸ But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries. He has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in days to come. Your dream and the visions that passed through your mind as you were lying in bed are these: ²⁹ As your Majesty was lying there, your mind turned to things to come, and the revealer of mysteries showed you what is going to happen. ³⁰ As for me, this mystery has been revealed to me, not because I have greater wisdom than anyone else alive, but so that your Majesty may know the interpretation and that you may understand what went through your mind.

³¹ "Your Majesty looked, and there before you stood a large statue — an enormous, dazzling statue, awesome in appearance. ³² The head of the statue was made of pure gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze, ³³ its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of baked clay. ³⁴ While you were watching, a rock was cut out, but not by human hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and smashed them. ³⁵ Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were all broken to pieces and became like chaff on a threshing floor in the summer. The wind swept them away without leaving a trace. But the rock that struck the statue became a huge mountain and filled the whole earth.

³⁶ "This was the dream, and now we will interpret it to the king. ³⁷ Your Majesty, you are the king of kings. The God of heaven has given you dominion and power and might and glory; ³⁸ in your hands he has placed all mankind and the beasts of the field and the birds in the sky. Wherever they live, he has made you ruler over them all. You are that head of gold. ³⁹ After you, another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours. Next, a third kingdom, one of bronze, will rule over the whole earth. ⁴⁰ Finally, there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron — for iron breaks and smashes everything — and as iron breaks things to pieces, so it will crush and break all the others.

⁴¹ Just as you saw that the feet and toes were partly of baked clay and partly of iron, so this will be a divided kingdom; yet it will have some of the strength of iron in it, even as you saw iron mixed with clay. ⁴² As the toes were partly iron and partly clay, so this kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle. ⁴³ And just as you saw the iron mixed with baked clay, so the people will be a mixture and will not remain united, any more than iron mixes with clay. ⁴⁴ In the time of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will crush all those kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will itself endure forever. ⁴⁵ This is the meaning of the vision of the rock cut out of a mountain, but not by human hands — a rock that broke the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold to pieces. The great God has shown the king what will take place in the future. The dream is true and its interpretation is trustworthy."

⁴⁶ Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell prostrate before Daniel and paid him honor, ordering that an offering and incense be presented to him. ⁴⁷ The king said to Daniel, "Surely your God is the God of gods and the Lord of kings and a revealer of mysteries, for you were able to reveal this mystery." ⁴⁸ Then the king placed Daniel in a high position and lavished many gifts on him. He made him ruler over the entire province of Babylon and placed him in charge of all its wise men. ⁴⁹ Moreover, at Daniel's request the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego administrators over the province of Babylon, while Daniel himself remained at the royal court.

chapters.title: Daniel 3
paragraphs: ¹ King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon. ² He then summoned the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the other provincial officials to come to the dedication of the image he had set up. ³ So the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the other provincial officials assembled for the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before it. ⁴ Then the herald loudly proclaimed, "This is what you are commanded to do, O peoples, nations, and men of every language: ⁵ As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, you must fall down and worship the image of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.

⁶ Whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace." ⁷ Therefore, as soon as they heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and all kinds of music, all the nations and peoples fell down and worshipped the image of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up. ⁸ At this time some astrologers came forward and denounced the Jews. ⁹ They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "O king, live forever! ¹⁰ Your Majesty has issued a decree that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music must fall down and worship the image of gold,
